- cleanup on a dirty worktree (modified tracked files) exits with an explanatory error without --force; dep dirs alone do not count as dirty.
- Regression tests cover both; full gate suite passes.

title: Match the write tool check case insensitively so a lowercase alias cannot pass it
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 by the tool-name investigation (see basicly-8sxf's comments for the full measured
report). This is a hardening gap in our own validator, not in a third party.

`src/basicly/agents.py` defines `WRITE_TOOLS = frozenset({"Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit",
"NotebookEdit"})` and matches it by an exact, case-SENSITIVE set intersection to decide whether an
agent declaring a read-only posture is actually read-only.

Measured against GitHub's published alias table
(`docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-agents-configuration`): copilot's tool aliases are
explicitly **case insensitive**, and its `edit` primary accepts `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `Write` and
`NotebookEdit`. So a catalog source declaring `edit`, `write`, `create` or `notebookedit` in lowercase
would:

- pass our read-only posture check, because none of those strings is in `WRITE_TOOLS`; and
- be granted real file-writing tools on copilot, because the alias resolves case-insensitively.

Our own authoring convention is PascalCase, and `catalog lint` plus review make a lowercase
declaration unlikely today, so this is latent rather than live. It is still the exact class of defect
the posture check exists to prevent, and the fix is small.

Two adjacent facts from the same investigation worth handling here or recording as out of scope:

- `MultiEdit` is **no longer** on Claude Code's published tool list, though copilot still accepts it as
  an alias. Keeping it in `WRITE_TOOLS` is harmless and still correct for copilot.
- `NotebookEdit` alone resolves on the copilot CLI to **both** `create` and `edit` - general filesystem
  write. So the narrowest notebook-only write tool on claude becomes full write on copilot. We do not
  ship it, and this check would reject it in a read-only agent, but the asymmetry is worth a comment so
  a future author does not assume tool breadth is preserved across families.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Author an agent source declaring a read-only posture and `tools: [Read, edit]` (lowercase `edit`).
- Run `basicly catalog lint`.
- Observed: the read-only posture check passes, because `"edit"` is not in `WRITE_TOOLS`.
  Expected: it fails, because the declared tool grants writes on at least one supported family.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an agent source that declares a read-only posture and a write-granting tool named in any
  casing when the agent lint runs then it fails naming the tool and the posture, and given the same
  source with only read tools in any casing then it passes, with tests
acceptance_criteria: Given an agent source that declares a read only posture and a write granting tool named in any casing when the agent lint runs then it fails naming the tool and the posture, and given the same source with only read tools in any casing then it passes, with tests

title: install initializes the beads workspace with a derived prefix
description:
basicly install converges catalog, overlay, config, projections, and hooks — but not the tracker: a fresh consumer must hand-run br init, and the harness loop/commit hooks depend on the workspace existing. Install should initialize beads when absent, with a prefix derived from the repo directory name (sanitized to the single-hyphen id shape the commit-msg hook accepts), idempotent and graceful when br is not on PATH.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fresh repo: basicly install initializes .beads with a derived prefix (e.g. repo "terminal" -> terminal-<hash> ids); re-running install leaves an existing workspace untouched.
- br missing from PATH: install prints actionable guidance and continues (no failure).

title: Design the specialized agent roster for the factory
description:
## Context

Requested 2026-07-24 as the feature after the factory (basicly-kjc5) completes: give the factory named specialist personas with their own expertise, quirks and identity instead of one generic dispatched agent, so the engine routes each judgment step to the role best suited to it. Design only - no implementation until the factory is complete.

The design must reconcile the roster with the factory decisions it touches: D1/D2 (the supervisor is a deterministic event loop, not an LLM that spawns agents), D4 (verify is deterministic, validate is the rubric gate), D5 (no merge-time AI resolution), D7 (read-only helpers allowed inside a lane under one global process budget), and 7.1 (the decider contract, already a persona).

## Acceptance Criteria

- docs/agent-roster-design.md exists as an agreed design that names each persona with its role contract, the loop phase it serves, its tool policy, model tier and gate authority, reconciles the roster against factory decisions D1-D8, states which proposed roles are rejected and why, and defines the config and catalog surface the roster ships through under the dual-use constraint

## Scope

- `docs/agent-roster-design.md`

title: Ship advance must surface a skipped tracker-state commit
description:
During basicly-kjc5.4 ship an unrelated dirty file (.gitignore) in the base checkout made merge.commit_tracker_state return False, so loop _on_ship closed the issue but silently skipped the closing chore(beads) commit - the advance printed 'worktree torn down and issue closed' with no hint, and the operator pushed before noticing the tracker state was uncommitted. Fix: when commit_tracker_state returns False in _on_ship (and the claim commit in _start_build_leaf), append an explicit warning to the AdvanceResult detail naming the foreign paths and the recovery (stash the foreign dirt and re-run, or commit it), instead of omitting the 'tracker state committed' suffix silently.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Leave an unrelated dirty file in the base checkout (for example an edit to `.gitignore`) so it is neither staged nor part of `.beads/**`.
2. Drive any tracked issue to its ship phase and run `basicly loop advance <issue>`.
3. The advance prints "worktree torn down and issue closed" and exits 0, but no `chore(beads)` commit was made - `git status` still shows the tracker export dirty, and a push at this point ships the code without the tracker state.

Expected: the advance detail explicitly warns that the tracker-state commit was skipped, names the foreign paths that blocked it, and states the recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Given a base checkout with non-beads dirt when a loop advance closes or claims an issue then the advance detail explicitly warns that the tracker-state commit was skipped and names the blocking paths, with a regression test

title: Tracker-only commits trigger pointless builds - investigate and fix commit discipline
description:
Every push to main triggers CI (and in consumer repos like dreidesk, a long verify build), but the harness loop currently produces multiple .beads/issues.jsonl-only commits per track (claim, loop-state, close after teardown). Investigate WHY tracker commits were separated from work commits (suspected: worktree provisioning syncs base jsonl and committing on both sides makes the landing rebase conflict - see beads-tracker-vs-loop-worktrees memory and basicly-djt). Then judge and decide the optimal fix, e.g.: fold the close into the last work commit (close bead before the resolving commit), batch pushes until the closing commit lands, and/or paths-ignore .beads/** in CI workflows (authoring + the consumer CI template). br is the essential tracker the harness builds on, so the chosen discipline must be conflict-free with worktrees and documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Root cause for the separated tracker commits is documented on this issue with evidence from code/history. A decision comment records the chosen design and rejected alternatives. Implementation lands: workflow/CI changes (including the consumer CI template if applicable) and/or loop commit-discipline changes so tracker-only pushes stop triggering full builds and tracker state stays conflict-free with worktree landings. Agent instructions/skills (tool-br, harness-loop, fragments) updated to the new discipline. Full gate suite passes.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: INVESTIGATION (root cause, with evidence): tracker commits are separated from work commits structurally, not accidentally. (1) worktree provisioning copies the BASE WORKING-TREE issues.jsonl into the new worktree (worktree.py create, basicly-djt fix 32dc562) purely so the beads-commit-msg hook recognizes freshly filed ids; (2) merge.py _assert_base_ready requires a CLEAN base checkout at landing, so any base-side tracker mutation (claim, work type, checkpoint approvals - all recorded via br from base) must be committed before the landing advance; (3) the br daemon rewrites the full jsonl export in every checkout, so a harness branch that also commits issues.jsonl guarantees a rebase conflict at merge_worktree step 1 - br sync --merge (reconcile_beads) only runs AFTER a successful merge and cannot rescue the rebase; (4) the close cannot ride the last work commit because loop._on_ship closes the issue AFTER the merge commit exists (phase order: land at build->verify, then verify gate on base, then ship checkpoint, then close). Folding the close into a work commit is therefore impossible in the current two-checkout model; the tool-br rule (close folded into the resolving commit) applies only to non-loop base-checkout work.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: DECISION: the pointless builds are a CI-trigger problem, not a commit-count problem - GitHub runs the workflows per push to main regardless of content, and the expensive job is the 3-OS quality-gates matrix (and in consumer repos like dreidesk, the scaffolded basicly-gates workflow / their own verify build). Chosen fix: (a) add paths-ignore .beads/** to the push and pull_request triggers of basicly.yml and quality-gates.yml, and to the CONSUMER_CI_WORKFLOW template so new consumer installs get it; (b) keep tracker commits separate (structural, see investigation) but cut them to exactly two per track via skill discipline: ONE pre-provisioning chore(beads) commit folding claim+work-type+classify approval, and ONE closing commit after ship; (c) push discipline: push once per track after the closing commit, never push tracker-only commits alone. Trade-off accepted: a tracker-only push skips CI commit-message validation for those commits; the local commit-msg hooks are the deterministic floor and already validated them. REJECTED (for now): engine redesign folding the close into the merge commit (git merge --no-commit + stage jsonl) - it requires reordering the loop so landing happens AFTER verify+ship approval (today code lands on main BEFORE the ship checkpoint), would also remove the duplicate base re-verify, but changes governance and feature fan-in semantics; filed separately as a design bead. NOTE for existing consumers: install never overwrites the scaffolded CI workflow, so dreidesk must add paths-ignore .beads/** to its own workflow manually.

title: The python skill description runs two triggers together after the dogfood edit
description:
## Context

Introduced by lane `basicly-hxnf.1` during the basicly-kjc5.22 dogfood run (2026-07-26) and found
in the post-run review of what the headless lanes wrote.

The lane rewrote the `python` skill's `description` to add its new trigger and dropped a
coordinating "or" while restructuring the list. Before:

    ...creating or changing .py files wiring up a subprocess call or chasing a test that
    passes on POSIX but fails only on Windows CI...

After:

    ...creating or changing .py files wiring up a subprocess call chasing a test that
    passes on POSIX but fails only on Windows CI ... or second-guessing syntax...

So it now reads "a subprocess call chasing a test", merging two distinct triggers into one
ungrammatical phrase. The body prose the lane added is accurate and well-sourced; this is only the
description field.

It matters more than a typo because a skill `description` is the always-loaded trigger text every
agent sees in its skill list, so a garbled trigger degrades retrieval for every session in every
consuming repo — and the always-on baseline is near its character cap
(see the always-on budget notes), which is why descriptions get restructured rather than extended.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n "subprocess call chasing" .basicly/core/skills/python/skill.yaml`
2. Observed: the two triggers are run together with no conjunction.
3. Expected: "wiring up a subprocess call, chasing a test ... or second-guessing syntax ..." — three parallel triggers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the python skill description when it is read then its triggers are grammatically parallel and separated and the projections are regenerated with every gate passing

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/python/**`
- `.claude/skills/python/**`
- `.agents/skills/python/**`
acceptance_criteria: Given the python skill description when it is read then its triggers are grammatically parallel and separated and the projections are regenerated with every gate passing

title: Decide whether losing the github com copilot surface is acceptable per fragment
description:
## Context

So scoping is a deliberate removal from the github.com Copilot surface: on that surface the guidance simply stops being delivered.

That makes it a guarantee change per fragment rather than a refactor, and the call has to be made per fragment - subprocess discipline, test isolation and catalog authoring are the named candidates.

Blocks the scope declarations. Filed as a bead so the scheduler enforces it; an unfiled decision cannot be a dependency edge.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
[harness-info] Owner decision, 2026-07-26. Plan section 7.2 resolved.

DECIDED: scope test-isolation and subprocess-discipline. Keep catalog-authoring always-on.

Reasoning recorded because the call is per fragment and a future session must not re-litigate it. The github.com Copilot surface reviews pull requests; it does not run tests and does not spawn subprocesses, so test-isolation and subprocess-discipline do little work there and losing them costs little. Catalog-authoring is different: a pull request that edits catalog YAML is exactly what gets reviewed on that surface, so that guidance must keep being delivered there and stays always-on.

New input that sharpened the trade, measured under basicly-agzx.1: scoping does not merely fail to help Codex, it costs it. AGENTS.md grew 7014 to 8484 chars from one scoped fragment because codex inlines scoped fragments, so each fragment scoped is a real Codex increase against a Claude and Copilot decrease. Codex caps at 12000 rather than 9000, so there is headroom, but any claim that scoping cut the baseline must name the family.

Also relevant: basicly-agzx.1 refuted the strong cliff hypothesis, so this is a cost optimisation rather than a rescue. That lowers the urgency but does not change the answer.

Unblocks basicly-a3ab.2.

title: A missed coupling edge gates the bounced lane it is meant to teach
description:
## Context

Found by review while narrowing basicly-kjc5.26 (see the `[design-narrowing]` comment there).

`merge.record_coupling` writes a **gating** `blocks` edge and justifies itself with "A `blocks`
edge onto an already-landed lane gates nothing now (that lane is done)". In the supervisor that
premise is false: `_land_green` routes a landed lane `merged`, and it then parks in verify
awaiting a human ship approval - the bead is still open. `br blocked` therefore reports the
bounced lane as blocked, and `ready_lanes` drops it.

So the D5 bounce, whose whole purpose is to send a collided lane back to its own agent to
re-apply its intent, instead holds that lane behind a human ship approval on the lane it
collided with. At autonomy ceiling L0 (every ship checkpoint is a human stop) that is
indefinite. The lane also already spent a rework attempt on the way.

`kjc5.26` sidestepped this for the pre-emptive cancel path by publishing a `kind=coupling`
found-info record instead of an edge. The bounce path still writes the edge, and it is the
path that carries the design's "the graph learns" requirement - so the fix here has to keep
the graph learning without gating the lane that is supposed to re-run.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Two session lanes whose branches touch the same file with incompatible content.
2. Run one supervisor pass over both green outcomes: `supervise.route_outcomes(repo, session, (green_a, green_b))`.
3. Observed: lane A routes `merged` (open, parked in verify awaiting ship), lane B routes
   `bounced` and gains a `blocks` edge onto A, so `br blocked` lists B and `ready_lanes` omits it.
4. Expected: B is bounced *and still dispatchable* next pass, while the missed coupling is
   recorded for future decompositions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a bounced lane whose collision is attributed to a lane that landed but has not shipped when the next pass derives its ready set then the bounced lane is dispatchable and the missed coupling is still recorded for future decomposition with tests

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a bounced lane whose collision is attributed to a lane that landed but has not shipped when the next pass derives its ready set then the bounced lane is dispatchable and the missed coupling is still recorded for future decomposition with tests

title: Observability: fleet rollup across housed repos
description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 3. `basicly status --json` is single-repo and self-labelled (STATUS_SCHEMA_VERSION) "for fleet loops", and every dispatch drops a run-record into `.basicly/usage/`, but basicly does no aggregation across the housed repos of the dev workspace.

Add a read-only fleet rollup: `basicly status --fleet [--root PATH]` discovers the basicly-installed repos under the workspace root and rolls up, per repo, the `status --json` snapshot plus a run-record summary into one JSON payload. JSON-first, read-only, exit 0.

Rollup model (decided): in-process — call the current engine's `_status_report(repo_root)` on each discovered repo plus `run_record.load_run_records`; a per-repo failure is captured as an `error` field, never failing the whole rollup. Default root is the parent of the current repo; `--root` overrides. Reuses the existing single-repo status + run-record loaders (no new snapshot logic).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `basicly status --fleet` discovers the basicly repos (immediate subdirs of the workspace root containing a `.basicly/` dir), and emits a JSON payload `{schema_version, workspace_root, repos: [...], totals: {...}}`, sorted deterministically by repo name, exit 0.
- Each repo entry carries its name, the `status --json` payload (or an `error` string if the snapshot raises), and a run-record summary (total runs, counts by outcome, distinct agents/models, beads with runs).
- The command writes nothing anywhere (read-only) and returns 0 even when a repo is unreadable, has no `.basicly/`, or has no run-records.
- `--root PATH` overrides the discovered workspace root; the default is the parent of the current repo.
- Totals aggregate the per-repo run-record counts across the fleet.
- Full suite, ruff, ruff format, pyright, bandit, and the projection gates (basicly check / skills-check / agents-check / hooks-check) pass; verified by exercising the real command against this workspace (not just unit tests).

## Notes

- Cross-repo scope is READ-ONLY aggregation only (dimension 3's explicit ask); it respects the workspace boundary (no writes, no cross-repo mutation, no --add-dir).
- Human-formatted fleet table and a subprocess-per-repo execution model are out of scope (JSON-first, in-process).

title: Commit the claim at provisioning and document team push cadence
description:

Cross-machine races that still slip through remain covered by br stale-claim detection (scheduler --stale-claim-hours, coordination).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Provisioning a leaf (and feature fan-out) commits pending tracker-only dirt first, with a conventional chore message referencing the issue; non-beads dirt does not block provisioning and is left alone (tests cover both). The harness-loop skill documents the three engine commit points (claim at provisioning, rollup at landing, close at ship) and the solo vs team push cadence. Full gate suite passes.

title: Distribute three verification rules the retro found missing
description:
## Context

Three findings from the 2026-07-31 session retro, each traceable to a wrong statement that reached the
owner, and each preventable by one rule in an existing on-demand skill. Grouped because they are the
same class - how a claim becomes evidence - and because all three are skill edits, which cost **zero
always-on budget** (skills load on invocation). That matters: `copilot-instructions.md` has 974
characters of headroom, the tightest always-on surface, so none of this may become an
`applies_to: [all]` fragment.

### 1. A bead's third-party claim is not evidence -> `harness-loop` (build phase)

`basicly-kjc5.61`'s description asserted that models.dev "decisively" carries a `base_model` field
linking a provider serving id to the underlying model. Measured against the live endpoint before
implementing: present on **0 of 5911** records, and absent from the record schema entirely. Filed two
days earlier, so it was plausibly true once or never checked. A bead reads as authoritative because it
passed DoR, and dispatching on that text would have had an implementer build against a phantom field
and either fail or silently invent a fallback. The join that actually works is exact `name` equality
corroborated by `family`.
Rule to add: before implementing, re-verify any third-party API, CLI or schema claim the bead asserts,
and record the verification on the bead. Cheap, and it is what saved this lane.

### 2. A zero-finding scan needs a positive control -> `test-discipline`

While checking whether copilot CLI supports hooks, `strings` on the CLI binary found no hook
identifiers, and that was reported as evidence the capability was absent. A control then showed that
strings the CLI had been **directly observed emitting** (`allow-all-tools`, `premiumRequests`,
`modelMetrics`) also returned zero matches, because the JS payload is a compressed bundle. The method
was blind and the finding was retracted.
Rule to add: a search or scan that finds nothing is evidence only if the same method finds a
known-present control; without one, report the method inconclusive rather than the thing absent. The
repo already learned this shape once (a zero-finding tracker audit that had to be proved against a
known-bad item) but nothing distributes it.

### 3. Tracker semantics must be read through the engine -> `tool-br`

The owner was told `basicly-jr0l` carried an L1 grant with a 5M budget, read by regex over
`.beads/issues.jsonl`. The authoritative parse, `policy.active_grant`, reports **L3 with a 4M budget**,
because the last grant marker wins and the regex surfaced an earlier one. Same class as the existing
documented trap that `br` keeps one gate result per (gate, provider) so a gate must never be decided by
collapsing rows.
Rule to add: read tracker *semantics* - grants, gate results, derived phase - through the engine's own
API, never by grepping the export. The export is a record, not the interpreter. Reading the export
directly stays correct for whole-tracker counting, which is why the existing guidance recommends it.

## Scope

`.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`, `.basicly/core/skills/test-discipline/skill.yaml`,
`.basicly/core/skills/tool-br/skill.yaml`, then `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the three skill sources when the catalog is built and the projection gates run then each skill
  carries its rule with the incident that motivated it, the always-on baselines are unchanged because
  no fragment was touched, and skills-check passes across all default roots
acceptance_criteria: Given the three skill sources when the catalog is built and the projection gates run then each skill carries its rule with the incident that motivated it and the always on baselines are unchanged because no fragment was touched and skills-check passes across all default roots

title: Document three verified tool behaviours in the skills that own them
description:
## Context

Three tool behaviours cost an agent a wrong diagnosis or a stalled landing during the
2026-07-26 session, and none of them is written down in the skill that owns the tool. Each was
verified directly, not inferred, so the prose can state a fact rather than a caution.

1. **`python`** — this repo's floor is 3.14, where PEP 758 allows `except A, B, C:` with no
   parentheses. `src/basicly/decompose.py` uses that form. An agent reading it flagged it as a
   Python 2 syntax error and stopped to re-verify that the module imports at all.
2. **`tool-br`** — `br dep add` is idempotent (a repeat prints "Dependency already exists" and
   leaves exactly one row), and an existing edge's **type cannot be changed**: a later
   `dep add ... -t blocks` over a `related` edge is refused as a duplicate rather than upgraded.
   The second half is load-bearing for `supervise.propose_coupling_edges`, which now depends on
   whichever path records an edge first.
3. **`harness-loop`** — more than one agent session can share the one base checkout, and a
   landing mutates that shared tree. `merge._assert_base_ready` counts untracked files, so a
   second session's stray file blocks every landing, and clearing it is not the lander's call.

This is the acceptance-run subject for basicly-kjc5.22: three genuinely disjoint file scopes
(each skill projects only to its own `<skill>/` directories, verified by a projection probe), so
the governor can size them and the supervisor can run them as concurrent lanes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the three verified tool behaviours when the owning skills are read then each states the behaviour with its consequence and every projection gate passes

## Success Criteria

- Each of the three skills documents its behaviour and `basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` plus `basicly check` pass
acceptance_criteria: Given the three verified tool behaviours when the owning skills are read then each states the behaviour with its consequence and every projection gate passes

title: Record the 3.14 unparenthesized except form in the python skill

title: Stop a closed beads rework escalation from poisoning lights out forever
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 while landing basicly-kjc5.59 and basicly-kjc5.60. Every ship under the
basicly-kjc5 root demands a human confirm code despite an active L3 grant, and the reason the
engine prints is `rework escalation on basicly-kjc5.56 (gate verify: 2/2)`.

basicly-kjc5.56 is **closed**. It shipped 2026-07-27 with a human-answered ship checkpoint. Its
two verify-rework markers are resolved history from that landing.

`policy.lights_out_violations` walks `_session_issue_ids` (the root plus its whole transitive
parent-child tree) and, for each bead, counts `[harness-policy] rework gate=<g>` comment markers.
Once a bead reaches `max_rework` that count never decreases, because rework is recorded as
append-only comments and nothing marks an escalation resolved. So a **closed** bead's historical
escalation is read as a live session-wide violation forever.

Consequence: the L3 lights-out feature degrades permanently on any long-lived epic. The first
escalation anywhere in the tree drops every later child ship to a human for the rest of the
epic's life - basicly-kjc5 has 55+ children - and it degrades silently, since the operator only
sees that a human must approve. That is the opposite of what the D3 lights-out preconditions are
for, and basicly-u6jq.1 needs unattended operation to prove.

This is the same defect shape basicly-hsrs already fixed for grants: a grant on a **closed** root
issue is dead regardless of its markers. A marker on closed work is history, not live state.

**Not to be confused with the correct behaviour** it sits next to: an escalation on an **open**
bead is real unresolved work and must keep blocking a delegated ship. Only closed work is at
issue, so the fix must not widen what may be self-approved.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take an epic with a child that once hit the rework cap on a required gate and has since been
   closed and shipped (basicly-kjc5 and basicly-kjc5.56 are a live example in this repo).
2. Hold an active L3 grant on the epic root with autonomy L3.
3. Drive any other child of that epic to its ship checkpoint with `basicly loop run <child> --root <epic>`.
4. Observed: ship refuses to self-approve, citing `rework escalation on <closed child> (gate verify: 2/2)`.
   Expected: a closed bead's resolved escalation does not count as a live violation, so ship
   delegates; an escalation on an open bead still refuses.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a session tree containing a closed bead whose rework markers reached the cap when the
  lights-out preconditions are computed then that bead contributes no violation and a covering L3
  grant may delegate ship, and given the same markers on an open bead then the violation still
  stands and ship returns to a human, with tests
acceptance_criteria: Given a session tree containing a closed bead whose rework markers reached the cap when the lights out preconditions are computed then that bead contributes no violation and a covering L3 grant may delegate ship and given the same markers on an open bead then the violation still stands and ship returns to a human with tests

title: Correct the gastown merge-queue claim and absorb the seven-repo analysis
description:
## Context

`basicly-imnu.9` added section 2.11 to `docs/research/2026-07-26-sota-review.md` on 2026-07-30 and
put a factually wrong claim in it. The claim was written from gastown's README, fetched rather than
read from source:

> **Take - their merge queue is ahead of ours in one specific, adoptable way.** [...] Gastown
> *bisects* on verification failure [...] Bisecting is a pure throughput win with no new dependency
> and no LLM in the loop [...] worth filing against `merge.py`.

**The batch-then-bisect merge queue is dead code.** Verified in the clone at `649b832`:
`AssembleBatch` and `ProcessBatch` appear only at their own definitions
(`internal/refinery/batch.go:58`, `:211`) with no call sites outside tests; the config field that
would enable them is never read (`engineer.go:177-179`); `ProcessMRInfo` (`engineer.go:1321`) has no
callers at all including tests; and the Go merge engine is unreachable because the Refinery is a
Claude agent in a tmux session, with the Go-driven foreground mode returning a hard error -
*"foreground mode is deprecated; use background mode"* (`internal/refinery/manager.go:154-156`). The
agent runbook says it processes the queue **sequentially**
(`.claude/commands/patrol.md:126`). `README.md:96` and `:653-661` describe an algorithm the shipped
binary cannot run.

So the corrected conclusion inverts the original one: **basicly's strictly serial queue is ahead of
what gastown actually runs, and deterministic where gastown's is an LLM.** The full analysis also
computed bisection's break-even at a per-lane pass rate of about 0.86 for a batch of five, for
roughly 2,100 lines and a blame defect that would corrupt the coupling graph - so it should not be
filed as work, which is the opposite of what section 2.11 currently recommends.

The durable lesson is the one this repo already has a rule for and I broke anyway: a README claim is
not evidence. The first pass read gastown through a fetched README summary; every corrected fact
here came from reading source. Record that in the section rather than quietly fixing the text.

## Scope

Also absorb the other six repos from the 2026-07-30 analysis, which currently live only in
`reference-repos/_analysis/` outside the repo: `oh-my-agent`, `oh-my-openagent`, `symphony`, `ccpm`,
`Archon`, `hankweave-runtime`. One subsection each, adopt and reject, with the `file:line` evidence
that supports it - so the review is the synthesis input for the new implementation plan rather than
a set of files on one machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given section 2.11 when it is read after this change then it records that the batch-then-bisect queue is unreachable code with the evidence, states that basicly's serial queue is ahead of what gastown runs, withdraws the recommendation to build bisecting, and names the readme-is-not-evidence failure that produced the original claim, and the other six analysed repos each have a subsection with adopt and reject findings
acceptance_criteria: Given section 2.11 when it is read after this change then it records that the batch-then-bisect queue is unreachable code with the evidence states that basicly serial queue is ahead of what gastown runs withdraws the recommendation to build bisecting and names the readme-is-not-evidence failure that produced the original claim and the other six analysed repos each have a subsection with adopt and reject findings

title: Record that phases stay engine code and declarative phases are rejected
description:
## Context

Owner decision 2026-07-30, after the seven-repo sweep put the question on the table: **the loop's
phases stay engine code. Declarative phases are rejected, not deferred.**

Two of the analysed projects had made phases declarative - Archon a Zod-validated node DAG in
`.archon/workflows/*.yaml`, Symphony an engine that knows only three predicates with the lifecycle in
`WORKFLOW.md` front matter - so the option was real and worth answering rather than ignoring.

Three reasons, in the order that decided it:

1. **The part that would have to move cannot move safely.** `derive_phase`
   (`src/basicly/loop_state.py:106-143`) is a five-rung predicate ladder, and most rungs are
   mechanical enough to express as data. The exception is the `verified` term -
   `gates.can_advance and (worktree is not None or has_children)`, plus ship's
   `(worktree is None or verified)`. That encodes the *landed* invariant found by incident
   `basicly-k35r`: approving ship before the landing wedged the phase with no route back to the
   merge. Expressed in YAML it becomes a boolean expression language, and the invariant lives where
   pyright cannot check it, the test suite cannot easily target it, and review will not catch a
   subtle edit. The general form of the cost is worth stating once: **every rule that moves from
   code to data leaves the type checker, the test suite, and code review.**
2. **Nobody has asked.** Zero beads request configurable phases, no consumer has raised it, and the
   eight phases were stable through the entire factory build. The repo rule is to solve the stated
   requirement rather than build a speculative abstraction.
3. **What a consumer would actually want to vary is already configuration** - `required_gates`,
   `max_rework`, the verify checks per mode, and the autonomy levels all live in `basicly.toml`.
   The demand that declarative phases would serve is largely already served.

Record honestly what the evidence does *not* show. It is tempting to argue that declarativeness
caused the determinism failures in those two projects; it did not. Archon's flaw is a disjunction in
a completion gate (`dag-executor.ts:4602`) and Symphony's is having no persistence at all. Both are
independent design errors in projects that also happened to be configurable. The correlation is not
causation, and the reason to reject is the typed-invariant argument above, not guilt by association.

Two things are adopted independently of this rejection and must not be lost with it:

- `basicly-m4zv.13` - Archon's evidence-artifact presence check, which needs no phase machinery.
- Symphony's three-predicate engine is worth reading as a **simplification prompt** for our own
  ladder rather than as a config feature: if an engine can drive a seven-stage lifecycle knowing
  only active/terminal/neither, our five rungs deserve a look for accidental complexity. Filed
  separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the architecture reference and the implementation plan when each is read after this change then both record that phases stay engine code with the landed-invariant reason and the no-recorded-demand reason, both note that the correlation with those projects' determinism failures is not causation, and the plan states that declarative phases are not on the roadmap
acceptance_criteria: Given the architecture reference and the implementation plan when each is read after this change then both record that phases stay engine code with the landed-invariant reason and the no-recorded-demand reason both note that the correlation with those projects determinism failures is not causation and the plan states that declarative phases are not on the roadmap

title: Record the two restricted licences and withdraw the derivation recommendations
description:
## Context

The licence review of the seven repos swept on 2026-07-30 found **two rider-class restrictions that
the LICENSE file alone does not reveal** - the same class of finding as the `beads_rust` rider that
`references.md` section 2 exists to record. Analysis in
`reference-repos/_analysis/licenses.md`.

Five are clean stock licences: `gastown` MIT (Steve Yegge, 2025, diffed byte-exact), `oh-my-agent`
MIT, `openai/symphony` genuine stock Apache-2.0 with `NOTICE`, `ccpm` MIT (grant covers the markdown,
which matters because the reuse there is methodology and prose), `Archon` MIT. No licence file was
missing anywhere.

**`oh-my-openagent` is not open source.** `LICENSE.md` is the **Sustainable Use License 1.0**
(non-OSI): *"You may use or modify the software only for your own internal business purposes or for
non-commercial or personal use. You may distribute the software or provide it to others only if you do
so free of charge for non-commercial purposes."* Confirmed that the three files cited in review
section 2.12 - `model-resolution-pipeline.ts`, `category-model-requirements.ts`,
`model-settings-compatibility.ts` - all live under `packages/model-core/src/`, and **`model-core` has
no LICENSE of its own**, so the root SUL governs them. Only `pi-goal`, `pi-webfetch` and
`lsp-tools-mcp` carry their own; `omo-senpi/plugin/LICENSE` is a scoped MIT covering six named
portions only.

**`hankweave-runtime` carries a competition restriction through its `NOTICE.md`**, not its LICENSE:
*"By using Hankweave, you agree to Southbridge AI's Terms of Service"*, whose key provisions include
*"Competition restrictions on using Hanks to build competing products"* and *"Managed services
restrictions require prior written consent"*. basicly is a coding-agent harness and hankweave an
agent-orchestration runtime, so the restriction plausibly reaches us. Whether a NOTICE can bind at all
is genuinely unsettled - Apache-2.0 says notices are informational - and that is a question for
someone qualified, not for this bead to resolve.

## What is actually wrong in the repo right now

Two things were committed that these terms do not support, and both are mine:

1. **Review section 2.12** recommends the oh-my-openagent tier logic as *"about 400 lines of pure
   logic that ports to stdlib Python unchanged"*. Under the SUL that is not an available option.
2. **`basicly-vkh0.9`** and the **`basicly-kjc5.58` comment** carry the same recommendation shape -
   adopt these mechanisms, with source line ranges as the reference.

The sharp part: section 2.12 already contains the warning that *"reusing any of this text or deriving
an implementation from a quoted snippet requires reading that project's LICENSE first"* - written in
the same commit that then recommended derivation from two repos whose licences had not been read. The
warning was right and was not followed.

**What survives, and it is most of the value.** A licence restricts copying expression, not learning a
fact. The *measurements* stay usable and are the strongest findings: hankweave's own committed fixture
having 44.5% of events share a millisecond is a measured property of published data, not their code.
The *concepts* - declare a tier rather than a model id, return a provenance enum, clamp an unsupported
setting and record the downgrade, carry a running aggregate so the tail answers the common query - are
ideas. What must stop is treating their source as the implementation reference: no port, no snippet,
no line-by-line transcription, exactly the clean-room posture section 2.10 already sets for
`beads_rust`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given references.md when it is read after this change then all seven repos appear in the section 1 table with revision and reuse verdict, the two restricted licences have their operative clause quoted and their consequence stated, and review section 2.12 and beads vkh0.9 and kjc5.58 no longer recommend porting or deriving from either restricted source while keeping the measurements and concepts that are unaffected
acceptance_criteria: Given references.md when it is read after this change then all seven repos appear in the section 1 table with revision and reuse verdict the two restricted licences have their operative clause quoted and their consequence stated and review section 2.12 and beads vkh0.9 and kjc5.58 no longer recommend porting or deriving from either restricted source while keeping the measurements and concepts that are unaffected

title: Refresh implementation plan section 2 against the tree and fix its entry miscount
description:
## Context

Plan §2 is stamped "checked against the tree at b02b527" and §8 last row makes refreshing it against the tree a standing obligation at the start of each phase. Re-verified 2026-07-26 at 13a4647. Most of §2 holds; four groups do not.

Numbers moved: 39 engine modules -> 40 (session.py); 55 test files -> 57; 1247 tests -> 1416 collected; 19 fragments -> 20 (17 core + 3 local); tracker 42 open / 5 deferred / 4 tombstones / 314 closed -> 60 / 6 / 0 / 332; 3 open epics -> 9 (u6jq agzx m4zv imnu a3ab s2xf as phase-0..5, vkh0 phase-6, jr0l phase-7, kjc5 phase-multi).

A claim inverted: §2 says "Zero fragments declare a scope". One now does - platform-hermetic-tests.fragment.yaml at 62cabc8, projected to .claude/rules/platform-hermetic-tests.md. The row must stop claiming zero.

The inversion produced a measurement that changes Phase 4 framing. AGENTS.md went 7014 -> 8484 chars (+1470, +21%) while .claude/CLAUDE.md (7209) and .github/copilot-instructions.md (7343) did not move at all. So one scoped fragment removed nothing from two families and added 1470 chars to Codex, because codex inlines scoped fragments. Codex max_size_warning is 12000 not 9000 (targets/codex.yaml:6), so there is no gate pressure, but the direction is fixed by construction: for codex, scoping a fragment is strictly a cost increase. §4 Phase 4 currently reads as "not a reduction for codex"; the measurement says "an increase for codex", and Phase 4 exit criterion "smaller on two of three families" is the only achievable form rather than a conservative target.

A miscount: §2 says "7 subagents". There are 3 (code-reviewer, security-auditor, test-runner) plus 4 reusable prompt blocks under .basicly/core/agents/blocks (context-priming, escalation-honesty, evidence-discipline, read-only-discipline) which are composed into agents and are not independently routable. The 48 figure was 19 + 29 with subagents and rubrics listed but never added; the current equivalent is 49 routable entries (20 fragments + 29 projected skills). title: Write the ceremony threshold and the lightweight path below it
description:
## Context

Plan §7.1, resolved by owner decision 2026-07-26. The decision is made; this bead implements it.

DECIDED: the threshold is the touched path. The harness loop is required for any change touching `src/**` or catalog sources under `.basicly/**`. A docs-only, tracker-only, or config-only change may take a lightweight path.

Chosen because it is the only form of the rule that can be enforced rather than hoped for: a hook can check which paths a commit touches. The rule today mandates the loop for "non-trivial work", which is the agents own judgment call, so the rule is currently unenforceable - every loop decision this repo has made was an agent choosing to comply. A diff-size threshold was rejected as a poor proxy: a one-line change to a gate or a hook is exactly the kind of edit that most needs the ceremony.

The lightweight path skips the ceremony and never the hooks. That is the whole point of naming it - an unnamed escape hatch becomes "skip the loop" and then "skip the gates".

## Notes

The threshold belongs in the always-on Harness Loop fragment, and the recall measurement under basicly-agzx.1 is a reason to keep it short: content phrased as an imperative constraint is retrieved, descriptive prose is not - the one rule that scored 0/3 in both families was the only non-imperative line in the file.

Consider whether a hook can assert it, since that is the justification for choosing this form over the alternatives. If it cannot be asserted, say so rather than shipping an unenforceable rule in different words.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/fragments/project/harness-loop.fragment.yaml`
- `docs/design/steering-surfaces-design.md`
acceptance_criteria: Given a written ceremony threshold when a change touches src or catalog sources then the harness loop is required and when a change is docs-only or tracker-only or config-only then a named lightweight path applies that skips the ceremony but never the hooks and the rule is stated as an imperative constraint rather than descriptive prose

title: Absorb the recall test result into the implementation plan
description:
## Problem

`basicly-agzx.1` is closed and its result (claude recalls 98% of 53 baseline rules, copilot 93% of 54, against 17%/6% no-guidance controls) has not been folded back into `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`. Principle 5 of the plan's own section 3 says each phase ends by folding its result into the reference; this one did not.

Six places still read as though 1a had not run:

- Section 2 line 85: the always-on baseline row still asserts **The cliff concern stands** on a word-count argument, which the measurement refuted.
- Section 4 Phase 1 item 1a: written in the imperative as work to do, with no result, no pointer to the committed harness (`.scripts/recall_eval.py` + `.scripts/recall_rules.toml`), and the sentence that no cap change in either direction is legitimate until it runs. The cap policy is now asymmetric: lowering is housekeeping, raising still has no evidence.
- Section 4 Phase 1 exit criteria: three numbers owed, one now delivered; the partial state is not recorded.
- Section 4 Phase 4 priority line: still **P1 if 1a shows a cliff, P2 if it shows a slope**, a conditional that resolved to P2 routine tidying.
- Section 4 Phase 4 exit criteria: **1a's recall test re-run shows improved recall** is close to unsatisfiable now that the baseline measures 98%/93%; the achievable criterion is recall not degraded.
- Section 5 dependency graph and section 6 cut-list still carry 1a as pending work.

Codex stays unmeasured because its CLI is absent, and it is the family that matters most since `AGENTS.md` is the largest baseline and the only one that grows when a fragment is scoped. Any rewrite must say so rather than implying three families were measured.

## Notes

The result must be recorded narrowly. It is mechanism confirmed, never outcome improved: recall under a direct cue is an upper bound and says nothing about whether a rule binds during work, and `catalog-efficacy-design` section 4.1 forbids citing it as evidence of quality. What it kills is only the claim that the baseline is past the cliff so the tokens are wasted.

Docs-only, so no loop track per the ceremony threshold decision (`src/**` or `.basicly/**` requires the loop). Sibling of `basicly-imnu.6`, which covers the section 7 owner decisions and is deliberately separate.

title: Realign the README with the four-pillar positioning the site already ships
description:
## Context

`site/index.html` already leads with the four-pillar framing - guidance, gates, the loop, the
work graph - and says "Most agent harnesses ship instructions and skills. basicly also ships
the workflow and the state". `README.md` still leads with the projector alone: "One command
installs a complete coding-agent harness - instructions, skills, and gates." It never mentions
the loop or the work graph.

So the README lags the site by a whole positioning generation. A visitor arriving from the
repo homepage sees a config compiler and no sign of the 60% of the code that is the
orchestration engine (`loop.py`, `supervise.py`, `merge.py`, `decisions.py`, `rubrics.py`).

Owner decision 2026-07-30: adopt the site's four-pillar framing in the README so both surfaces
match, rather than inventing a third framing.

Both surfaces are also missing the strongest available claim, which is structural rather than
a feature list: the loop and the headless agents it dispatches both read the artifacts the
projection layer emits, so the config layer's output *is* the orchestrator's contract. Nothing
that implements only one half can copy that.

Competitive grounding gathered 2026-07-30, to keep the copy honest: `oh-my-agent` already does
SSOT-to-multi-runtime projection with a CI drift check, so "we project and we gate the
projection" is no longer a unique claim. What remains genuinely ours on that half is
enforcement at *commit time* - it installs no git hooks - so the copy should say commit-time
rather than implying gating in general.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a reader arriving at the README when they read the opening section then it presents the same four pillars as the site with the contract sentence that the loop reads what the projector emits, claims commit-time enforcement rather than gating in general, and no longer describes basicly as only instructions skills and gates
acceptance_criteria: Given a reader arriving at the README when they read the opening section then it presents the same four pillars as the site with the contract sentence that the loop reads what the projector emits, claims commit-time enforcement rather than gating in general, and no longer describes basicly as only instructions skills and gates

title: Correct the two SOTA leads that new comparables have caught up on
description:
## Context

`docs/research/2026-07-26-sota-review.md` section 5 lists six "real, structural leads". Two of
them are now overstated, verified against sources on 2026-07-30:

- Lead 1, "enforcement is code and git hooks, not prose", and lead 3, "agent-agnostic
  projection from one catalog - others ship per-host adapters maintained by hand ... we
  generate, and we gate the generation". `first-fluke/oh-my-agent` keeps `.agents/` as a single
  source of truth, projects it into each runtime's native layout via `oma emit`
  (Agent-Skills-conformant skill folders, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`), and
  ships "a drift check in CI keeping the generated output honest" plus `oma verify <agent>`, a
  deterministic per-agent check battery.

So generate-and-gate is no longer differentiating on its own. What survives is narrower and
should be stated precisely: oh-my-agent installs **no git hooks** - its drift check is CI-only -
so our edge is enforcement at *commit time*, which is a different guarantee from a check that
fails the build afterwards. It also has no autonomous ticket-driven loop, no worktrees and no
merge queue.

The review was also written before six comparables the owner surfaced. The most important is
`gastownhall/gastown`, from the same org as the beads tracker section 2.10 already analyses. It
covers the orchestration half in full - worktree-isolated agents, a Bors-style merge queue that
bisects to isolate a failing MR, a supervisor patrol tier, human-gated convoys - in Go, and it
requires `bd` 0.57+ **plus Dolt plus tmux 3.0+**.

That does not make our orchestration redundant, and the review should say why: Gastown sits on
the DB-authoritative fork section 2.10 deliberately diverged from, so it is evidence the fork is
real and widening rather than evidence we are reinventing. Our dependency floor on that half is
materially lighter - no database, no daemon, no terminal multiplexer.

Also not yet covered: `oh-my-openagent`, `Archon` (YAML phases plus worktrees plus validation
gates), `openai/symphony` (ticket-driven isolated runs), `hankweave` (checkpoint-gated
resumability over existing harnesses), `CCPM` (PRD to parallel agents over GitHub Issues).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the SOTA review when section 5 is read after this change then leads 1 and 3 state the narrowed commit-time claim with oh-my-agent named as the project that matches the CI-gated projection, and the review records Gastown as covering the orchestration half on the DB-authoritative fork with our lighter dependency floor as the stated difference

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
Design proposal (2026-07-16, needs approval before build):

COMMAND SPLIT (from cli.py inventory)
- Consumer (run in a consumer repo, usually via the pinned uvx or the scaffolded VS Code tasks): install, uninstall, build, check, hooks-build, hooks-check, skills-build, skills-check.
- Contributor (author the catalog in this repo): list, skills-list, skills-new, agents-list, agents-new, fragment-new, catalog-lint, catalog-verify, review.
- Harness/agent-facing (either repo, drives the loop): worktree, verify, policy, decompose, loop, runner.
Proposal: encode the split in --help via argparse epilog sections (three grouped lists with one-liners) — no renames, nothing breaking.

UPDATE COMMAND: not needed — re-running install is the documented upgrade path (update was removed pre-release, basicly-zrj.12.1); the readme now says so explicitly.

OUTPUT STYLE, two options:
(a) stdlib-only polish: consistent status glyphs (wrote/removed/unchanged/error), aligned summary line per command (e.g. 'skills: 2 written, 50 unchanged, 1 pruned'), a single install epilogue table of what converged, dim/bold via ANSI only when stdout is a TTY. No new dependency.
(b) rich-based TUI: real tables for list/skills-list, progress spinners for install steps, colored diff-style drift reports for check/skills-check. Requires adding the 'rich' dependency — needs explicit approval per repo policy.
Recommendation: (a) first (cheap, portable, no dependency decision), (b) only if the plain version still feels flat.

Open for the user: pick (a)/(b) and approve the help-grouping approach; then this decomposes into per-command tasks.

title: Decide whether a model tier resolves to an ordered preference list
description:
## Context

Owner requirement described 2026-07-31: a tier should be able to fall back, so that if the tier's
model is unavailable on a family the agent still runs on another model of the SAME capability class
rather than failing or silently inheriting. Split out of basicly-kjc5.61 by owner decision to keep that
lane single-model and land on schedule.

All facts below were verified against live vendor docs today, not recalled.

## What each surface can actually express

- **GitHub Copilot / VS Code: an ordered list, natively.** `model` accepts "a single model name
  (string) or a prioritized list of models (array)", documented example
  `model: ['Claude Opus 4.5', 'GPT-5.2']`, tried in order. So copilot can honour a preference chain
  with no work on our side beyond emitting the array.
- **Claude Code: a single value only.** Subagent frontmatter `model` takes `sonnet`/`opus`/`haiku`/
  `fable`, a full model id (`claude-opus-5`), or `inherit`; it defaults to `inherit`. There is no array
  form. Claude Code resolves a subagent's model in this order: (1) the `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`
  env var, (2) the per-invocation `model` parameter, (3) the definition's `model` frontmatter, (4) the
  main conversation's model. Neither (1) nor (2) is usable for per-agent tiers - the env var is
  session-wide across ALL subagents, and the per-invocation parameter is chosen by the orchestrating
  model, not by the harness. So (3) is our only per-agent slot and it holds one value.
- **Claude Code's own degradation is NOT tier-preserving**: a value excluded by the org
  `availableModels` allowlist is skipped and the subagent "runs on the inherited model instead" -
  which may be any tier, higher or lower.

## The trap this bead exists to prevent

The roster's tier table (docs/design/agent-roster-design.md R5) maps the GPT classes as luna=low,
terra=medium, sol=high AND maximum. So an intuitive-sounding chain like "Claude Opus 5, else
GPT-5.6 Terra" **silently demotes a high-tier judgment to medium**. Any fallback list must be
constrained to same-tier members, and the generator should refuse a chain that mixes tiers rather
than trusting the author to get it right.

## The decision to make

1. Does a tier carry an ordered list, or exactly one model? If a list, is it authored per tier in the
   anchor source, or derived from the map by capability class?
2. What does an unavailable tier model mean where the surface cannot express a chain (claude)? The
   repo's standing rule is fail closed on an indeterminate answer, and "cannot tell" must never read
   as "safe to proceed" - so silently inheriting an unknown tier is arguably the wrong default and a
   refusal or a recorded not-honoured marker may be right. basicly-kjc5.59 already establishes the
   record-the-fallback-rather-than-imply-it stance for a family with no slot; reuse it, do not invent
   a second convention.
3. Whether the fallback is worth having at all given it is honourable on exactly one of our two
   required families today.

## Adjacent observation, not this bead's scope

Both families also expose a REASONING EFFORT axis independent of model choice - Claude Code subagent
frontmatter has `effort` (`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`, overriding session effort) and copilot
custom agents have `reasoningEffort`. A tier arguably wants to carry an effort as well as a model.
Worth its own bead if it turns out to matter; noted here so the observation is not lost.

Scope: `.basicly/core/schemas/agent.schema.json`, `.basicly/core/models/`, `src/basicly/agents.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the decision recorded then either a tier resolves to an ordered same-tier preference list
  which the generator refuses when the list mixes tiers and which is emitted as an array only to a
  surface documented to accept one, or the single-model contract is written down with the reason and
  the behaviour on an unavailable model is stated explicitly rather than left to the host default
acceptance_criteria: Given the decision recorded then either a tier resolves to an ordered same-tier preference list which the generator refuses when the list mixes tiers and which is emitted as an array only to a surface documented to accept one, or the single-model contract is written down with the reason and the behaviour on an unavailable model is stated explicitly rather than left to the host default

title: DX: stop the recurring markdownlint MD060 aligned-table re-pad friction in docs
description:
Recurring DX friction (hit at least three times: v0.2.0 release tables, basicly-h0f0, and noted again in basicly-yw28 prep). markdownlint MD060 uses the "aligned" table style, so editing any cell in a wide docs table (e.g. the command table in docs/architecture.md, ~490 chars wide) requires re-padding every pipe to match the header column widths, and `markdownlint-cli2 --fix` does NOT auto-repad the aligned style. Widening the FIRST column cascades a re-pad to every row. The reliable fix each time is a hand-run Python script that reads the header pipe columns and rebuilds the edited row.

Pick a durable fix so this stops recurring. Candidate directions: (a) add a small committed `.scripts/` helper that re-pads a markdown table to MD060-aligned style (invoked manually or as a pre-commit auto-fix); (b) relax MD060 for docs (switch the config to a non-aligned table style, or disable MD060) accepting ragged pipes; (c) split the offending wide tables so cells stay short. Evaluate the trade-off (aligned tables read better in raw markdown but cost edit friction).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Editing a wide docs table no longer requires a hand-authored re-pad script: either a committed helper does it, or the lint rule no longer demands aligned pipes.
- The chosen approach is applied to docs/architecture.md's wide tables and markdownlint passes.
- Decision (helper vs relax-rule vs split-tables) recorded.
close_reason: disabled MD060 in .markdownlint-cli2.yaml so editing wide aligned tables no longer forces a hand re-pad; verified inconsistent tables lint clean and architecture.md passes; landed via base checkout

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: Decision: disable MD060 (table-column-style) in .markdownlint-cli2.yaml. Root cause investigated — MD060 default style 'any' requires each table to stay internally consistent with one pipe style, so editing one cell of an aligned table without re-padding every pipe errors, and --fix does not re-pad aligned. Chose disable over style:compact+--fix (which would churn every table to ragged) or a re-pad helper: minimal one-line diff, keeps existing aligned tables readable, ragged edits now lint clean. Verified with an inconsistent table (0 MD060) and architecture.md still passes.

title: beads-commit-msg id detection should be prefix-anchored like beads own scanner
description:
beads-commit-msg.py validates issue-id references with a too-loose regex '\b[a-z][a-z0-9]*-[a-z0-9]+\b' that matches ANY hyphenated word, not just the configured beads prefix. The beads rust tool (br orphans) scans commits with a prefix-anchored pattern '\b(<prefix>)-[a-z0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)*\b', matching the id token by word boundary anywhere in the message (trailing parenthetical or footer alike). Because our hook is looser, when a commit lacks a matching known id it reports a confusing 'unknown beads issue id: fork-drove, the-loop' listing hyphenated description words as offenders, obscuring the real cause (no valid trailing id). Investigation (br 0.2.16 binary) confirms beads matches the id anywhere by prefix, so the current trailing-paren format is fine and no footer migration is needed. Fix: align our hook's id detection with beads' prefix-anchored scanner, deriving the prefix set from the known ids.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Write a commit whose description has a hyphenated multi-word phrase (e.g. fork-drove-the-loop) and omit or typo the trailing beads id
2. beads-commit-msg rejects with 'unknown beads issue id: fork-drove, the-loop', naming description words as ids
3. The real cause (no valid trailing id present) is obscured by the red-herring candidates

## Acceptance Criteria

* beads-commit-msg detects candidate ids with a prefix-anchored pattern mirroring beads' own scanner, so non-prefix hyphenated words are never treated as ids
* the prefix set is derived from the known ids with no new configuration
* a commit with a valid trailing id passes regardless of hyphenated description words; a missing id yields the no-id error; a typo'd prefix id (basicly-nope) yields an accurate unknown-id error naming only that token
* regression tests cover the valid-id-with-hyphens pass and the missing-id and typo cases

Caveat found during verification: nested AGENTS.md scoping is DIRECTORY-based while basicly scoped fragments are GLOB-based (**/*.py), so per-directory offload cannot faithfully express glob scopes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Architecture §7.4 corrected: Codex has skills + nested AGENTS.md; scoped fragments stay inlined for glob fidelity (directory-scoped nesting cannot express globs), with the verification date and sources recorded.
- Cap decision recorded in §7.1: the shared 8000 soft cap stays for CLAUDE.md/copilot; the codex target gets a documented higher warning threshold (justified by the inlined scoped content and the verified 32 KiB real budget) — codex.yaml max_size_warning updated to match, and the current AGENTS.md (8022) no longer sits over its cap.
- Projector offload via nested AGENTS.md/skills explicitly deferred with the glob-vs-directory rationale.
