- `tests/` plus a shared fixture helper
acceptance_criteria: Given a fixture repository with a real git history and a real br tracker when a leaf lands and a lane runs its sub-tasks then the integration test asserts the merge the recorded gate and the closed bead without stubbing git or br and it runs in the default pytest selection

title: Dogfood the factory: run a real basicly feature through loop supervise end to end
description:
## Context

Filed in the 2026-07-24 triage. The epic success criterion is that the eleven components are "implemented and dogfooded on basicly itself", but every component to date was built through the single-track loop (intake/classify/build/land/ship, one bead at a time, human-driven). Nothing tracks the factory actually running as a factory, so the epic can reach all-components-closed without `basicly loop supervise` ever having orchestrated a real multi-child feature.

This is the acceptance run for components 5-7: pick a genuine basicly feature with three or more unblocked children, start the supervisor, and let it fan out worktrees, dispatch lanes concurrently, run the lane mini-loop, route outcomes and land through the consume-as-ready merge queue. Record what it cost and where it needed a human.

Recommended to land first (not hard blockers): basicly-kjc5.18 (held lanes are re-dispatched, wasting a full implement pass), basicly-kjc5.15 (a stalled runner leaves grandchildren mutating the worktree), basicly-kjc5.14 (the D8 occupancy ceiling is inert for claude lanes), basicly-kjc5.19 (lane validate is vacuous), and the prose pass basicly-sco6/basicly-z25w/basicly-l7zo (each is a commit-time rejection a dispatched lane cannot diagnose, costing a bounded rework attempt).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a real basicly feature with at least three unblocked children when loop supervise runs then it dispatches the lanes concurrently and lands them through the merge queue without a human editing code, and the run is written up with per-lane token cost, every human intervention it required, and a bead filed for each defect found

## Scope

- No production code by default; findings land as new beads
acceptance_criteria: Given a real basicly feature with at least three unblocked children when loop supervise runs then it dispatches the lanes concurrently and lands them through the merge queue without a human editing code and the run is written up with per-lane token cost every human intervention it required and a bead filed for each defect found

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
DOGFOOD RUN 2026-07-25 - results.

Root: basicly-jr0l.9 (the three D10 operator-surface consequences, .42 .43 .44). Runner: claude headless via a gitignored basicly.local.toml. Autonomy L0 (no grant); guardrails max_rework=0 and runner_timeout=1200 to bound re-dispatch.

WHAT HAPPENED. The supervisor adopted three lanes and dispatched them concurrently. All three agents did real work. Two committed (.42 886 insertions incl a new commit.py and 364 lines of tests; .43 519 across 10 files), both with correct Conventional Commits and a beads trailer, unprompted. The third timed out at 1200s with work uncommitted. Then all three lanes FAILED TO LAND: the two that finished crossed the D8 context ceiling (145570 and 145489 vs 120000), correctly entered the 7.6 finalize protocol, and crashed creating the follow-up bead. Routed to the decision queue; the pass halted with 3 decisions pending and merged nothing.

COST. 25250591 tokens this pass (.42 7674671 / .43 7695800 / .44 9880120), ~21.40 USD at list rate; 30705839 including an earlier aborted pass. Roughly 8M tokens per agentic lane. This draws the Team seat allowance, not per-token API billing (auth is the OAuth subscription credential; no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set).

HUMAN INTERVENTIONS REQUIRED. 1) provisioning the worktrees - supervise does not fan out, so the root had to be driven through the single-track loop first; 2) configuring the runner - loop supervise takes no options, so a config edit is the only way; 3) three checkpoint approvals; 4) disposing 3 decisions; 5) landing both lanes by hand after the crash; 6) reviewing the agent code before it reached main.

DEFECTS FILED. jr0l.7 local config overlay not gitignored (FIXED). jr0l.8 loop supervise cannot pin a runner or autonomy per session. jr0l.10 a provider usage-limit refusal is reworked as a merit failure and the pass prints no spend while it runs. jr0l.11 finalize_followup spliced --parent between -t and its value so no overrun follow-up could ever be created from a child lane (FIXED). jr0l.12 the overrun follow-up drops acceptance criteria held in the description body. jr0l.13 commit envelope rules duplicated from the commit-msg hook. Unfiled observations: supervise never provisions worktrees though section 3 component 5 claims fan-out and section 9 marks it landed; the shipped claude adapter passes no permission mode where codex carries sandbox and approval.

WHAT WORKED. Concurrent dispatch, the process budget, D8 metering and the context ceiling, runner_timeout, the stall queue, outcome routing, max_rework=0 containment, and loop session as a live read against a running supervisor.

STILL OPEN. The acceptance criterion is not met: the lanes did not land through the merge queue without a human editing code. jr0l.11 was the blocker and is fixed, but that path has not been re-run. .42 and .43 were landed by hand and are on main (CI green, 3 runners); .44's partial work is committed unlanded on harness/basicly-kjc5-44.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
SIZING RETRO - why the lanes cost what they did.

Owner's rule stated 2026-07-25: agent cost is bounded implicitly by cutting each agent's work to the right size, never explicitly by stopping an agent mid-work. The roster (docs/agent-roster-design.md) is what supplies that capability - Dana at the maximum tier producing tight scope globs, R5 tier routing, section 6 lever 2 keep every dispatch inside the D8 band.

Measured against that rule, this run's cost was self-inflicted. basicly-jr0l.9 was hand-assembled by re-parenting three existing backlog beads, so decompose never ran and govern_working_set never ran. D8 is estimate then govern then meter; only the meter fired, which is exactly why two lanes crossed the context ceiling.

basicly-u6tw now makes this checkable, and run against the three packages this dogfood dispatched it refuses two of them in advance:

  assemble the commit envelope (kjc5.42)  103271 tokens  REFUSED (max 64000)  -> overran the ceiling at 145570
  apply the formatters        (kjc5.43)    8696 tokens  in band              -> the only lane that finished cleanly
  scaffold bead sections      (kjc5.44)  103271 tokens  REFUSED (max 64000)  -> timed out at 1200s, committed nothing

Perfect correlation: the one in-band package succeeded, both out-of-band packages failed as the estimate predicted, and the estimate was available before any token was spent. A re-run of this dogfood must decompose the root through the governor rather than re-parenting beads by hand.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
DOGFOOD RE-RUN 2026-07-26 - ACCEPTANCE CRITERION MET.

Root: basicly-hxnf, a real feature (document three verified tool behaviours in the skills that own them), DECOMPOSED THROUGH THE GOVERNOR rather than assembled by re-parenting - the correction the 2026-07-25 sizing retro demanded. Runner: claude headless via the gitignored basicly.local.toml. Autonomy L0. Guardrails runner_timeout=1200, max_rework=1 (raised to 2 mid-run, see interventions).

PRE-FLIGHT. decompose --dry-run put all three children inside the D8 band before a token was spent: 13994 / 27584 / 30392 against the 64000 max, three children in three parallel groups. Contrast the previous run where the same check would have REFUSED two of three packages at 103271.

WHAT HAPPENED. Pass 1: three lanes adopted and dispatched CONCURRENTLY via claude, all three finished and committed. Context occupancy 50843 / 53684 / 63894 against the 120000 ceiling - no lane came close, so the 7.6 finalize protocol never fired and could not crash it (the previous run overran at 145570 and 145489). hxnf.1's landing failed its verify gate and escalated; hxnf.2 and hxnf.3 held. Pass 2: both carried lanes LANDED THROUGH THE MERGE QUEUE unattended. Pass 3: idle, 3 decisions pending. hxnf.1 landed afterwards through the same merge path once its rework cap was lifted.

COST. 3361523 tokens total, 3.91 USD at list rate, against the previous run's 25250591 tokens / 21.40 USD. Per lane: hxnf.1 1022380 tokens / 1.21 USD / 201s; hxnf.2 856182 / 1.11 / 196s; hxnf.3 1482961 / 1.59 / 388s. That is ~1.1M per lane against ~8.4M before - a 7.5x reduction from right-sizing alone, with the same runner and the same autonomy level. Direct evidence for the owner's rule: bound cost by sizing the work, not by stopping an agent.

AGENT QUALITY. All three lanes stayed exactly in scope - three files each, their own skill source plus its two projections. No lane touched another lane's files, none committed tracker state, and every lane regenerated its projections unprompted, so the projection rejection that sco6/z25w/l7zo exist to prevent never occurred. All three commit messages were valid Conventional Commits carrying the beads id. Two lanes exceeded their brief usefully: hxnf.1 also documented that parentheses remain required when the clause binds with as, and hxnf.2 also found the br dep remove path for changing an edge type and the exit-0-on-no-op trap. Post-run review of all three diffs found one defect (basicly-g7os).

HUMAN INTERVENTIONS - nine, and NONE of them edited code. 1) driving the root through the single-track loop to fan out worktrees, because loop supervise still does not provision them though section 3 component 5 claims fan-out and section 9 marks it landed; 2) pinning the runner by config edit (jr0l.8); 3) classify checkpoint; 4) decompose checkpoint; 5) answering hxnf.1's escalation; 6) raising max_rework 1->2 in config, the only lever available because an answered retry cannot clear the counter (basicly-4tjt); 7) re-running hxnf.1's landing by hand, because the supervisor had already exited; 8) four ship checkpoints (three children plus the feature) - L0 by design; 9) restoring the runner to manual. Against the previous run this drops landing the lanes by hand and fixing agent code.

DEFECTS FILED. basicly-4tjt (P1) an answered retry escalation cannot be acted on because nothing clears the rework counter - the escalation offers retry/re-dispatch/park and implements none. basicly-8veb (P2) loop supervise hides its own progress when stdout is a pipe, so a logged run shows the lanes' hook and pytest noise and none of the orchestration until exit - the lanes had finished and spent 3.36M tokens before the first routed line was visible. basicly-55yh (P2) a flaky gate consumes a lane's rework budget as if the work were wrong - hxnf.1's verify died on the known br clock defect in test_landing_blocks_instead_of_reworking_an_uncommitted_worktree, which then passed twice on re-run in the lane's own worktree with no change. basicly-g7os (P3) the python skill description runs two triggers together after the dogfood edit.

CONFIRMED EXISTING BEADS. kjc5.29 - the run records carry model=None, so no run can be attributed to a model. kjc5.50 - forecast_tokens and scope_tokens are null on every run record, so the D8 estimate computed at decompose is never persisted next to the actual and this run's 7.5x improvement had to be reconstructed by hand from two write-ups.

VERIFIED AFTER. verify --mode full PASS (1213 tests, 8/8 checks) plus check, skills-check --all-default-roots, agents-check and hooks-check all up to date. All four beads closed, all worktrees and branches torn down, runner restored to manual.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
Closing: the acceptance criterion is met. A real feature (basicly-hxnf) with three unblocked children, decomposed through the governor, was dispatched concurrently by loop supervise and landed through the merge queue with no human editing code; the run is written up above with per-lane token cost and every human intervention, and four defects were filed (basicly-4tjt, basicly-8veb, basicly-55yh, basicly-g7os) plus two existing beads confirmed (kjc5.29, kjc5.50).

Honest caveat on 'unattended': two of the three lanes landed inside the supervisor run with no human in the path at all. The third (hxnf.1) needed an operator to answer its escalation and raise the rework cap in config before the same merge path landed it - because a pre-existing flake failed its gate (basicly-55yh) and an answered retry cannot clear the counter (basicly-4tjt). No code was edited by a human at any point, which is what the criterion tests, but those two beads are what stands between this and a genuinely hands-off run.

Not driven through the build phase deliberately: this bead's scope is 'no production code by default; findings land as new beads', so there is nothing for a worktree to commit.

title: Halt supervisor dispatch when the grant token budget is spent
description:
## Context

Design-coverage gap found in the 2026-07-24 audit of docs/factory-design.md against the code. D3 says: "The supervisor enforces the grant `token_budget`: once run-record spend for the session reaches it, **no new dispatches** or delegated decisions occur - the session drops to human-only until re-granted." The stated purpose is that "unbounded lights-out" is unreachable.

Only half of that is built. `policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded` checks `spent >= grant.token_budget` and returns None, so *delegated checkpoint approvals* stop (policy.py around line 520). But `supervise.py` never reads the grant or the spend at all - its only grant contact is passing `grant_root=` into that approval call - so the supervisor keeps provisioning worktrees and dispatching lane runners after the budget is exhausted. Under an L2/L3 grant the spend ceiling is therefore advisory on the largest spender in the system.

Fix: check `policy.session_spend_tokens` against the active grant before each dispatch in the supervisor pass; when the budget is reached, dispatch nothing new, let in-flight lanes finish and land, and surface the halt (decision queue item or pass detail) so the human knows re-granting is required. The decider is covered by the same halt per D3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an L2 or L3 grant whose token budget is already spent when a supervisor pass runs then no new lane or decider dispatch starts while in-flight lanes still land and the halt is surfaced to the human with tests

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`, `src/basicly/policy.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given an L2 or L3 grant whose token budget is already spent when a supervisor pass runs then no new lane or decider dispatch starts while in-flight lanes still land and the halt is surfaced to the human with tests

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: D9 adoption 2026-07-25: verified that session_spend_tokens has exactly one caller - policy.py:521 inside _grant_approval - so the halt is consulted only when approving a checkpoint and never at dispatch admission. basicly-kjc5.31 adds the two missing spenders (judge and decider) to the meter; this bead owns enforcing the ceiling where D3 says it enforces.

title: Propose a dependency edge from a coupling found-info record
description:
## Context

Design-coverage gap found in the 2026-07-24 audit. Design 7.4 says a `[harness-info]` record with `kind=coupling` "additionally proposes a dependency edge", and D6 says the supervisor "adds dependency edges where it implies a missed coupling" so the graph learns from a discovery rather than only from a merge collision.

Built today: `record_found_info`/`parse_found_info`/`found_info_records` and the folding into future dispatch bundles (`build_bundle`), which is the reading half of D6. The edge-proposing half is absent - the only `dep add ... blocks` calls in the engine are decompose sequencing, the D5 merge bounce (`merge.record_coupling`), and the finalize follow-up. `FOUND_INFO_KINDS` names `coupling` and a comment says it "implies a missed coupling", but no code acts on it.

Fix: when a `kind=coupling` record names or scope-overlaps other session beads, record the `blocks` edge (reuse `merge.record_coupling`) so a lane that *discovers* a coupling teaches the graph immediately, instead of the graph only learning after a landing collides. Keep it idempotent - a re-read record must not add duplicate edges.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a lane that publishes a kind coupling found-info record affecting another session bead when the supervisor next reads records then a blocks edge is recorded once between the affected beads and the landing order honors it with tests

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a lane that publishes a kind coupling found-info record affecting another session bead when the supervisor next reads records then a blocks edge is recorded once between the affected beads and the landing order honors it with tests

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
[design-input from kjc5.26] Three findings from the kjc5.26 build that this bead must absorb before it is implemented.

1. DIRECTION. A kind=coupling record published by lane L naming or scope-overlapping bead B means the two are coupled. The edge to record is B blocks-on L (br dep add B L -t blocks): L is the discoverer and is already ahead, so B is the one to serialize behind it.

2. THE EDGE OVER-WAITS - this bead is now blocked on basicly-grrb. merge.record_coupling writes a gating blocks edge, and ready_lanes drops any bead br reports as blocked. A blocks edge releases only when the blocker CLOSES, but a supervisor-landed lane is merged and parks in verify awaiting a human ship approval - so it stays open. Proposing an edge onto an in-flight or just-landed lane therefore strands the affected bead behind a human rather than merely serializing it, which is the opposite of what D6 wants. grrb is the fix (the gate must release on LAND, not on CLOSE); implementing this bead before it would spread the same defect from the bounce path to the found-info path.

3. IDEMPOTENCE IS FREE. Verified against a throwaway br repo on 2026-07-26: a repeated br dep add prints 'Dependency already exists' and leaves exactly one dependency row. merge.record_coupling already wraps it in try_run_br, so the AC's 'recorded once' needs no extra bookkeeping - only that re-reading records is safe to re-run.

Placement still to settle at pickup: the proposal should run once per supervisor pass (in the _cmd_loop_supervise body, before dispatch) rather than inside build_bundle - build_bundle is called concurrently from the dispatch threads, so writing edges there means concurrent br writes and a nondeterministic graph.

title: Detect a stalled lane runner and queue it as possibly-stuck
description:
## Context

Design-coverage gap found in the 2026-07-24 audit. Design 6 defines `[runner] stall_after = 900` s: "No output/commit activity -> flagged possibly-stuck to decision queue". Nothing named `stall` exists anywhere in `src/basicly/`; only `runner_timeout` (3600 s hard kill) is implemented, so a wedged lane holds a concurrency slot for a full hour with no signal, and the human learns about it only when the hard kill fires.

Fix: sample the dispatch for activity (runner stdout progress and/or new commits on the harness branch) and, past `stall_after` with no activity, enqueue a possibly-stuck decision item for that lane while the run continues - it is a flag, not a kill; the timeout remains the terminal action. Add the config knob with the documented default.

Depends on basicly-kjc5.15 in spirit: a stall that is escalated and then killed must take the whole process tree with it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dispatched lane with no output or commit activity past stall_after when the supervisor samples it then a possibly-stuck decision item is queued once for that lane and the run is left to continue until runner_timeout with tests

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`, `src/basicly/supervise.py`, `src/basicly/config.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a dispatched lane with no output or commit activity past stall_after when the supervisor samples it then a possibly-stuck decision item is queued once for that lane and the run is left to continue until runner_timeout with tests

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: Correction 2026-07-25 (triage): the Context line 'Nothing named stall exists anywhere in src/basicly/' is no longer true and will mislead whoever picks this up. A stall decision KIND now exists (decisions.KINDS) and supervise._dispatch_lane enqueues it - but only on the runner_timeout hard kill, which is precisely the gap this bead names. Still genuinely absent: stall_after itself, from both config.py and basicly.toml, so there is no no-activity sampling and a wedged lane still holds a slot for the full hour. The bead's substance is unchanged; only its absence claim needs rewording when picked up.

title: Cancel and re-dispatch a running lane invalidated by a landing
description:
## Context

Design-coverage gap found in the 2026-07-24 audit. D6 ends: "If a landed lane invalidates a running lane assumptions, the supervisor **cancels and re-dispatches** that lane rather than messaging it." This is the write-side counterpart to the fold-at-dispatch rule - never mutate a running lane, but do not let it keep building on a base that moved out from under it either.

Not implemented: the only cancellation in `supervise.py` is the executor shutdown on lock loss. A lane whose declared scope was just rewritten by a landing runs to completion and then discovers the problem as a merge conflict, spending a full dispatch plus a bounce-back rework attempt.

Open design question to settle at pickup: what counts as invalidation. The cheap deterministic reading is a scope-glob overlap between the landed lane changed paths and the running lane declared scope - the same signal `merge.missed_couplings` already computes, applied pre-emptively instead of after the collision. Needs a guard against thrash: re-dispatch at most once per lane per landing, counted against the rework cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a running lane whose declared scope overlaps the paths a just-landed lane changed when the supervisor observes the landing then that lane run is cancelled and re-dispatched at most once against the new base counted against the rework cap with tests

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a green lane whose branch no longer merges cleanly because of paths another lane landed in the same pass when the supervisor routes that lane then its landing is skipped and it is re-dispatched at most once per pass with the collision published as a kind coupling found-info record for its next prompt counted against the dispatch rework cap and escalating at the cap with tests

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: [design-narrowing] The AC originally triggered the cancel on declared-scope overlap with a landing's changed paths. Review (2026-07-26) showed two defects in that reading, both verified: (1) merge.record_coupling writes a GATING blocks edge justified by 'the lane it names is done', but a lane the supervisor just landed is merged and not shipped - still open - so the edge dropped the cancelled lane out of ready_lanes and held it behind a human ship approval, the opposite of re-dispatching it; (2) scope overlap is not a collision, so cancelling on it spent an agent run replacing landings that would have succeeded, and the re-dispatch was uninformed (nothing rebases a lane worktree at dispatch time and no found-info was published, so the second run saw the same tree and the same prompt). Owner approved narrowing the trigger to merge.probe_merge (git merge-tree, exact and non-destructive) attributed via merge.missed_couplings, and replacing the dependency edge with a kind=coupling found-info record that build_bundle folds into the lane's next prompt. Follow-up bead filed for the same gating-edge defect on the D5 bounce path.

title: Provision worktrees against the callers repo root not the process cwd
description:
## Context

Session retro 2026-07-25. Every other engine module takes `repo_root` explicitly (`loop.advance`, `merge.*`, `policy.*`, `supervise.*`), but `worktree.create(name, base=None)` takes no repo root at all - it resolves `worktrees_root()` and `current_branch()` from the **process cwd**. So `loop.advance(repo_root=X)` provisions the worktree wherever the process happens to be standing, silently ignoring the repo root it was handed.

Incident: a driver exercising `loop.advance` against a sandbox repo, launched from the basicly checkout, created two real worktrees and two real `harness/*` branches **in basicly itself** (recovered with `git worktree remove --force` plus `git branch -D`). No user-facing bug today because the CLI always runs with cwd at the repo root, but it makes the engine untestable against a fixture repo: this is exactly what basicly-kjc5.21 has to do, and an integration test that pollutes the developer checkout is worse than no test.

Fix: thread `repo_root` through the worktree module (`create`, `worktrees_root`, `current_branch`, `load_session`, teardown) so the caller decides which repository is operated on, defaulting to the discovered root for the CLI path. Prefer a default argument over a second code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a caller that passes a repo root different from the process cwd when a worktree is provisioned or torn down then it is created under that repo root and the process cwd repository is untouched with a test that drives provisioning against a fixture repo

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From the basicly checkout, call `loop.advance(repo_root=<other repo>)` on an issue whose phase is build (or call `worktree.create("probe")` directly with the process cwd inside basicly).
2. Observe `git worktree list` and `git branch --list 'harness/*'` in the basicly checkout.
3. The worktree and its `harness/probe` branch are created under `basicly.worktrees/`, not under the repo root that was passed; the target repo is untouched.

Expected: the worktree is provisioned under the caller-supplied repo root and the process cwd repository is unmodified.
acceptance_criteria: Given a caller that passes a repo root different from the process cwd when a worktree is provisioned or torn down then it is created under that repo root and the process cwd repository is untouched with a test that drives provisioning against a fixture repo

title: Record the dispatch inputs that make a run reproducible
description:
## Context

D9 (docs/factory-design.md) requires every dispatch to be reproducible in its inputs and recorded in its outputs. Today the run-record carries agent model and command but no adapter version and no prompt hash, and supervise.build_bundle folds found-info records in br comment order truncated to the newest 20 without recording which ones were folded. So a rework attempt sees a different prompt than the attempt before it and neither prompt survives - nothing can say whether attempt 2 differed because the model varied or because the input did.

Add to the run-record: the resolved runner name, the resolved model, the adapter CLI version, a sha256 of the exact prompt, the ids of the folded found-info records, and the scope token count used for sizing. latest_record already drops unknown fields so the schema change is backward tolerant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two dispatches of the same node when their run-records are compared then the resolved runner and model and adapter version and prompt hash and folded record ids are all present and any difference in the prompt is attributable to a recorded input difference

## Scope

- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/runner.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given two dispatches of the same node when their run-records are compared then the resolved runner and model and adapter version and prompt hash and folded record ids are all present and any difference in the prompt is attributable to a recorded input difference

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: Design locked 2026-07-25 (owner): the carrier is a new br comment marker family [harness-run] on the bead, one marker per dispatch, NOT the self-ignored run-records file. Header id is content-derived like decision_id_for - <bead>#<sha6(prompt_sha+phase)>-<attempt> - so a re-write is idempotent rather than duplicated. Payload carries agent, model, adapter_version, prompt_sha256, tokens, cost, estimated, duration_s, returncode, timed_out, handoff, scope_tokens, forecast_tokens, folded_info. Comments are exported in issues.jsonl (confirmed: 140 harness markers already committed), so this is the shared ledger per D11. calibrated_build_factors and latest_record switch to reading markers via br; the local usage file is dropped rather than maintained as a second writer. Owner confirmed jsonl volume is acceptable.

title: Refuse to dispatch a runner whose model is unresolved
description:
## Context

D9 requires dispatch inputs to be pinned. No built-in RunnerSpec sets model and basicly.toml pins none either so with default auto the agent family is resolved by a PATH scan plus a live help probe and the model is whatever the CLI defaults to that day. The four-tier cost argument in the roster design rests on a mapping nothing currently requires.

Require a concrete model per configured agent with sane per-adapter defaults and refuse to dispatch when a tier resolves to nothing - the same stance _apply_model already takes when a model placeholder has no model. Keep the resolved value in the run-record and the Harness-Model trailer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a configured agent with no resolvable model when a dispatch is attempted then the engine refuses with a clear message naming the agent and the config key and given a resolvable model then the resolved value reaches the run-record and the commit trailer

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
acceptance_criteria: Given a configured agent with no resolvable model when a dispatch is attempted then the engine refuses with a clear message naming the agent and the config key and given a resolvable model then the resolved value reaches the run-record and the commit trailer
close_reason: Decomposed into basicly-kjc5.58 (declare a model per agent), basicly-kjc5.59 (refuse an unresolved dispatch and record the resolved value) and basicly-kjc5.60 (carry it into the commit trailer). Deferred 2026-07-26 as undispatchable at 77601 working-set tokens against a band maximum of 64000; the validated three-way split in the comment above is now filed, every child in band and the two later ones disjoint. Not abandoned - superseded by its own decomposition.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
[harness-sizing] Deferred 2026-07-26: not dispatchable as sized. The D8 governor estimates 77601 working-set tokens against a band of 8000..64000 - 21 percent above the maximum - and its guidance is to split it into smaller top-level packages.

A validated three-way split along the acceptance criteria, every child in band and every scope group disjoint so they can run as parallel lanes:

  36228  declare a model per configured agent with per-adapter defaults   src/basicly/config.py, basicly.toml
  52707  refuse to dispatch an unresolved model and record the resolved value   src/basicly/runner.py, src/basicly/run_record.py
  13326  carry the resolved model into the commit trailer   src/basicly/commit.py

The first gates the other two, which are disjoint from each other. Reopen by decomposing along those lines.

Deferred rather than left ready because nothing enforces the band at dispatch - basicly-jr0l.16 - so the supervisor would otherwise have dispatched it at 77601 silently, which is the failure the repo already knows in the other direction: cost is bounded by sizing the work, never by killing an agent mid-run.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
[harness-info] Prerequisite for the cost calibration, recorded 2026-07-26 after the u6jq.1 proof run.

Per-model calibration is impossible without the model provenance this bead lands. The same work costs different amounts on different models and models are replaced constantly, so a forecast calibrated across an unpinned mapping is noise - which is the same argument the plan already makes for 7bur, now with numbers behind it: three lanes forecast in band cost 34 dollars, at 160 to 420 times their forecast, dispatched with no model recorded.

So this bead gates basicly-jr0l.21 (forecast spend and wall clock per model) as well as basicly-7bur. It remains deferred pending the validated three-way split in the note above; that split is now on the critical path for two things rather than one.

title: Autonomy grant ledger L0-L3
description:
Component 3. Session-scoped grant ledger L0-L3 as [harness-policy] markers on the session root issue; issuance interactive-only (TTY/confirm-code); approve_checkpoint_guarded accepts a covering grant; token_budget required for L2+ and enforced by a spend halt (D3). Plumb br attribution flags through dispatch. Declared scope: src/basicly/policy.py, src/basicly/cli.py, src/basicly/config.py.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an interactively issued grant when an agent approves a delegable checkpoint then approve_checkpoint_guarded accepts it only within the grant level and preconditions, refuses agent-issued grants, and refuses L2+ grants without a token budget, with tests
acceptance_criteria: Given an interactively issued grant when an agent approves a delegable checkpoint then approve_checkpoint_guarded accepts it only within the grant level and preconditions, refuses agent-issued grants, and refuses L2+ grants without a token budget, with tests

title: Freeze the sizing estimate at plan acceptance
description:
## Context

D8 calls the sizing estimator deterministic and it is - per invocation. Across invocations it drifts: calibrated_build_factors recomputes a rolling median over the last calibration_window samples and re-derives scope read cost against the current tree because the record does not persist it. So govern_working_set can refuse a plan today that it accepted last week with no change to the plan or the code. D9 forbids a gate whose verdict depends on when it runs.

Persist scope_tokens at dispatch and stamp the resolved build factor and estimate onto the child bead when the governor accepts it so re-running the same plan reuses the recorded estimate instead of a drifted one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a plan the governor accepted when the same plan is governed again after unrelated landings have changed the calibration window then the recorded estimate is reused and the verdict is unchanged

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a plan the governor accepted when the same plan is governed again after unrelated landings have changed the calibration window then the recorded estimate is reused and the verdict is unchanged

title: Bound and meter the judge and decider dispatches
description:
## Context

D9 requires every agent dispatch to be timed out and metered and section 6 calls runner_timeout a hard kill per dispatch. Two call sites escape both: rubrics.evaluate (src/basicly/rubrics.py:227) and decisions.invoke_decider (src/basicly/decisions.py:476) call runner.run with no timeout and no capture_usage and neither writes a run-record. A hung judge or decider therefore hangs the pass forever and their tokens never reach run-records.json so policy.session_spend_tokens under-counts and the D3 grant budget leaks on two real spenders.

Pass runner_timeout and capture usage at both sites and record a run for each. The judge parses plain-text stdout today so metering must not change what it reads - use the format-aware extraction or fall back to the estimate.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a runner whose command blocks forever and make a lane select a rubric with a judged check.
2. Run the lane integrate advance.
3. The pass hangs with no timeout - runner_timeout is never passed. Separately after any decider or judge dispatch inspect run-records.json and observe no record and no token attribution for it.

Expected: both dispatches are killed at runner_timeout and both appear in the run-record with their token usage counted against the session grant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a judge or decider dispatch that exceeds runner_timeout then the process tree is killed and the pass reports it and given a completed judge or decider dispatch then a run-record exists for it and its tokens count toward session spend

## Scope

- `src/basicly/rubrics.py`
- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a judge or decider dispatch that exceeds runner_timeout then the process tree is killed and the pass reports it and given a completed judge or decider dispatch then a run-record exists for it and its tokens count toward session spend

title: Attribute a missed coupling independently of landing order
description:
## Context

D9 forbids any outcome that outlives the pass from depending on completion order. supervise._bounce_lane attributes a missed coupling via merge.missed_couplings against landed - the lanes that landed earlier in this same pass - and merge.record_coupling then writes a blocks edge into the graph permanently where it changes future decompositions. Which lane receives the edge therefore depends on thread interleaving. This is the only place in the engine where scheduling order mutates long-lived state.

Attribute from the declared scopes of the two lanes plus the conflicting paths and compute it after the pass over all landings rather than incrementally.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a supervisor pass with two lanes whose declared scopes both touch a shared path so the second landing conflicts.
2. Repeat the pass with the lane completion order reversed (vary the runner durations).
3. The recorded blocks edge points a different way each time even though the plan and the scopes are identical.

Expected: the coupling edge is a function of the declared scopes and the conflicting paths only and is identical under any completion order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two lanes whose scopes collide when the pass is run with either completion order then the recorded coupling edge is identical and is derived from the declared scopes rather than from which lane landed first

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given two lanes whose scopes collide when the pass is run with either completion order then the recorded coupling edge is identical and is derived from the declared scopes rather than from which lane landed first

title: Stop copying the tracker database into every work-repo fixture
description:
## Context

tests/test_cli.py work_repo copytrees the whole repo per test ignoring only .git and .venv. That leaves .beads (beads.db is 44 MB and about 110 MB on disk with its WAL and shm) plus node_modules at 16 MB in every copy - about 132 MB per test across roughly 44 tests so a full run wrote about 2 GB of tmp. tmp_path_retention_policy = failed now deletes it for passing tests so the disk symptom is gone but the copy cost is paid on every test either way and it grows with the tracker.

Add .beads and node_modules to the ignore_patterns after confirming no work_repo test reads the tracker or needs installed node modules. Where a test genuinely needs a tracker seed it with a minimal one rather than the real 44 MB db.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the work-repo fixture when a test copies the repo then the copy excludes the tracker database and node_modules and the whole suite still passes with any test that needs a tracker given a minimal seeded one instead

## Scope

- `tests/test_cli.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given the work-repo fixture when a test copies the repo then the copy excludes the tracker database and node_modules and the whole suite still passes with any test that needs a tracker given a minimal seeded one instead

title: Reword the confirm-code challenge so an agent knows it may execute after approval
description:
## Context

Session correction 2026-07-25. cli.py:1982 and cli.py:2033 print "no interactive terminal detected; a human must re-run with the one-time code" on a checkpoint challenge. An agent reads that as "the human's hands must type this" and hands the command over, which wastes a round-trip and races the 900 second code TTL - a ship code did expire between the ask and the paste. The owner states the intent was always that an agent may execute the command once the user approves: what the gate protects is the human decision not the keystrokes.

Reword both sites to say the decision needs a human and the caller may re-run with the code once approved. Teach the protocol in the harness-loop skill as well - present the command and what approving it does, get an explicit answer, then run it - since the skill currently documents only the plain --approve form and says nothing about the challenge path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a checkpoint challenge when the message is printed then it states that a human decision is required and that the caller may re-run with the code once approval is given and the harness-loop skill documents presenting the command and obtaining approval before executing it

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/`
acceptance_criteria: Given a checkpoint challenge when the message is printed then it states that a human decision is required and that the caller may re-run with the code once approval is given and the harness-loop skill documents presenting the command and obtaining approval before executing it

title: Enqueue a decision item when a judged rubric check says no
description:
## Context

D4 as amended 2026-07-25 and roster R4: a judged NO must not fail the lane and must not be advisory. It routes a decision-queue item carrying the failing criterion and the validator's evidence and the lane holds - it neither lands nor bounces - until a human or the decider under an L2+ grant disposes of it. Today rubrics.gate_status ignores judged verdicts entirely (it fails only on deterministic checks) and loop._validate_lane just records the gate so a judged NO is silently discarded.

This is the producer side only. The rubric content half - every shipped rubric carrying at least one deterministic check plus the missing task and chore rubrics - is basicly-kjc5.19.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a lane whose judged rubric check answers no when the lane integrates then a decision-queue item is enqueued carrying the failing criterion and the evidence and the lane holds without landing or bouncing and the required gate is neither passed nor failed by the verdict

## Scope

- `src/basicly/rubrics.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a lane whose judged rubric check answers no when the lane integrates then a decision-queue item is enqueued carrying the failing criterion and the evidence and the lane holds without landing or bouncing and the required gate is neither passed nor failed by the verdict

title: Require acceptance criteria on every bead regardless of work type
description:
## Context

D4 makes validate a required gate and the shipped rubrics judge against the acceptance criteria recorded on the bead, so a bead with none cannot be meaningfully validated - the judged checks evaluate nothing and the gate reads green having proved nothing. That is the same hole basicly-kjc5.19 and basicly-kjc5.35 closed on the rubric side, reopened from the tracker side.

policy.definition_of_ready takes its missing-section list from br lint, and br lint decides required sections from the per-type template: a chore is never asked for acceptance criteria at all. So lint staying silent does not mean the criteria exist - it can mean the template never asked. Four open chores passed DoR carrying none.

DoR is basicly's own gate, so the requirement belongs there rather than in the tracker's templates: enforcing it in definition_of_ready makes it independent of the work type, of br's template config, and of whichever br version a consumer has installed. Satisfied by either the structured acceptance_criteria field or an Acceptance Criteria section in the description body - never by absence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a bead of any work type including chore when its acceptance criteria are absent from both the structured field and the description body then definition_of_ready reports the Acceptance Criteria section missing and blocks, and given either one present then it does not

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a bead of any work type including chore when its acceptance criteria are absent from both the structured field and the description body then definition_of_ready reports the Acceptance Criteria section missing and blocks, and given either one present then it does not

title: Express lane ownership in the assignee field so claim tooling works
description:
## Context

Audit 2026-07-25: assignee, owner, labels and estimate are unset on all 31 beads and the engine reads none of them. Most of that is correct - unused fields that read as meaningful are worse than absent ones - but assignee is load-bearing for tooling the harness already claims to rely on.

The engine expresses ownership only through the worktree binding on external_ref, which is a basicly-specific convention invisible to br's own surfaces. So br list --assignee cannot answer who is working what, and br scheduler --stale-claim-hours (default 2 hours), which the harness-loop guidance names as the backstop for cross-machine claim races, can never fire because no claim is ever expressed.

Set assignee when a lane is provisioned and clear it at teardown, using the resolved runner or role id as the value (the same identity already exported as BR_AGENT_NAME in runner.py). Keep it derived from engine state rather than agent-authored, so it stays a projection of the binding rather than a second source of truth. - Given a lane whose worktree is provisioned when the binding is recorded then the bead's assignee names the resolved runner or role and br list --assignee finds it, and given teardown then the assignee is cleared so a stale claim cannot outlive the lane

title: L3 ship delegation can never fire while the session root is open
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-25 while trying to use the autonomy ladder for a multi-lane run. policy.lights_out_violations requires every required gate green on the session ROOT issue, and an epic's verify gate is missing until the epic itself closes. So an L3 grant can never delegate a child's ship checkpoint during the session - every ship falls back to a human challenge, and L3 silently degrades to L2 for exactly the long multi-lane sessions it was written for.

The preconditions are right in spirit: zero rework escalations and zero needs-input events are genuinely session-wide. The root gate check is the part that cannot hold mid-session. Either scope it to the node being shipped plus its closed siblings, or state that L3 covers only the root's own ship and say so in D3 instead of implying per-child delegation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Issue an L3 grant on an open epic with a token budget.
2. Drive any child to its verify phase with all its gates green.
3. Approve the child's ship checkpoint non-interactively.
4. It is refused and falls back to a confirm-code challenge; lights_out_violations reports the root's verify gate as not green even though the child is fully green.

Expected: an L3 grant delegates the child's ship when the child's own preconditions hold, or D3 states plainly that L3 never covers a child's ship.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an L3 grant on an open session root when a child whose own gates are green and whose session has no escalations or needs-input events reaches ship then the approval is delegated without a human challenge, or D3 is amended to state that L3 does not cover a child ship and the code matches that wording

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `docs/factory-design.md`
acceptance_criteria: Given an L3 grant on an open session root when a child whose own gates are green and whose session has no escalations or needs-input events reaches ship then the approval is delegated without a human challenge, or D3 is amended to state that L3 does not cover a child ship and the code matches that wording

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-07-25: scope the lights-out gate check to the node being shipped, not the session root. The two session-wide preconditions (zero needs-input events, zero rework escalations on any session bead) stay session-wide, so any wrinkle anywhere still drops ship to a human per D3. Rejected alternative: amending D3 to say L3 never covers a child ship - that would make L3 equivalent to L2 for every epic-shaped session, which is exactly the case D3 was written for. The root-gate check was never a safety property: an epic's verify gate cannot exist until the epic closes, so it refused unconditionally.

title: Invoke the decider from the supervisor so autonomous mode is reachable
description:
## Context

D3 L2 and section 7.1 describe autonomous mode as the supervisor invoking the decider agent per delegable decision under the grant. In code decisions.invoke_decider has exactly one caller - the human-triggered basicly loop decide command - and supervise never calls it. A pending item simply holds the lane via decisions.has_pending, so an L2 grant delegates nothing and the autonomy ladder has no autonomous path at all.

Wire the supervisor to invoke the decider per pending delegable item when the active grant covers it, honoring decider_max_decisions, the corpus bound, the abstain-to-human path, and the reserved decider process slot. Depends in spirit on basicly-kjc5.23 (spend must be enforced at dispatch admission before more dispatch sites exist) and on basicly-kjc5.16 (the decider should be confined before it runs unattended).

title: Drive the whole loop ceremony from one command per phase boundary
description:
## Context

Zero-token principle (owner 2026-07-25): anything fully deterministic should be scripted and merely triggered by an agent. The loop ceremony violates it. Taking one leaf bead from intake to shipped currently needs about six agent-issued commands - loop advance --work-type, policy dor, policy checkpoint mint, policy checkpoint confirm, loop advance, then land and the same mint-confirm-advance again at ship. Every one is deterministic. During the 2026-07-25 autonomous run the driving agent wrote a throwaway shell wrapper mid-session purely to survive the repetition, which is the clearest possible signal the engine is missing the command.

loop run already advances until it blocks, but a checkpoint challenge stops it and cannot be answered from inside, so the agent must interleave policy checkpoint calls by hand. Give the engine one command per phase boundary: take a bead from intake to awaiting-the-agents-work, and from committed to shipped, resolving the checkpoints it is authorized to resolve and blocking clearly on the ones it is not. The authorization question is separate and already tracked - a grant covers it when the ceiling permits, otherwise the command surfaces the challenge once rather than per checkpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a ready leaf bead when one command is invoked then the engine advances it to the point where agent work is required resolving every checkpoint it is authorized to resolve, and given committed work when the shipping command is invoked then it lands verifies and closes the track without further agent-issued commands

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a ready leaf bead when one command is invoked then the engine advances it to the point where agent work is required resolving every checkpoint it is authorized to resolve, and given committed work when the shipping command is invoked then it lands verifies and closes the track without further agent-issued commands

description:

Only the description needs judgment. Today the agent composes the whole message and the commit-msg hook rejects it on envelope errors - a capital letter in the description cost a round trip during the 2026-07-25 run, and the repo keeps a skill plus a memory note to help agents avoid the same class of rejection.

title: Replace metaphor-domain terms with their engineering equivalents
description:
## Context

Review 2026-07-25. Terminology acts as a retrieval key for a model: a precise domain term co-occurs in training data with the correct procedures and failure modes, while a metaphor term retrieves the metaphor's domain. Most of this repo's vocabulary is already strong - worktree, merge queue, idempotent, topological order, dispatch, bounded rework, and the IEEE-style verify versus validate split that D4 rests on. Four terms borrow from the wrong domain and have exact equivalents.

persona is marketing and UX language for what RBAC calls a role, and the engine already keys on a role id while R2 makes names display-only, so the change is nearly free. roster is HR language while section 8 of the roster design already calls the same thing a role registry - the document contradicts itself. quirks is informal for what R8 then spends a paragraph redefining as operational contracts, so it should simply say invariants or contracts. Conductor is musical for what the code calls supervise.

Keep rubric, which is the correct term in the LLM-evaluation literature, and Definition of Ready, which is the industry-standard name despite its Scrum origin. Note in passing that factory collides with the Factory design pattern, though software factory is an established organizational term - out of scope for this bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the design docs and the engine when the terminology pass lands then persona reads as role and roster as registry and quirks as contracts or invariants and Conductor as scheduler or supervisor consistently across prose and code identifiers, with no behavior change and the projection gates green

## Scope

- `docs/agent-roster-design.md`
- `docs/factory-design.md`
acceptance_criteria: Given the design docs and the engine when the terminology pass lands then persona reads as role and roster as registry and quirks as contracts or invariants and Conductor as scheduler or supervisor consistently across prose and code identifiers, with no behavior change and the projection gates green

title: Measure whether domain-precise wording changes agent behavior
description:
## Context

Owner hypothesis 2026-07-25: using correct software-engineering language rather than business or marketing language helps a model reach the knowledge it needs, and so produces better results. The mechanism is well-supported - terminology is a retrieval cue - but the magnitude in this repo is unmeasured, and it should not become an authoring rule on the strength of an argument. If it holds it applies to every skill, fragment, prompt and doc in the project, which makes it worth a number rather than a belief.

The instrument already exists. basicly-4t9z runs trigger-accuracy and behavioral-lift evals per skill against a task set with hidden objective checks. Add a paired-phrasing case: the same skill expressed once in domain-precise engineering terms and once in metaphor or business terms, everything else held constant, scored on the same hidden checks. Relates to basicly-7bur for the cost-per-landed-package unit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given one skill authored in two phrasings that differ only in domain vocabulary when the eval runs both against the same task set and hidden checks then it reports the difference in trigger accuracy and behavioral lift with enough runs to distinguish the arms from noise, and the finding is recorded as an authoring rule or explicitly refuted

## Scope

- `tests/`

title: Label beads with the derived facets that are otherwise unqueryable
description:
## Context

Field-usability review 2026-07-25. labels are unset on every bead and the engine reads none, but two derived facets are currently invisible to any br query and would be genuinely useful to slice a ready set by.

The first is the D8 scope group. Decompose computes scope disjointness to decide what can run in parallel, and that grouping exists only inside the computation - a human or a second session cannot ask which beads share a scope group, which is exactly the question when a landing bounces on a missed coupling. The second is provenance: whether a bead was planned, filed by a retro, or derived from a found-info record. Both are engine-derived, so labelling them adds a queryable projection rather than a new authority.

Do not label the work class - issue_type already carries it. The governing constraint is that a label written by the engine must be a projection of engine state refreshed at a defined point, never hand-edited, or it becomes a stale second source of truth.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a decomposition when children are created then each carries a label naming its scope group and one naming its provenance, and br list with a label filter returns exactly the beads in that group with the labels refreshed rather than duplicated when the decomposition is re-run

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a decomposition when children are created then each carries a label naming its scope group and one naming its provenance, and br list with a label filter returns exactly the beads in that group with the labels refreshed rather than duplicated when the decomposition is re-run

title: Predict a beads wall-clock estimate from run-record duration telemetry
description:
## Context

Field-usability review 2026-07-25. The owner asked whether the beads estimate field should carry story points on a Fibonacci scale, with anything above 13 requiring further decomposition.

Rejected as an authored field, and the reasoning matters: D8 already decides whether a package is too big, deterministically - scope-glob tokenization times a telemetry-calibrated per-class build factor, governed against the working-set band, where above working_set_max the engine refuses and the agent must split. That is the same function the above-13 rule performs. An authored story point would put a second, non-deterministic number in charge of the same decision, which D9 forbids and R3.1 answers directly, and it would be the weaker of the two signals: consensus effort versus measured context cost.

The honest use of the field is a derived prediction. Run records now carry duration_s per dispatch, so a per-class median duration gives a wall-clock estimate in the minutes unit the field actually documents. That is useful to a factory that wants to forecast when a session completes, and it never competes with the sizing governor because it predicts time rather than gating size.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given enough run-record duration samples for a work class when a bead of that class is created or governed then its estimate field carries a derived wall-clock prediction in minutes, and the sizing decision continues to come from the working-set governor alone with no story-point input anywhere

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given enough run-record duration samples for a work class when a bead of that class is created or governed then a [harness-estimate] comment marker carries a derived wall-clock prediction in minutes rather than the br estimate field and the sizing decision continues to come from the working-set governor alone with no story-point input anywhere

title: Require proving a regression test red when it is written after the fix
description:
## Context

Session retro 2026-07-25. Two concurrency tests written for basicly-kjc5.17 passed with the fix removed - they proved nothing. One used an Event that returns immediately for the thread that set it, so the intended interleaving never happened; the other was accidentally serialized by the GIL because the fake tracker does no IO. Both were caught only because the agent chose to disable the lock and re-run, which nothing asked it to do.

The test-discipline skill says to add the regression test that would have caught the bug first, which assumes test-first ordering and prevents this. In practice a test is often written after the fix, and then passing is not evidence of anything. The missing rule is explicit: when a test is authored after the fix it claims to pin, prove it red against the pre-fix shape - revert the fix, watch it fail for the stated reason, restore. Add the concurrency corollary too, since it bit here: a test cannot prove mutual exclusion by racing, because forcing an interleaving inside the critical section is exactly what the lock prevents and a barrier there deadlocks - assert the contract instead, or use a timed handshake that discriminates in both worlds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the projected test-discipline guidance when an agent writes a test after the fix it pins then the prose requires demonstrating the test fails against the pre-fix shape and names the reason, and states how to test a mutual-exclusion invariant without a race, with the projection gates green

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/test-discipline/skill.yaml`
acceptance_criteria: Given the projected test-discipline guidance when an agent writes a test after the fix it pins then the prose requires demonstrating the test fails against the pre-fix shape and names the reason, and states how to test a mutual-exclusion invariant without a race, with the projection gates green

title: Record forecast and actual cost on the bead so history survives a clone
description:
## Context

Owner question 2026-07-25: build history so future work can be forecast in time, money and tokens. The blocker is not the forecasting - it is that the history is machine-local. run-records live in .basicly/usage/ which is self-ignored, so calibrated_build_factors reads samples that never leave the machine that produced them. A fresh clone or a new team member forecasts from the seed build factors, and two machines size the same plan differently. The tracker is committed, so the bead is the only carrier that survives a clone.

Write a cost projection onto the bead at ship: the forecast that was made and the actual that resulted, in tokens, cost and wall-clock, plus the dispatch and rework counts behind it. Keep the pair rather than the actual alone - forecast error per class is the learning signal, and D8 currently recomputes a median of raw actuals instead of correcting a biased estimator. The actual must aggregate every dispatch on the bead including failed attempts, or it understates exactly the packages whose cheap dispatch produced an expensive result. Money comes from the cost already captured per run at the price of the day; never recompute it later.

Engine-written at ship, never hand-edited: this is the bead as evidence, not as state, and nothing branches on it. Complements basicly-kjc5.48, which predicts the wall-clock figure; this bead is the ledger that makes such predictions improve and travel. Feeds basicly-7bur's cost-per-landed-package unit, which becomes computable from the tracker alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a shipped bead when the ship advance completes then the bead records the forecast and the actual tokens cost and wall-clock together with the dispatch and rework counts aggregated over every dispatch including failed attempts, and given a fresh clone with no local usage files then calibration and cost-per-landed-package are computable from the tracker alone

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`

title: Measure the human wait time that dominates a factorys wall clock
description:
## Context

Owner question 2026-07-25 about forecasting delivery time. duration_s measures dispatch time only. A factory's wall-clock is dominated by waiting on humans - checkpoint approvals and decision-queue items - and nothing records those intervals, so any delivery forecast built from current data predicts the compute and misses the bottleneck.

The data is already present: checkpoint and decision markers are br comments with timestamps, so the interval from enqueued to answered, and from a checkpoint being requested to being approved, is derivable without new state. Record it as evidence per bead and roll it up per session, distinguishing who answered - human or decider - because that distinction is what quantifies the value of an autonomy grant: the wait time it removes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a bead whose track waited on a checkpoint approval or a queued decision when it ships then the recorded evidence includes the wait interval per event and who answered it, and a session rollup reports total human wait time separately from dispatch time

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`

title: Fingerprint the environment behind a gate result so it is portable evidence
description:
## Context

D9 requires dispatch inputs to be reproducible and recorded, but says nothing about the deterministic side. A recorded verify gate currently means passed on some machine with some tool versions: the gate result carries pass or fail and a provider, not the verify mode, the check set that ran, or the versions of the tools that ran them. A teammate therefore cannot tell whether a green gate is comparable to their own, and on a machine with different tool versions the same green means something different.

Record the mode, the check names, and the resolved tool versions alongside the gate result, as the deterministic counterpart to the dispatch-input recording in basicly-kjc5.28. Evidence rather than state - nothing branches on it, so a missing fingerprint degrades the audit trail without blocking a track.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a recorded verify gate when it is inspected then it names the verify mode the checks that ran and the resolved version of each tool, and given two machines running the same mode then the fingerprints are comparable well enough to tell an environment difference from a code difference

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a recorded verify gate when it is inspected then it names the verify mode the checks that ran and the resolved version of each tool, and given two machines running the same mode then the fingerprints are comparable well enough to tell an environment difference from a code difference

title: Telemetry recording must never raise on a spec and result mismatch
description:
## Context

Regression from basicly-kjc5.28, caught by CI on all three runners 2026-07-25. runner.record_dispatch derives the redacted command with format_command whenever the result does not report a handoff, and format_command raises ValueError for a handoff-only spec that has no command. The call sits outside every exception guard, so a telemetry helper can abort a dispatch.

It passed locally because select_runner with default auto resolves to a headless CLI on a developer machine; CI has no agent CLI installed, so it resolves the manual handoff runner and the mismatch appears. The same crash is reachable from the loop and supervisor dispatch paths, not only from the rubric judge, so this is a robustness defect rather than a test artifact - telemetry must never fail a landing, which is the stance the surrounding suppress calls already take.

Guard the command derivation so a mismatch degrades to an empty command, and cover it with a test that passes a handoff spec together with an executed result.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Resolve the manual runner spec and build a RunResult with executed true and handoff false.
2. Call runner.record_dispatch with that spec and result.
3. It raises ValueError saying the runner is handoff not headless and has no command.

Expected: the record is written with an empty command and nothing is raised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dispatch whose resolved spec is a handoff runner while the result reports execution when the dispatch is recorded then no exception escapes and the record is written with an empty command

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a dispatch whose resolved spec is a handoff runner while the result reports execution when the dispatch is recorded then no exception escapes and the record is written with an empty command
close_reason: Fixed in d8f51db: command derivation guarded so a handoff spec paired with an executed result degrades to an empty command instead of raising; verified green on all three CI runners

title: Windows CI fails on POSIX-only os attributes in the kill-tree tests
description:
## Context

quality-gates has been red on main since 2225cfe (basicly-kjc5.15, 2026-07-24) - before the 2026-07-25 session, which did not cause it. Three tests fail on windows-latest with AttributeError: module os has no attribute getpgid, because monkeypatch.setattr requires the attribute to exist and os.getpgid is POSIX-only. pyright fails on the same reference.

The tests exercise the process-tree kill introduced by kjc5.15, which is deliberately platform-conditional. The fix is to make the POSIX branch's tests skip or patch tolerantly on Windows while keeping the coverage on POSIX, rather than weakening the kill path itself.

Note for whoever picks this up: main is red for this reason independently of any other work, so a green local verify does not mean a green CI. The repo's own os-matrix decision is why this is caught at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the suite on Windows, or inspect the quality-gates run for any commit at or after 2225cfe.
2. tests/test_runner.py fails three kill-tree tests with AttributeError on os.getpgid, and pyright reports the same missing attribute.

Expected: the suite and pyright pass on all three runners while the POSIX kill path stays covered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the Windows CI runner when the suite runs then no test monkeypatches a POSIX-only os attribute that is absent there and pyright reports no error for it, with the process-group kill path still covered on POSIX

## Scope

- `tests/test_runner.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given the Windows CI runner when the suite runs then no test monkeypatches a POSIX-only os attribute that is absent there and pyright reports no error for it, with the process-group kill path still covered on POSIX
close_reason: Fixed at the source: the hard-kill signal now has a portable module fallback and the tests assert against it; reproduced the exact CI error before fixing and verified with pyright resolving as Windows plus the kill-tree tests under a complete POSIX-name simulation

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
REOPENED 2026-07-25: the first fix was incomplete and Windows CI stayed red. It corrected the two symptoms I had reproduced (os.getpgid/os.killpg absent for monkeypatch, signal.SIGKILL as a static pyright error) but missed the runtime one, because my simulation deleted only the os attributes and not signal.SIGKILL - an incomplete simulation looks exactly like a passing check.

Actual root cause: src/basicly/runner.py:491 references signal.SIGKILL directly inside the POSIX branch. The tests fake os.name = posix, which drives runner into that branch on Windows, where the attribute does not exist. So the fix belongs in the source, not the test - a portable module constant like the existing CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP fallback - and the tests should assert against that same constant rather than defining their own, or the two disagree on Windows.

title: Make cross-platform and no-agent-CLI verification part of the gate
description:
## Context

Owner correction 2026-07-25: a fix or a check that lives outside the repo is not replicable or transferable, and must not be how correctness is established.

Two real defects this session were caught only by ad-hoc local shell incantations that nobody else will know to run. basicly-kjc5.53 - telemetry raising on a handoff spec paired with an executed result, reachable from the loop and supervisor dispatch paths - was invisible locally because a developer machine has an agent CLI on PATH and CI does not, so select_runner resolves differently there; it was found by re-running the suite with a stripped PATH. basicly-kjc5.54 - POSIX-only names in the kill-tree tests - was verified with pyright --pythonplatform Windows and by deleting os.getpgid and os.killpg in a throwaway interpreter, and that simulation is what revealed a second patch site the first attempt missed.

Both checks belong in the repo. Add them to the verify gate or as marked test configurations so they run for everyone: type resolution for every supported platform rather than only the host, and a dispatch path exercised with no agent CLI resolvable. The pattern to avoid is the one this bead exists to correct - proving something with a command only one machine ever ran.

Related: basicly-kjc5.41, where the same principle applies to the loop ceremony, since the previous session hand-rolled a shell wrapper outside the repo instead of the engine providing the command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the verify gate when it runs on any platform then it resolves types for every supported platform and exercises the dispatch path with no agent CLI resolvable, so a defect that only appears on another runner is caught before the push rather than by CI

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/`
acceptance_criteria: Given the verify gate when it runs on any platform then it resolves types for every supported platform and exercises the dispatch path with no agent CLI resolvable, so a defect that only appears on another runner is caught before the push rather than by CI

title: Score a known dependency defect as an unreliable gate without waiting for a re-run
description:
## Problem

basicly-55yh shipped the right idea and it does not cover the defect it was built for. When a landing gate fails, `verify.rerun_failures` re-runs exactly the failed checks in the same tree; if they pass the landing returns verify-unreliable and charges no rework (`loop.py:590` wires this into the single-track path, `merge.py` into the queue).

That detects a flake only if it fails to reproduce within seconds. The `br` clock defect is not a per-run coin flip: when the host clock has stepped backwards it stays stepped for a window, so the re-run reproduces and the failure is scored as a merit failure.

Measured on basicly-m4zv.9's landing 2026-07-27:

    unreliable events on m4zv.9 gate='merge':  0
    unreliable events on m4zv.9 gate='verify': 0
    rework verify: 1

Zero unreliable events with rework charged means the re-run reproduced. Contrast the kjc5.22 dogfood, where re-running gave 1 fail then 2 passes and the mitigation would have worked. So coverage is probabilistic against precisely the defect that motivated it.

The signature is unmistakable and cannot be produced by the work under test:

    Error: Validation failed: updated_at: cannot be before created_at

It can only come from `br`'s own validation, which rejects a write whose `updated_at` precedes its `created_at` when the machine's clock steps backwards. Root cause on this host: two time authorities correcting one clock - Hyper-V TimeSync IC 4.0 plus an active systemd-timesyncd.

Deliberately NOT fixed by stabilising the developer's clock. That is not committable, does not port to CI or the other platforms, hides the defect from consumers, and would remove the only reliable way to reproduce the condition while testing this fix.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a landing advance whose verify gate fails on the clock signature while the host clock is still stepped.
2. Observe the landing returns verify-failed and charges a rework attempt.
3. Observe `policy.unreliable_gate_events` records nothing, because `rerun_failures` reproduced the failure.

Observed: a dependency defect consumes the bounded rework budget.
Expected: the signature is recognised on the first failure and the gate is scored unreliable with no re-run needed.

## Notes

Complements basicly-vkh0.6 rather than duplicating it: vkh0.6 carries the clock error forward as a requirement with a regression test so the replacement cannot reintroduce it; this stops the harness paying for it in the months before cutover. Also independent of the clock specifically - the signature list is the mechanism, and a second entry can be added when another dependency defect is proved.

Keep the register narrow and evidenced. A signature earns its place only when it can be shown to be impossible for the work under test to cause, otherwise this becomes a way to launder real failures.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a landing whose verify gate fails with a known dependency-defect signature when the landing is scored then the gate is reported unreliable and no rework attempt is charged without needing the failure to fail to reproduce and the signature register is narrow enough that a failure the work under test could have caused is still scored as a merit failure with tests covering both directions
