title: A change to the landing logic cannot take effect on the landing that merges it
description:
## Problem

`basicly loop run` executes from the base checkout. Python imports `merge`/`verify`/`loop` from base's files at process start, then the landing merges the harness branch into base *during that same process*. Modules are never reloaded, so the landing is scored by the code as it was **before** the merge it just performed.

For most work this is invisible. For a change to the landing logic itself it is actively misleading: the fix looks broken on its own landing, and the run spends rework attempts proving it.

Observed on basicly-kjc5.56, which added signature-based unreliable-gate scoring. Commit timestamps on main:

    23:29:53  fix v1 merged  (singular-only signature register)
    23:30:14  merge commit
    23:34:20  attempt 2 process starts - imports base modules from disk
    23:34:26  fix v2 merged  (adds the plural br message shape)
    23:34:47  merge commit

Attempt 2 therefore ran v1's matcher against a message only v2 recognises, did not match, and escalated at rework 2/2. Base's code forgives that exact message when called afterwards, so the fix was correct the whole time. The bead spent its entire rework budget on the defect it fixes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Change the scoring logic in `merge._verify_for_landing` or `verify`.
2. Commit it on the harness branch and run `basicly loop run <id>`.
3. Observe the landing merges the change and then scores itself with the pre-merge code.

Observed: the new behaviour does not apply, and a failure it would have forgiven charges rework.
Expected: either the landing scores itself with the code it merged, or it says plainly that it did not.

## Notes

Not obviously worth making the engine re-exec itself - that is a real complexity cost for a narrow case, and re-exec mid-landing has its own failure modes. The cheap and honest option is to name it: when the merged diff touches the landing-scoring modules, print that the verdict was produced by the pre-merge code and that a re-run will use the new logic. Then nobody spends a rework budget rediscovering it.

Related: basicly-55yh (the re-run mitigation), basicly-kjc5.56 (the signature register), basicly-4tjt (clearing a rework counter after an escalation).

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a landing whose merged diff touches the modules that score a landing when the verdict is reported then the report states the verdict came from the pre-merge code and that a re-run applies the merged logic so no rework attempt is spent rediscovering it with a test covering a diff that touches those modules and one that does not

title: Declare a capability tier on a catalog entry instead of a model id
description:
## Context

Re-scoped 2026-07-29 after the owner picked the tier-table-as-catalog-data design. Supersedes
the earlier "declare a model per configured agent" framing, which put provider model ids in
config; the defect is that a model id is never portable across agent families.

Measured: `providers/github-copilot/models/claude-haiku-4.5.toml` on models.dev spells the
same model `claude-haiku-4.5` where Anthropic spells it `claude-haiku-4-5`. Hyphens on
Anthropic, dots on Copilot, and they coincide only on the `-5` generation. A one-character
divergence per entry, which is why a model id must never appear in a family-agnostic
catalog source.

This is already leaking: `.basicly/core/agents/test-runner/agent.yaml` declares
`model: haiku`, an Anthropic-only alias, and it lands verbatim in
`.claude/agents/test-runner.md` frontmatter while the copilot projection has no model field
to receive it at all.

The roster design already owns the portable vocabulary - four tiers low, medium, high,
maximum, with "the concrete model behind each tier is config (R2)". Reuse it; do not invent
a second vocabulary.

Scope: `.basicly/core/schemas/agent.schema.json`, `src/basicly/agents.py`,
`src/basicly/catalog_lint.py`, `.basicly/core/agents/test-runner/agent.yaml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a catalog source that declares a raw model id or alias when catalog lint runs then it
  fails naming the source and the tier field to use instead, and given a source that declares
  a tier when agents-build runs then the projected agent file carries no model line for any
  family, with tests
acceptance_criteria: Given a catalog source that declares a raw model id or alias when catalog lint runs then it fails naming the source and the tier field to use instead, and given a source that declares a tier when agents-build runs then the projected agent file carries no model line for any family, with tests

title: Refuse to dispatch an unresolved model and record the resolved value
description:
## Context

Re-scoped 2026-07-29 for the tier design. basicly-kjc5.58 gives catalog entries a tier;
basicly-kjc5.61 gives the engine a committed tier-to-model map. This is the resolution seam
that consumes both at spawn time - the mechanism that sets the model per coding agent
without any model id living in a projected agent file.

Resolution order, most specific first: an explicit `model` pin on `[[runner.agents]]`, then
a configured tier on that agent, then the tier the role or catalog entry declares, then the
family default tier, then refuse. Refusal names the agent and the config key rather than
dispatching an unpinned runner - the same stance `_apply_model` already takes when a model
placeholder has no model.

`model` is a declared field on all 122 run records in `.basicly/usage/run-records.json` and
null on all 122, because no built-in RunnerSpec pins one and `basicly.toml` declares no
`[[runner.agents]]` at all. The plumbing from spec to run record already exists
(`runner.py` writes `model=spec.model`); what is missing is a resolved value to put in it.
That null is why basicly-jr0l.21 has no key to calibrate a per-model forecast against.

Claude subagents need no per-file model: `agents.DEFAULT_MODEL` is `inherit` and the
frontmatter omits it, so a session model set here is inherited. Where a role's tier differs
from the session tier and the family has no per-agent model slot - copilot has none - fall
back to the session model and record that the tier was not honoured rather than implying it
was.

Scope: `src/basicly/runner.py`, `src/basicly/run_record.py`, `src/basicly/config.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a configured agent whose tier resolves to no model when a dispatch is attempted then
  the engine refuses with a message naming the agent and the config key and no agent process
  starts, and given a resolvable tier then the concrete model id and the tier it came from are
  both written to the run record, and given a role tier a family cannot express then the
  fallback to the session model is recorded rather than reported as honoured, with tests
acceptance_criteria: Given a configured agent whose tier resolves to no model when a dispatch is attempted then the engine refuses with a message naming the agent and the config key and no agent process starts, and given a resolvable tier then the pinned model id the tier it came from and the model the adapter reports it actually used are all written to the run record, and given the observed model differs from the pinned one then the mismatch is recorded rather than silently accepted, and given a role tier a family cannot express then the fallback to the session model is recorded rather than reported as honoured, with tests

comments.author: niksa

title: Generate the family model map from models dev with pinned provenance
description:
## Context

Filed 2026-07-29 as the generation half of the tier design. basicly-kjc5.58 makes catalog
sources declare a tier; this resolves a tier to the concrete per-family model id, from data
rather than by hand.

models.dev publishes a documented unauthenticated API (`https://models.dev/api.json`, plus
`models.json` and `catalog.json`) whose per-provider serving records carry `cost`
(input/output/cache) and `limit`, and - decisively - a `base_model` field linking a
provider's serving id to the underlying model. So four hand-authored anchors, one per tier,
resolve to every family's own spelling automatically.

Per-family serving data is not cosmetic: copilot serves `claude-haiku-4.5` at a 136000-token
input limit where Anthropic's `claude-haiku-4-5` is 200000, which the working-set band needs.

The confirmed anchors are low `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, medium
`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, high `anthropic/claude-opus-5` (the workhorse), maximum
`anthropic/claude-fable-5`.

Two hard constraints. The fetch runs at authoring and check time only, never in the dispatch
path, so no runtime network dependency is added and determinism holds. And because the
upstream is community-contributed, the generated map is committed and reviewed as a diff
while the drift check reports rather than auto-applies, so a bad upstream edit surfaces as a
failing check instead of silently changing dispatch behaviour.

Note medium reverts from 2 dollars/10 dollars to 3 dollars/15 dollars per MTok on
2026-09-01 when Sonnet 5 introductory pricing ends; the drift check is what catches it.

Scope: `.basicly/core/models/`, `.scripts/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the four tier anchors when the generator runs then it resolves each family serving id
  via base_model and writes a committed map carrying the model id input and output cost and
  input limit per family and tier, stamped with the upstream commit sha and the fetch date,
  and given a pinned id that no longer resolves upstream or whose cost moved when the drift
  check runs then it fails naming the id and the change without mutating the committed map,
  with tests
acceptance_criteria: Given the four tier anchors when the generator runs then it resolves each family serving id via base_model and writes a committed map carrying the model id input and output cost and input limit per family and tier, stamped with the upstream commit sha and the fetch date, and given a pinned id that no longer resolves upstream or whose cost moved when the drift check runs then it fails naming the id and the change without mutating the committed map, with tests

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (owner-driven, verified against live authoritative docs, not recall). This bead currently assumes models.dev alone can resolve a tier to a per-family model id. That is insufficient: the value you write to select a model differs by SURFACE, not just by family, and there are at least three spellings for one model. For claude-haiku-4.5 the three observed forms are: (1) Anthropic / Claude Code agent frontmatter - claude-haiku-4-5, hyphenated, or the short alias haiku; (2) GitHub Copilot and VS Code custom-agent frontmatter - the DISPLAY NAME with spaces dots and capitals, e.g. Claude Haiku 4.5; (3) models.dev provider serving id - claude-haiku-4.5. So the committed map must carry a per-surface spelling column, and models.dev covers only (3) plus the cost and limit data. Sources: VS Code custom agents doc states model accepts a single model name string or a prioritized list array, with the literal example model: ['Claude Opus 4.5', 'GPT-5.2'] - so copilot also supports an ORDERED FALLBACK LIST, which our schema has no way to express today and which is a genuinely useful reliability primitive for a tier. GitHub's supported-models reference page lists 29 models across 6 vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Moonshot AI, xAI) but publishes DISPLAY NAMES ONLY and gives no canonical config identifier list and no machine-readable endpoint, so the copilot spelling cannot be generated the way models.dev data can and needs a reviewed hand-maintained anchor set per tier with the drift check pinning it. Docs: docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models and docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-agents-configuration and code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/custom-agents

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: EMPIRICAL VALIDATION 2026-07-31, owner-suggested method, run live against copilot CLI 1.0.75. Method: write .github/agents/<name>.agent.md files declaring different model values, then ask the CLI to list agents (the command is /agent, singular - /agents is not it). Probed three values in one dispatch, deliberately including a known-bad one so a clean result could not be vacuous. Results: 'Claude Haiku 4.5' -> VALID, and the CLI named the canonical id as claude-haiku-4.5 WITH A DOT; 'claude-haiku-4-5' (the Anthropic hyphenated spelling) -> NOT a known id, flagged explicitly as needing a dot; 'Claude Haiku 9.9 Nonexistent' -> no such model. So copilot accepts BOTH the display name and the dotted id, and REJECTS the hyphenated Anthropic form. This is direct empirical confirmation of basicly-kjc5.58's founding premise and it agrees with models.dev, which also spells the copilot serving id claude-haiku-4.5. Consequence for this bead: the per-surface spelling column is required, and for copilot the dotted models.dev serving id is usable directly, so the copilot column CAN be generated from models.dev after all rather than hand-maintained - the display name is a second accepted alias, not the only accepted form. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the verdict above was produced by the model after it read the files with shell commands, not by a deterministic CLI validator, so under this repo's own rule (deterministic checks block, judged checks advise) this method ADVISES and must never be the sole gate. A deterministic equivalent still needs either a real validator flag or a machine-readable model list, and GitHub's supported-models page publishes display names only with no such endpoint. Cost of the probe: 24.3 AI credits, 80.6k input (49.9k cached, 28.2k cache-write) and 1.1k output including 404 reasoning tokens.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: PREMISE CORRECTION 2026-07-31 - measured against the live endpoint before implementing, and the bead's stated mechanism does not exist. This description says models.dev carries 'decisively - a base_model field linking a provider serving id to the underlying model'. It does not. Fetched https://models.dev/api.json (HTTP 200, 3331578 bytes, 176 providers, 5911 model records) and base_model is present on ZERO of 5911 records; it is not in the record schema at all. The actual per-record fields are attachment cost description family id knowledge last_updated limit modalities name open_weights reasoning reasoning_options release_date structured_output temperature tool_call. Either the field was removed since 2026-07-29 or it was never there. WHAT TO JOIN ON INSTEAD: 'name' is identical across providers for all four anchors, corroborated by 'family'. Measured: low anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 vs copilot claude-haiku-4.5 - ids DIFFER, family claude-haiku on both, name 'Claude Haiku 4.5 (latest)' on both; medium claude-sonnet-5 both; high claude-opus-5 both; maximum claude-fable-5 both. So join on exact 'name' (handling the '(latest)' suffix) with 'family' plus cost plus limit as corroboration, not on base_model. SECOND MEASURED FINDING that shrinks the work: only the LOW anchor's id actually diverges between anthropic and github-copilot - the other three are byte-identical, because only haiku carries a minor version and copilot spells a minor version with a dot where anthropic uses a hyphen. That is exactly basicly-kjc5.58's 'they coincide only on the -5 generation' claim, now measured. The map is therefore small today, but the mechanism is still required: the next model with a minor version diverges again. THIRD: the per-family serving limit the description predicted is real and only on the copilot side - github-copilot records carry limit.input (haiku-4.5 136000, opus-4.5 168000, opus-5 936000) which anthropic records do not, and note copilot claude-sonnet-5 has NO limit.input, so the generator must treat it as optional rather than assuming every copilot record has one.

title: Teach the wait-for-the-condition rule in the test-discipline skill
description:
## Context

Root cause of the only CI red this session (run 30168113819, macos-latest, three tests): the StallWatchdog tests asserted a timing outcome after a fixed time.sleep, so passing depended on how fast the host scheduled a background thread. Green on ubuntu and windows, red on macos. The failure did not reproduce locally even under twelve CPU spinners, so the constant could not have been tuned with any confidence - the shape of the test was wrong, not the number in it.

The test-discipline skill already carries two sections paid for by earlier sessions (Set up the condition the code actually reads, and A seam is not duplication). It has nothing about timing.

Proposed section, authored as a general rule with no Python or basicly specifics: 'Wait for the condition, not for a duration.' A test that sleeps then asserts encodes an assumption about host speed, and the assumption is invisible until the slowest runner in the matrix disagrees. Poll the condition with a generous timeout instead, so the test asserts what it means (the thing happened) rather than when it happened. Pair it with the prohibition's alternative: if the assertion really is about elapsed time, measure it with a monotonic clock and assert a bound, never a sleep-then-check. Include the corollary that a fixed sleep long enough for the slowest CI runner is far too slow for a laptop suite, so tuning the constant trades one failure mode for another.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the test-discipline skill when it is projected then it carries a section teaching wait-for-the-condition over fixed sleeps with the monotonic-bound alternative, authored as a general rule with no language-specific or repo-specific detail, and the catalog lint and skills-check gates pass

title: Warn that a relative core-hooksPath silently disables hooks in a worktree
description:
## Context

Session retro (basicly-kjc5.9). A commit run from a loop worktree with `git -c core.hooksPath=.git/hooks commit` passed with no hook output: a linked worktree has `.git` as a *file*, so the relative path resolves to a directory that does not exist and git skips every hook silently - pre-commit, commit-msg, and the beads gate all bypassed without a word. The next amend without the override caught a subject the gate rejects, proving the first commit had been ungated.

Root cause: nothing in the harness prose says the shared hooks dir is already wired by provisioning and must not be overridden. The worktree-isolation skill documents hook provisioning but not this failure mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the worktree-isolation skill when an agent commits from a loop worktree then the skill states that hooks are already wired to the shared dir and that overriding core.hooksPath there silently disables every gate with the projection gates green

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/worktree-isolation/**`
acceptance_criteria: Given a commit run from a linked worktree when the harness prose is projected then it states that provisioning already wires the shared hooks dir and that overriding it with a relative core-hooksPath resolves to nothing and silently skips every hook

title: Correct the superseded codex path-scoping rationale and the stale surface figures
description:
## Context

Raised by the owner 2026-07-31: they read that `AGENTS.md` is larger because everything must be
inlined for codex, and challenged it, citing OpenAI's official documentation for the view that codex
does not support commands / rules / instructions as separate files.

Verified against the live OpenAI docs (`learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*`) on 2026-07-31. **The projection's
behaviour is correct and needs no change. The docs describing why are wrong in two places, and the
owner was reading those.**

### What is actually true

Codex has **no glob- or pattern-based instruction scoping** — no `applyTo`, no `paths:` frontmatter,
no `globs` field, in `AGENTS.md` discovery, the config reference, `SKILL.md` frontmatter, or the
customization overview. Directory placement is the only scoping axis. Codex *does* support separate
instruction files (nested `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, `project_doc_fallback_filenames`),
repo-checked-in skills at `.agents/skills/`, project subagents at `.codex/agents/*.toml`, and project
sandbox rules at `.codex/rules/`. So the mechanism our inlining rests on is the **glob-vs-directory
type mismatch**, exactly as §7.4 says — not any absence of separate files.

### The defects to fix

1. **Two surviving lines assert the rationale that `2d04834` (basicly-joj, 2026-07-15) retired**, and
   they contradict `docs/architecture/architecture.md:653-666` in the same file:
   - `docs/architecture/architecture.md:496` — "inlines scoped fragments (codex can't path-scope)"
   - `docs/architecture/architecture.md:507` — "scoped fragments inlined because it has no
     path-scoping mechanism"
2. **A stronger justification is unrecorded.** Nested `AGENTS.md` is loaded only along the path from
   project root **down to the cwd** — "Codex stops searching once it reaches your current directory".
   A file at `src/foo/AGENTS.md` is therefore **not loaded at all** when codex runs from the repo
   root. Per-directory offload would not merely lose glob fidelity; in the normal case it would not
   load. This strengthens the `[Deferred]` §11.3 offload decision and should be recorded next to it.
   (Exception worth noting: codex code review on GitHub does walk changed files, so that surface
   behaves differently from the CLI.)
3. **Stale cap figure.** `architecture.md:625` says a "shared soft cap of 8,000 chars" and
   `.basicly/core/targets/codex.yaml:4` says "Higher than claude/copilot (8000)", but both YAMLs set
   **9000** (raised in `e70e4db`, basicly-c5to). Also stale in `docs/archive/foundry-spike.md:307,343`.
4. **Stale doc URLs.** `developers.openai.com/codex/*` now 308-redirects to `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*`
   and page paths moved (`/codex/guides/agents-md` -> `/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md`). Any
   citation of the old path still resolves but is stale. `project_doc_max_bytes` is still 32 KiB and
   is configurable.
5. **Corrected measurements** (the cap counts characters via `len(content)` at `cli.py:311-317`; the
   figures previously carried were bytes):

   | Surface | chars | cap | headroom |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `AGENTS.md` | 10775 | 12000 | 1225 |
   | `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | 7894 | 9000 | 1106 |
   | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | 8026 | 9000 | 974 |

   A scoped fragment costs **~1500 chars (measured 1462 and 1614)**, to `AGENTS.md` only — not the
   "~1600" carried before. So: **copilot is tightest by absolute headroom**; `AGENTS.md` is the
   binding constraint **for the path-scoped tier specifically**, and the **next** scoped fragment
   already overflows its cap (1225 < ~1500) rather than "two more" as previously recorded. Correct
   this wherever it appears, including `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:143`.
6. **Record the naming collision.** Codex's own "Rules" feature is a sandbox command-execution policy
   (`.codex/rules/`, Starlark `prefix_rule(pattern=...)`), unrelated to per-file instructions. Reading
   that page and concluding codex has no instruction rules is the exact trap the owner hit, so the
   distinction is worth one line wherever we describe the codex surface.
7. **Note that file-based custom prompts are deprecated** in favour of skills and are user-scope only
   (`~/.codex/prompts`), so they cannot ship in a repo — relevant if a codex command tier is ever
   proposed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `docs/architecture/architecture.md:496` and `:507`.
2. Read `:653-666` of the same file.
3. Observed: `:496`/`:507` say codex has no path-scoping mechanism, while `:653-666` documents that it
   does (root->leaf concat, nearest wins, `AGENTS.override.md`). The authoritative doc contradicts
   itself, and a reader acting on §4.4 reaches a conclusion the repo retired on 2026-07-15. Expected:
   one consistent rationale — the glob-vs-directory mismatch, plus the root->cwd loading limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the architecture doc and the catalog when the codex steering surface is described then the rationale is the glob-vs-directory mismatch plus the root-to-cwd loading limit with no surviving claim that codex cannot path-scope, the cap figure reads 9000 everywhere, the surface table gives characters not bytes with copilot as the tightest always-on surface, and the per-scoped-fragment cost reads about 1500 with the next fragment overflowing AGENTS.md

title: Guardrails: inject --deny-tool flags on the copilot runner (invocation-time deny)
description:
From basicly-u0zg.2 (closed infeasible). GitHub Copilot CLI has NO config-file deny mechanism (deny is --deny-tool CLI-flag-only, session-scoped, never persisted; permissions-config.json stores allows only; github/copilot-cli#2398 unshipped). So the baseline deny-list cannot be projected as managed catalog output for copilot. The only enforcement is invocation-time: extend the copilot runner command template to inject --deny-tool flags derived from permissions.yaml. Belongs at the runner seam (overlaps basicly-45ld). Render-testable via runner dry-run.

Verified 2026-07-18 against copilot CLI v1.0.70: --deny-tool[=tools...] takes copilot-native tool specs and matches shell commands by PREFIX, e.g. --deny-tool='shell(git push --force)' (does not block plain 'git push'); tool names like 'write'. No infix wildcards, so the fine-grained claude glob deny-list maps only PARTIALLY - a documented best-effort projection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- permissions.yaml deny rules gain an optional copilot field of copilot-native --deny-tool specs, authored only for rules copilot can meaningfully express (destructive-rm, force-push, bypass-gates, destructive-git); rules with no faithful copilot form (env-read/env-edit) are omitted with a comment.
- permissions.py exposes the flat de-duplicated copilot deny specs (mirroring claude_deny_patterns).
- The copilot runner command injects one --deny-tool=<spec> per spec, placed after the binary and before -p, populated from the repo permissions.yaml at runner-config load.
- runner dry-run --runner copilot renders the exact argv including the --deny-tool flags; a non-copilot runner is unchanged.
- The prefix-match limitation (variants/flag-reordering not all caught; env rules omitted) is documented where the mapping is authored.
- Deterministic tests cover the spec loader, format_command injection, and the dry-run surface.

title: Resolve a wrapped command past its flags so usage counts the real tool
description:
## Context

Found by the 2026-07-31 session retro while reading `basicly usage report`. The report's Terminal
tools table counts things that are not tools, which undermines its own stated purpose - the skill
uses it to name never-used catalog skills as culling candidates, so noise there can drive a real
culling decision.

**Not a heredoc bug.** `.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py` already tracks heredoc bodies and quote
state (basicly-zcvo). The heredoc-shaped entries (`def` 90, `assert` 83, `PYEOF` 33, `EOF` 28,
`return` 31) all carry `last used` dates of 2026-07-16/17 - they are pre-fix residue, and because
the counter file accumulates by design and is never reset, that residue never ages out.

The live defect is wrapper resolution. Measured on entries last used 2026-07-31 that are not on PATH:

- **Worktree names, 49 counts across 7 entries**: `basicly-kjc5-61` 36, `basicly-jr0l-37` 8,
  `basicly-sy8c` 3, `basicly-2rn9` 1, `basicly-qvd2` 1, `basicly-jr0l-38` 1, `basicly-jr0l-50` 1.
  These come from `uv run --directory <abs-path> <cmd>`: `uv` is in `WRAPPER_TOKENS`, so it unwraps,
  but the flag and its value are not skipped, so the path lands as the head instead of `<cmd>`.
- **`run` 64** - the `uv` subcommand itself surviving as a head rather than resolving to the command
  after it.
- **Shell keywords and functions**: `continue` 9, `break` 6, `write_src` 3 (a function defined and
  called in the same script).

So a session that runs its work through `uv run --directory <worktree>` - which is exactly what this
repo's own multi-lane pattern does - pollutes the table with one entry per worktree, and the real
tool it invoked is never credited.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run `uv run --directory /path/to/some-dir pytest -q` and then `basicly usage report`.
- Observed: the directory basename is counted as a terminal tool and `pytest` is not credited.
  Expected: `pytest` is credited and the path is not counted.
- Also run a script that defines and calls a shell function, and one containing `continue` or
  `break` inside a loop; observe each counted as a tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a shell command that wraps the real tool behind a wrapper token and its flags when the
  tool-usage hook records it then the credited head is the invoked tool rather than a flag value or
  the wrapper subcommand, and given a shell keyword or a function defined in the same command then it
  is not counted as a tool, with tests
acceptance_criteria: Given a shell command that wraps the real tool behind a wrapper token and its flags when the tool-usage hook records it then the credited head is the invoked tool rather than a flag value or the wrapper subcommand, and given a shell keyword or a function defined in the same command then it is not counted as a tool, with tests

title: Have verify produce a run artifact the evidence gate can point at
description:
## Context

Split out of basicly-m4zv.13 by owner decision 2026-07-31. That bead delivers the *mechanism*: a phase
may declare a required evidence artifact, and the advance is refused unless the declared path exists and
is non-empty (presence only — the engine never parses it).

It deliberately does not supply a producer, and today there is none. `verify.py` streams each check's
output straight to the terminal uncaptured (that is intentional, so a consumer sees tool output live),
and `rerun_failures(..., capture=True)` captures only on the failure re-run path. So on a **passing**
run nothing is written anywhere, and declaring an evidence artifact for the verify phase would refuse
every advance.

This bead gives verify something to point at, which is what lets this repo dogfood the gate by
declaring it in its own `basicly.toml`.

Design constraints inherited from m4zv.13:

- The engine gates on **presence only**; the producer owns the content. Do not add parsing.
- Live terminal output must not regress — a consumer watching a run still sees each tool's own output.
- Deterministic: no model involvement, no judged content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a passing verify run when it completes then a non-empty run artifact exists at a stable declared path and the live terminal output of each check is unchanged, so the evidence gate from basicly-m4zv.13 can be declared for the verify phase in this repo and passes

title: Release v0-6-0
description:
## Context

Cuts the first release since v0.5.1 (2026-07-20). 535 commits are unreleased - 42 feat and 39
fix - including the whole parallel factory: the supervisor, concurrent lanes, the merge queue,
the decision queue, L0-L3 autonomy grants with a spend ceiling, `basicly commit`,
`basicly release`, the invocation axis, the path-scoped rules tier, the recall eval and the
tracker usage ledger.

Version is 0.6.0: the owner ruled in basicly-m4zv.9 that requiring `invocation` on every skill
source is breaking, and a breaking change at 0.x is a minor bump. The tier work adds a second
breaking catalog-schema change by removing `model` from the agent schema.

Driven through the harness as a consumer would - `basicly loop` for the work,
`basicly release 0.6.0 --issue <this bead>` for the cut - so the release doubles as a dogfood
run. Awkwardness in the harness is a finding to file, never something to route around.

Two release-quality obligations that no gate covers:

- **The breaking-change audit.** Zero commits in the 535 carry a `!` marker or a
  BREAKING CHANGE footer, yet at least two breaking changes exist. The marker discipline did
  not hold, so grep cannot answer the question; the audit means reading the 42 feat and 39 fix
  subjects against the consumer-facing surfaces - catalog schema, projected output paths, CLI
  flags and their semantics, hook contracts, and `basicly.toml` keys.
- **Changelog curation.** `## [Unreleased]` holds exactly one entry against 81 feat and fix
  commits.

Also verify after tagging that the README roadmap's `✓ shipped` rows are true again - it
defines shipped as "running code in the current release", and about seven rows currently
describe code that exists only on main.

## Success Criteria

- Every blocking bead closed, the breaking-change audit written up with each break named or
  the audit recorded as finding none, `CHANGELOG.md` curated for v0.6.0, the annotated tag
  created by `basicly release`, both pushes done with explicit owner approval, and the GitHub
  release verified as published

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the blocking beads are closed and the changelog is curated when `basicly release
  0.6.0 --issue` this bead runs then it bumps the single-sourced version regenerates the
  version-stamped projections rewrites the pinned references creates the annotated tag and
  pushes nothing, and given the pushes are then approved and run then the GitHub release is
  published and `basicly status` on a fresh consumer clone reports the new version
acceptance_criteria: Given the blocking beads are closed and the changelog is curated when basicly release 0.6.0 --issue this bead runs then it bumps the single-sourced version regenerates the version-stamped projections rewrites the pinned references creates the annotated tag and pushes nothing, and given the pushes are then approved and run then the GitHub release is published and basicly status on a fresh consumer clone reports the new version

Release body is the 179-line curated section, not the commit dump - required fixing basicly-m3od.1 first. Fresh consumer install from the published tag reports engine 0.6.0 with no drift and hooks in sync. Roadmap shipped rows re-verified against the tagged CLI surface.

title: Release changelog strands curated notes under Unreleased and publishes a commit dump
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

`CHANGELOG.md` at `d5a3d61` carries 155 curated lines under `## [Unreleased]`. Run:

```sh
uv run basicly release 0.6.0 --issue basicly-m3od
```

Observed: `_insert_index` in `.scripts/generate_release_changelog.py` pins the new section

title: Declare the invocation axis on every catalog entry
description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2a. Prerequisite for 2b.

An entry is either model-invoked - keeps a description, is agent-reachable, pays permanent context load - or user-invoked - no description, zero context load, reachable only by a human. Declare which in the catalog source.

Two reasons it comes first. "Does it route correctly" is not a well-posed question until an entry knows whether anything can route to it. And it is an immediate win in its own right: every entry correctly reclassified as user-invoked stops paying context load forever.
acceptance_criteria: Given every catalog entry when the catalog is linted then each declares whether it is model-invoked or user-invoked and a user-invoked entry carries no description and contributes no context load and a missing declaration fails the lint

title: User-invoked skills fail to load on codex because they carry no description
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-29 by running a freshly installed codex CLI against this repo's own projected
skills. Codex refuses to load three of them:

    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-bat/SKILL.md: missing field `description`
    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-fzf/SKILL.md: missing field `description`
    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-git-delta/SKILL.md: missing field `description`

This is a regression inside the unreleased set, not a pre-existing wart. At v0.5.1
`tool-bat/SKILL.md` carried a description; on main it does not, because basicly-m4zv.1 makes
a user-invoked entry project no `description` line. Claude tolerates the omission - that
tolerance is what basicly-m4zv.7 had to fix when the generated marker leaked into the
description slot - but codex treats description as required and hard-errors, so the skill
simply does not exist for a codex consumer.

The design tension is real rather than a coding slip. The invocation axis says a user-invoked
entry carries no description because nothing can route to it, so a description is context
load bought for no reach. Codex's loader makes "user-invoked" unrepresentable: an entry either
carries a description or fails to load. This is the same shape as the model-id problem - a
portable catalog concept one family cannot express - and it wants the same kind of answer, a
per-family projection rule rather than a change to the portable concept.

Two candidate stances, to be decided in the work: project a description for user-invoked
entries on families whose loader requires one, or omit the entry entirely for those families
rather than emitting a file that cannot load. Silently shipping an unloadable file is the one
option to rule out.

Blocks the release: v0.6.0 would otherwise ship a change that removes three skills from every
codex consumer without saying so.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run any codex command in this repo, e.g. `codex exec --json -s read-only "reply with
  exactly: ok" < /dev/null`, and read stderr.
- Observed: three `failed to load skill ... missing field description` errors for the
  user-invoked skills tool-bat, tool-fzf and tool-git-delta.
- Compare `git show v0.5.1:.agents/skills/tool-bat/SKILL.md` (has a description) against the
  file on main (has none).
- Expected: every projected skill loads on every agent family the projection targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user-invoked catalog entry when it is projected for an agent family whose loader
  requires a description then the emitted file loads without error on that family, and given
  the family cannot represent a user-invoked entry at all then no file is emitted for it
  rather than an unloadable one, and a check fails when a projected skill would not load,
  with tests
acceptance_criteria: Given a user-invoked catalog entry when it is projected for an agent family whose loader requires a description then the emitted file loads without error on that family, and given the family cannot represent a user-invoked entry at all then no file is emitted for it rather than an unloadable one, and a check fails when a projected skill would not load, with tests

title: No local gate catches a stale projection so the commit-time claim is overstated
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-30 while verifying a competitive claim from the `oh-my-agent` analysis
(`reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-agent.md`), and it turns out to be a hole in our own gate.

The repo's positioning - now in `README.md`, `site/index.html` and the GitHub About - claims
enforcement at **commit time** as the thing that distinguishes us from a projector whose drift
check is CI-only. On the specific axis of *projection staleness* that claim is currently false.

What actually runs locally:

- `protect-generated-commit` compares each **staged generated blob** against the hash in
  `generated-manifest.json`. Its docstring is precise about the case it covers: a hand-edit that
  skips the rebuild. It cannot see a stale projection, because a fragment edit does not stage the
  generated file at all - the output on disk still matches the manifest.
- `pre-commit-script` runs `[[verify.checks]]` mode `fast`: ruff, ruff-format, pyright, bandit,
  lint-imports.
- `pre-push-script` runs mode `full`: the above plus pytest.

`basicly check` appears in **none** of them. Nor do `skills-check`, `agents-check` or
`hooks-check`. They run in one CI job. `tests/test_docs_drift.py` is docs-to-code drift, not
projection drift, so pytest at pre-push does not cover it either.

So: edit a fragment, never rebuild, commit, push. Nothing local objects. The projection is stale
in the tree and on the remote until CI says so - which is exactly the posture we describe as the
competitor's weakness.

The fix is to add the four projection gates to the locally-run verify modes. They are the gates
`CLAUDE.md` already names as the projection gates, so this is wiring an existing check into the
stage that was supposed to run it, not new enforcement.

Open question this bead must settle rather than assume: whether they belong in `fast` (every
commit) or only `full` (pre-push). `fast` is the stronger guarantee and matches the published
claim; the cost is four extra subprocesses on every commit, and `skills-check
--all-default-roots` is the slowest of them. Measure before choosing, and if the answer is `full`,
then the published wording must say pre-push rather than commit time - correcting the claim is an
acceptable outcome of this bead, silently leaving it overstated is not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Edit any fragment body under `.basicly/core/fragments/`.
2. Do not run `basicly build`.
3. `git add` the fragment and commit, then push.
4. Observed: every hook passes; the generated instruction files are stale in the tree and on the
   remote, and only CI reports it. Expected: a local gate refuses the commit or the push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a fragment edited without a rebuild when the local git hooks run then a projection gate fails before the change can reach the remote, and the positioning wording in README site and repo About names the stage that actually enforces it
acceptance_criteria: Given a fragment edited without a rebuild when the local git hooks run then a projection gate fails before the change can reach the remote and the positioning wording in README site and repo About names the stage that actually enforces it

title: Refuse a catalog path that escapes the repo root when planning the projection
description:
## Context

Surfaced by the 2026-07-30 `oh-my-agent` analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-agent.md`) and
confirmed against our source and against pathlib's actual behaviour.

`planner.py` builds every projection output path by joining catalog-supplied strings onto the repo
root, with no containment check:

- `output_path=repo_root / output.path` (`src/basicly/planner.py:31`)
- `output_path = repo_root / output.path_template.format(fragment_id=fragment.id)`
  (`src/basicly/planner.py:39`)

Neither input is constrained. A schema audit found `pattern` on exactly two fields in the whole
catalog - `block.schema.json` `.properties.id` and `agent.schema.json` `.properties.name` - so a
fragment `id` and a target `path`/`path_template` are free-form strings.

Two distinct escapes, and the first is the nastier because it is silent:

1. **An absolute `path` replaces the root outright.** `Path('<redacted:posix-home-path>') / '/etc/passwd'` is
   `/etc/passwd` - pathlib discards the left operand. There is no traversal sequence to spot in a
   review; the string just looks like a path.
2. **A traversal sequence escapes upward.** `repo_root / '../../etc/passwd'` resolves outside the
   repo, and a `fragment_id` containing `../` reaches the same place through the `path_template`
   branch.

## Severity, stated honestly

**Not remote code execution and not a high-severity issue.** The inputs come from the catalog: our
own `.basicly/core/targets/` and the consumer's `.basicly-local/` overlay. Writing them is already
writing to the repo. So the realistic threat is a **third-party or copied overlay** a consumer
installs without auditing, and the realistic damage is `basicly build` writing a generated file
outside the repo - which is exactly the class of uninvited write `tracker_usage.is_enabled` was
already hardened against for a different reason.

It is worth fixing anyway on the repo's own rule - validate external input at trust boundaries -
and because the fix is small and the failure mode is silent. An overlay is a trust boundary the
moment it can come from somewhere else.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In `.basicly-local/`, declare a target output whose `path` is an absolute path outside the repo
   (or a `path_template` plus a fragment whose `id` contains `../`).
2. Run `basicly build`.
3. Observed: the projection writes outside the repo root, and the manifest records it. Expected:
   the build refuses the declaration and names the offending field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a catalog whose target output path is absolute or escapes the repo root, or a fragment id containing a path separator or traversal sequence, when the projection is planned then the build refuses with a diagnostic naming the field and the offending value, and every planned output path is asserted to resolve inside the repo root
acceptance_criteria: Given a catalog whose target output path is absolute or escapes the repo root or a fragment id containing a path separator or traversal sequence when the projection is planned then the build refuses with a diagnostic naming the field and the offending value and every planned output path is asserted to resolve inside the repo root

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: [harness-info] Review evidence 2026-07-30 at 2a0ba60: the escape is worse than filed - the write happens before any check would notice it. cli.py:304 write_if_changed(item.output_path) runs before the relative_to(repo_root) at cli.py:307 that would raise, so a hostile catalog gets one arbitrary file write per output before the crash. The refusal therefore belongs at plan time in planner.py (both join sites, planner.py:31 and :39), not in the render loop.

title: Require a declared evidence artifact before a phase can report success
description:
## Context

From the Archon analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/archon.md`). Its `evidence_policy.required`
plus typed node artifacts refuses terminal success unless a declared evidence file exists on disk -
the engine gating on **presence only**, the workflow producing the content. Their formulation is the
clearest statement of our own split: *"code computes, YAML coordinates"* (`schemas/workflow.ts:105`).

This plugs a hole we have. A lane can reach ship having recorded a passing verify gate with nothing
to point at: the gate records a status, not an artifact. When a landing is later questioned - a
forecast miss, a coupling dispute, a rework argument - the evidence is whatever happened to be
committed, which is exactly the situation the `[harness-*]` marker families were introduced to fix
for cost and decisions but never for verification output.

Presence-only is the important constraint and the reason this is cheap: the engine must not parse or
judge the artifact, only assert it exists and is non-empty, so it adds no nondeterminism and needs no
schema per artifact type. That keeps it on the deterministic side of the rubric contract.

Note the accompanying reject, worth recording next to it: Archon's own completion gate is
`completionDetected = signalDetected || bashComplete` (`dag-executor.ts:4602`), which lets a model's
self-emitted `<promise>DONE</promise>` short-circuit the deterministic check entirely. Adopt the
evidence requirement; reject the disjunction.

Open question this bead must settle: which phases owe an artifact, and whether a missing one blocks
or is recorded. Blocking every phase is likely too strict at first; verify is the phase where the
argument is strongest, because a verify gate with no output is the case that has actually caused
disputes here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a phase that declares a required evidence artifact when the loop attempts to advance past it then the advance is refused unless the declared path exists and is non-empty, the engine never parses or judges the content, and the artifact path is recorded on the bead
acceptance_criteria: Given a phase that declares a required evidence artifact when the loop attempts to advance past it then the advance is refused unless the declared path exists and is non-empty the engine never parses or judges the content and the artifact path is recorded on the bead

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-07-31 — the open question is settled: **opt-in declaration, blocking where declared.**

- A phase may *declare* a required evidence artifact path. When one is declared, the advance past that
  phase is refused unless the path exists and is non-empty. Presence only — the engine never parses or
  judges the content, so it stays on the deterministic side of the rubric contract.
- Nothing is declared by default, so there is zero behaviour change for existing consumers and the
  change is reversible. Blocking every phase was rejected as too strict; record-only was rejected as
  toothless (it reduces to a log line and would not have prevented the disputes this bead was filed
  about).
- The artifact path is recorded on the bead.

Scope boundary found while deciding: `verify.py` streams check output straight to the terminal and
captures nothing on a passing run, so **no artifact file exists for verify today**. Declaring one
therefore needs a producer. That is deliberately NOT in this bead — it is filed separately, so this
bead delivers the mechanism only and cannot destabilise the landing path before the u6jq.1 proof run.

Archon's own completion gate (`completionDetected = signalDetected || bashComplete`) stays rejected:
adopt the evidence requirement, never the disjunction that lets a self-emitted signal short-circuit it.

title: Stop the machine-global beads write lock making gates flaky and burning rework
description:
## Context

Two transient gate failures in one session (2026-07-30), both from the same cause, both passing on
a plain re-run with no code change:

1. The `basicly-imnu.12` landing merged the worktree and then failed `verify` on `pytest`, recording
   rework 1/2. Re-ran the suite twice by hand - serially and with `-n 4`, the form the gate uses -
   and got **1557 passed both times**. Recovered with `basicly verify --mode full --issue` from
   base, which re-recorded the gate green.
2. `git push origin main` was rejected by the `pre-push` hook. The identical command succeeded on
   the immediate retry with `pre-push-script ... Passed`.

`basicly.toml` already documents the mechanism on the `pytest` check: every `br init` takes a
**machine-global** write lock at `~/.beads/.write.lock` with a 30s timeout, so xdist worker count is
contention on one lock rather than parallelism, and `basicly-9s59` capped workers at 4 for exactly
this reason. Two failures in one session says the cap reduced the rate without removing the cause -
which is expected, because the lock is global to the machine and this session was also running `br`
commands continuously outside pytest (tracker commits, gate records, comment writes). The
contention is not just between workers; it is between the suite and whatever else is driving the
harness.

Why this matters more than an occasional retry: a transient failure inside a *landing* is not free.
It consumes a rework attempt against a cap of 2, and `basicly-55yh`'s re-run test only forgives a
failure that does not reproduce - so a second unlucky landing on the same node escalates to a human
for a defect that does not exist. That is the same class of waste `basicly-kjc5.56` addressed for the
clock defect, and the same argument applies: a gate that fails for reasons the work did not cause
corrupts the merit signal.

This is also a **requirement on the replacement tracker**, and belongs alongside the six already in
`docs/design/work-tracker.md` §2.1: a machine-global write lock is a scaling defect we inherited, and
an in-process store with a per-repo writer would not have it. Consider whether it becomes R7.

Options to weigh, not a chosen design:

- Serialise the tests that call `br init` into one xdist group (`--dist loadgroup`) rather than
  capping global worker count, so the rest of the suite keeps its parallelism.
- Give the test fixtures a private `BEADS_DIR`/`HOME` per worker so they never touch the global lock.
  This is the fix that removes the cause rather than reducing its rate, if br honours it.
- Widen the `pre-push`/landing retry: distinguish a lock timeout from a real failure by signature and
  do not charge rework for it - the register in `verify.py` already exists for exactly this shape.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drive a harness loop landing while other `br` commands run against the same machine.
2. Observed: the landing's `pytest` gate fails, rework increments, and the suite passes on a manual
   re-run with no change. Same for a `pre-push` rejection that succeeds on retry.
3. Expected: a lock-contention timeout is either prevented, or recognised and not charged as a
   merit failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the test suite running concurrently with other br activity on the same machine when the pytest gate runs then no test fails on the machine-global beads write lock, or such a failure is recognised by signature and does not consume a rework attempt, and the cause is recorded as a requirement on the replacement tracker
acceptance_criteria: Given the test suite running concurrently with other br activity on the same machine when the pytest gate runs then no test fails on the machine-global beads write lock or such a failure is recognised by signature and does not consume a rework attempt and the cause is recorded as a requirement on the replacement tracker

title: Gate catalog routing with stemmed tf-idf rank-1 evals
description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2b. Depends on 2a. Architecture §14.4 calls the routing tier the highest-value single deliverable and the thing nobody else in the field has.

Stemmed TF-IDF over descriptions, pure Python, no new dependency. Verified absent 2026-07-26 at c175c1a - no tf-idf, tfidf, stemmer or porter anywhere in src/.

Three assertions:
- a positive prompt ranks its owner in the top-k;
- a negative prompt declares an owner and the assertion is that the owner outranks this entry - a bare "must not rank first" passes vacuously when the prompt matches nothing;
- no two descriptions exceed a pairwise similarity ceiling - error at 75 percent, warn at 50.

The CI metric is rank-1 rate, with the floor set below a measured baseline, raised as routing improves, and never lowered to make a regression pass - lowering it is deleting the test while looking like maintenance. The floor value is plan §7.5, an owner decision after the baseline is measured, and is deliberately not guessable.

Refuse embeddings: they would make this semantic and therefore non-deterministic, network-dependent and unownable. Semantics are the Tier 3 job.
acceptance_criteria: Given the projected catalog when the routing eval runs in CI then a positive prompt ranks its owner in the top-k and a negative prompt owner outranks the entry under test and no description pair exceeds 75 percent pairwise similarity with a warning at 50 and the rank-1 rate is reported against a floor that the gate refuses to lower

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: [harness-info] Design input from the 2026-07-30 oh-my-agent analysis (reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-agent.md). oma skills audit is a dependency-free TF-IDF/cosine analysis over skill DESCRIPTIONS that flags near-duplicate pairs, black-hole skills whose mean similarity to the whole library is a statistical outlier, and sprawl by reference-doc count (cli/commands/skills/audit.ts:9-36; cli/utils/text-similarity.ts:105-129). Relevant because our routing rests entirely on 33 descriptions and we currently have NO cross-skill check of any kind - every catalog lint skill rule inspects one file in isolation (src/basicly/catalog_lint.py:219-292). So this bead's rank-1 eval should be paired with a pairwise-similarity check: a rank-1 failure tells you routing missed, while a near-duplicate pair tells you WHY, and the second is cheaper to compute than the first.

title: Require an eval case file per catalog entry as a tier-1 failure
description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2c. Depends on 2b.

An eval case file per entry, colocated with the catalog source so a reviewer sees the entry and its evidence in one diff, enforced as a Tier-1 failure from the start.

Surface measured 2026-07-26 at c175c1a: 19 fragments (16 core plus 3 overlay) and 28 projected skills = 47 projected entries, from 32 skill sources. Derive the enforced set at build time rather than hard-coding the plan §2 figure of 48, or the gate goes stale the first time an entry is added.

Stage it rather than attempting one pass, and scaffold from catalog new. Plan §8 names the failure mode: coverage stalls partway and the gate is quietly relaxed. Stage by adding entries to the enforced set, never by lowering a threshold.

Accept the consequence deliberately: this raises the cost of adding a catalog entry, which is the intended brake on accretion.
acceptance_criteria: Given the catalog entry set derived at build time when an entry has no colocated eval case file then the catalog gate fails as a tier-1 failure and catalog new scaffolds the case file so coverage can only grow by adding entries to the enforced set and never by lowering a threshold

title: Require a severity on judged output and refuse a pre-judging reviewer bundle
description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2d. Gates Phase 5.

Two deterministic checks, both currently absent - verified 2026-07-26 at c175c1a, severity appears nowhere in src/.

Severity as a required field on judged output - BLOCKER, IMPORTANT, MINOR - rejected as a schema violation rather than complained about. A judged verdict with no severity cannot pass a required gate.

Plus the no-pre-judging lint. Because dispatch prompts are assembled by code, the engine can refuse to emit a reviewer bundle containing a finding-suppressing directive. A rule an observer can mechanically check beats ten rules of good intent.

Note the plan lists a D4 prerequisite here. It is already satisfied: factory-design.md §D4 carries the 2026-07-25 amendment and loop.py implements it, so build against the shipped shape.
acceptance_criteria: Given a judged verdict with no severity of BLOCKER or IMPORTANT or MINOR when it is recorded then it is rejected as a schema violation rather than complained about and given an assembled reviewer bundle containing a finding-suppressing directive then the engine refuses to emit it

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
[harness-info] Owner decision, 2026-07-26. Gated on basicly-imnu.1 (the D4 amendment) by explicit ruling.

Plan section 4 Phase 2 states the prerequisite - build 2d and 2e against the amended shape, not the current one - but the decomposition wired imnu.1 to m4zv.6 only, leaving this bead unblocked. Ruled: imnu.1 lands first.

Why it matters here specifically. Severity is BLOCKER, IMPORTANT, MINOR on judged output, and what a BLOCKER *does* is exactly what D4 defines: whether the judged half of validate fails the lane or enqueues a decision. Building severity against the un-amended shape risks making a judged verdict fail a required gate directly, which contradicts the invariant that no persona passes or fails a required gate.

m4zv.5 was deliberately left unblocked - comparing open-finding sets between iterations does not depend on the composite gate shape.

title: Detect a non-converging rework loop from the open-finding set
description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2e first half. Gates Phase 5.

Compare the open-finding set between consecutive iterations, not the count - a round that fixes one finding and introduces one is not progress. Verified 2026-07-26 at c175c1a: policy.py has no convergence check at all. runner.StallWatchdog exists but is dispatch-level (no file activity for n seconds), a different mechanism entirely.

Escalation shape:
- one stalled round warns on the bead;
- two consecutive stalled rounds escalate immediately without consuming the remaining cap;
- a diverging round escalates on first occurrence.

Coupling to Phase 0. This rewrites the same rework accounting that 4tjt (clear the counter on an answered retry) and 55yh (do not charge an infrastructure failure) change. Both must land first or the three will collide in policy.py.
acceptance_criteria: Given consecutive rework iterations when the open-finding set is unchanged once then the bead is warned and when it is unchanged twice consecutively then the node escalates immediately without consuming the remaining cap and when the set grows then it escalates on first occurrence with tests

title: Classify every gate by type and forbid a pre-flight gate from writing state
description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 2 item 2e second half, split out from the convergence detector because it touches every gate call site, gates nothing downstream on its own, and is the piece the D4 composite-gate typing feeds.

Classify every existing gate into the four types - pre-flight, revision, escalation, abort - so "what happens when this fails" is answered by the type rather than per call site.

Then enforce the rule that a pre-flight gate writes nothing. The plan records why this earns its own enforcement: our two worst recorded incidents were both checks that recorded state where they should have blocked entry. See the loop-verify-gate-strands-merge and loop-ship-approve-wedges-phase histories.

Depends on the Phase 3 bead that records validate as a composite of a pre-flight and an escalation component, since that is the first gate to be typed and its typing sets the pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Given every gate in the engine when it is recorded then it declares one of pre-flight or revision or escalation or abort and given a gate typed pre-flight when it runs then it writes no state and a test proves the write is refused

title: Stop the generated marker filling a user-invoked entry description slot
description:
## Problem

Found immediately after basicly-m4zv.1 landed, by observing the effect in a live session rather than in a test.

basicly-m4zv.1 makes a user-invoked entry project no `description:` line. The intent is that the entry stops paying context load for reach it does not have. But the host does not simply omit a description - it falls back to the **first body line**, and our first body line is the generated-drift marker. So the three projected user-invoked skills are now advertised as:

    tool-bat: <!-- Generated by `basicly skills-build` from skill.yaml. Do not edit; edit the source. -->

Observed directly: the available-skills list in a session rooted at this repo showed exactly that for tool-bat, tool-fzf and tool-git-delta.

Two consequences.

The saving is about a third of what was claimed. The marker is 91 chars and is emitted per entry, so removing 430 chars of descriptions bought back 3 x 91 = 273, for a net 157 chars rather than 430. catalog-efficacy-design section 3-5 records 430 and about 107 tokens and is therefore wrong; correcting it is part of this bead.

The advertised string is now useless rather than merely cheaper. A description at least told the agent when to route; the marker tells it nothing while still costing tokens. That is a worse trade per character than what it replaced.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Project a user-invoked skill (`basicly skills-build --all-default-roots`).
2. Read `.claude/skills/tool-bat/SKILL.md` - frontmatter is name only, then the marker line.
3. Open a session rooted at the repo and inspect the advertised skill list.

Observed: the marker text occupies the description slot.
Expected: a user-invoked entry advertises no description text at all, or at worst its own short heading.

## Notes

The obvious fix is to move the marker for a user-invoked entry so it is not the first line after the frontmatter - a YAML comment inside the frontmatter block is one option and keeps the drift marker present. Whatever is chosen must keep `check_synced_skills` drift detection working and must not change the byte-for-byte fidelity contract for model-invoked entries, which the existing test asserts.

Re-measure after the fix and correct the figure in the design doc rather than restating the old one.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/skills.py`
- `tests/test_skills.py`
- `docs/design/catalog-efficacy-design.md`
acceptance_criteria: Given a user-invoked skill when it is projected then no generated-marker text occupies the advertised description slot and drift detection still reports a hand-edited projection and the byte-for-byte frontmatter of a model-invoked entry is unchanged and the design doc records the re-measured saving rather than the superseded 430 char figure

title: Apply the two measurement-discipline retro findings from 2026-07-26
description:
## Context

Retro findings from the 2026-07-26 session, approved by the owner. Both are about measurement discipline and both come from real incidents in that session, not from general caution.

### A. An elicitation prompt must not name the entity under test

While probing whether a description-less skill still loads, the prompt said "if a skill named probe-hidden is available to you, include it". The skill appeared - which proved nothing, because the prompt had supplied the answer. Caught and re-run neutrally; the result happened to hold, but the first run was worthless and read as a confirmation.

`catalog-efficacy-design.md` §4.3 already enumerates isolation requirements for Tier-3 arms and exists for exactly this class of bug (the ponytail SessionStart contamination). Add the rule to that requirements list.

### B. Verify what the agent is told, not the file you edited

basicly-m4zv.1 measured "430 chars of descriptions removed" from the source, wrote that figure into `catalog-efficacy-design.md` §3.5, and committed. The delivered saving was 157 chars, because the host fills an absent skill `description` from the first body line - which is our generated drift marker. The error surfaced only when the change appeared in the authoring sessions own skill list, by accident, after the commit. Tracked as basicly-m4zv.7.

The `quality-gate` fragment already says to exercise the change as it will really be used and read the output. The gap is narrower than that: for a guidance change the projected file is not the delivered artifact, because the host may substitute or fall back.

Put this on the `catalog-authoring` skill rather than the always-on baseline. It fires exactly when catalog sources are edited, which is when it applies, and it costs no always-on context - the recall measurement under basicly-agzx.1 removed the argument that the baseline is too dense to attend to, but not the argument that every always-on word is billed per turn to every consumer.

## Notes

Per the ceremony threshold the owner chose this session (by touched path), finding B touches `.basicly/**` so this goes through the loop; finding A alone would have qualified for the lightweight path.

## Scope

- `docs/design/catalog-efficacy-design.md`
- `.basicly/core/skills/catalog-authoring/skill.yaml`
acceptance_criteria: Given the Tier-3 isolation requirements when they are read then they forbid naming the entity under test in an elicitation prompt and given the catalog-authoring skill when it is read then it requires verifying a guidance change against what the agent is actually told rather than the projected file naming the description fallback as the concrete case

title: Decide whether invocation should be optional with a default for consumers
description:
## Context

Raised 2026-07-26 while assessing release readiness. Not yet decided.

basicly-m4zv.1 made `invocation` a **required** field on every skill source. Verified by building a throwaway consumer catalog with one hand-authored skill and running the lint:

    .basicly/core/skills/mine/skill.yaml: invocation is a required property

So every consumer who authors their own skills gets a red `catalog lint` on upgrade, with no migration command and nothing explaining why. At 0.x that makes the next release a minor bump rather than a patch, and it puts a migration burden on every install.

## The question

Should an absent `invocation` default to `model` and emit a projection warning, instead of failing the lint?

Arguments for defaulting:
- The breaking change disappears. Consumers upgrade clean; our own catalog still declares the axis explicitly on every entry, so nothing is lost here.
- `model` is the safe default and the same one the scaffold uses, for the same reason: over-declaring `model` only wastes a description, while over-declaring `user` silently removes an entry from the agent reach.
- For a distribution whose value is being installed by other repos, a hard lint failure on upgrade is a bad trade for a field the consumer has never heard of.
- The lint can harden to required in a later version once consumers have had a release to adopt it.

Arguments for keeping it required:
- A warning that nobody reads is how an unmeasured entry keeps paying context load forever, which is the exact waste the axis was introduced to find. A default means most consumer entries stay `model` by inertia.
- The plan calls 2a an immediate win; a default makes the win opt-in rather than forced.
- basicly-m4zv-2 (Tier-2 routing evals) is built on the axis being reliably declared, and a defaulted field is weaker evidence than a declared one.

## Also part of release prep, and not yet done

Nothing has audited the other commits since v0-5-1 for consumer-breaking changes. The invocation axis was found only because it was built this session; 488 commits have landed since the tag and a release must check them properly rather than assume this was the only one.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/schemas/skill.schema.json`
- `src/basicly/skills.py`
- `src/basicly/catalog_lint.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given the owner has ruled on whether invocation defaults to model for a consumer when the decision is recorded then the schema and lint match the ruling and a consumer catalog with no invocation field either upgrades clean with a warning or is documented as a required migration in the changelog before the next tag

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
OWNER RULING 2026-07-27: keep invocation REQUIRED. No default, no deprecation window. Document it as a breaking change in the release changelog and ship it.

Rationale (owner): there are no or very few consumers today, so the goodwill cost of a hard break is near zero now and rises with every release. Better to fix a critical thing at the start of implementation than to carry backwards compatibility forward. This rejects options A (default to model), C (migration command) and D (default now harden later).

Consequences accepted:
- Every consumer with a hand-authored skill gets a red catalog lint on upgrade. The break is total, not partial: the field is schema-required and skills.py hard-errors on it.
- v0.6.0 release notes must carry a Migration section. That is now a release blocker, not a nicety.
- No basicly catalog migrate command will be built.

Work this ruling implies, verified by probe rather than assumed:
1. The missing-field message is a raw jsonschema string - '.basicly/core/skills/mine/skill.yaml: invocation is a required property' - reproduced 2026-07-27 against a throwaway consumer catalog holding one pre-m4zv.1 skill plus the projected schemas. It names neither the two valid values nor the pairing rule. bc3add9's commit message claims the lint says what to do, but that is true only of _check_invocation_axis, which a missing field never reaches. If the break stays, this message must be actionable.
2. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] needs the breaking entry with the one-line fix a consumer applies.

Also recorded: because bc3add9 REPLACED description with invocation in the schema required list, every catalog valid on v0.5.1 already carries a description on every skill. That fact was the strongest argument for defaulting and is now moot, but it stays useful for the migration note: adding 'invocation: model' is sufficient for any previously-valid source, with no second edit needed.

Unchanged by this ruling: m4zv.7 remains a release prerequisite. Declaring 'user' today projects the generated drift marker into the description slot, so the axis cannot be advertised to consumers until that is fixed.
