title: Tool-usage counting hook projected to Claude and Copilot
description:
Deterministic, token-free usage telemetry: count which terminal tools (rg, fd, bat, jq, yq, uv, ...) the agent actually invokes, so idle skills/tools can be culled from the catalog with real data. Requested 2026-07-16; design delegated and settled below after researching both platforms.

## Design
- New catalog hook script .basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py (stdlib only, never blocks: every path ends exit 0). Reads the hook JSON from stdin, accepts BOTH shapes: Claude Code PostToolUse (tool_name == Bash, tool_input.command) and Copilot postToolUse (toolName/tool_name in {bash, Bash, shell}, toolArgs/tool_input command field). Splits the command string on shell operators (pipes, &&, ||, ;, newlines), takes each segment head token, skips env assignments and shell builtins (cd, echo, exit, ...), normalizes to basename.
- Persistence: .basicly/usage/tool-usage.json mapping tool -> {count, last_used date}; atomic replace (tmp + os.replace), tolerant of a missing/corrupt file (restart from empty). The hook writes .basicly/usage/.gitignore containing '*' on first run (self-ignoring dir, like .beads) so the data survives sessions but never enters git. Per-repo-folder by design (worktrees accumulate their own).
- Claude wiring: hooks.yaml entry (id tool-usage, manager claude, stage posttooluse, matcher Bash). claude_settings.py currently hardcodes PreToolUse + the Edit|Write matcher — generalize: derive the settings event from the spec stage (pretooluse -> PreToolUse, posttooluse -> PostToolUse) and add an optional matcher field to hooks.yaml (default stays the current write-tools matcher).
- Copilot wiring: hooks live in .github/hooks/*.json ({"version": 1, "hooks": {"postToolUse": [{type command, bash/powershell/command keys, optional matcher}]}}). Add manager 'copilot' to HOOK_MANAGERS with a projection to .github/hooks/basicly-tool-usage.json (bash + powershell keys both run the same python script via uv), wired into hooks-build/hooks-check/uninstall like the claude manager.
- Dogfood: the hook ships in this repo's own projections (hooks-build here).

## Non-functional
- Zero tokens: pure python, no model calls. Resilient: never fails the tool call (async-safe, exit 0 always), atomic writes, corrupt-file recovery. Survives sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Piping a recorded Claude PostToolUse Bash JSON into the script increments counts for each pipeline segment head (e.g. 'rg foo | jq .x' -> rg+1, jq+1) and writes the self-ignoring .gitignore
- The Copilot stdin shape is parsed by the same script (unit test with both payload shapes)
- A corrupt or missing usage file never fails the hook (exit 0) and the next write starts clean
- hooks-build projects the Claude PostToolUse group into .claude/settings.json and the Copilot hook file into .github/hooks/, both idempotent; hooks-check flags drift; uninstall removes both
- Existing pretooluse protect-generated behavior is unchanged (matcher default preserved)
- Dogfooded: this repo's projections carry the hook after hooks-build; git status stays clean after a counted command runs
- Regression tests cover parsing, counting, atomicity fallback, both stdin shapes, and both projections

title: Probe br redirect capability at worktree provisioning
description:
Team-rollout hardening for basicly-c9e5: the harness loop now depends on br honoring .beads/redirect - the first br CAPABILITY dependency (not just presence). An older br silently ignores the redirect, auto-imports the worktree's checked-out issues.jsonl into a fresh local DB, and runs a divergent tracker (lost gates/claims) with no error. Add a behavior probe to worktree provisioning: after writing the redirect (moved early, before the slow dep install), run br where --json from the worktree; if br runs successfully but resolves a path other than the base .beads, abort provisioning with guidance (br upgrade, floor br 0.2.16 known good, cleanup command). A missing br or a non-workspace .beads skips the probe - br-less repos remain a supported state. Document the br floor in architecture 12.6.1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Provisioning fails with a clear upgrade message when br resolves the worktree .beads instead of following the redirect (test), skips the probe when br is absent or errors (test), and passes silently on a redirect-capable br (existing tests). The redirect+probe step runs before dependency provisioning so the failure is fast. architecture.md names the br redirect capability as a loop requirement with 0.2.16 as the known-good floor. Full gate suite passes.

title: Harden loop ship against an unmerged worktree and document the hand-recorded gate trap
description:
Retro from basicly-45ld: recording the verify gate out-of-band (basicly verify --issue / br gate report) makes derive_phase jump past the build->verify landing (loop._on_build -> _verify_and_land), which is the only step that merges the worktree. The loop then shipped+closed the bead with the feature commit stranded on the harness branch, unmerged. Two complementary fixes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Engine guard: loop._on_ship refuses to close/teardown a leaf whose bound worktree branch is not merged into its base (branch tip not an ancestor of base HEAD); it blocks with a clear reason naming the branch and base instead of closing. A branch that no longer exists (already merged + cleaned) is treated as merged. The guard runs before worktree.cleanup and before br close.
- Deterministic and side-effect-free on the block path: no close, no teardown, no tracker commit when the guard trips.
- Regression tests: a bound-but-unmerged worktree blocks at ship (issue stays open, not closed); a merged worktree ships normally; a missing branch ships normally.
- Skill doc: the harness-loop skill warns never to record the verify gate by hand during an active leaf build because the build->verify advance is the only step that merges the worktree; let loop advance record it. Projected SKILL.md regenerated.
- pytest, ruff, and the projection checks (skills-check) stay green.

## Scope

loop._on_ship guard + a small reachability helper + tests; harness-loop skill.yaml note + skills-build. No change to merge.py, no new gate mechanism.

title: Retrieval: structured I-dont-know / needs-input as a first-class loop outcome
description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 6 (D5/D6 convergence). basicly's context contribution is static projection; the "I don't know" contract is soft prose in the knowledge-priming/decision-protocol fragments the model may ignore. The loop owns a hard block-and-resume outcome (`_blocked` in loop.py) but it fires only on runner failure/checkpoints/gates, never on the agent itself signalling "iteration budget spent, fact not found".

Make a structured needs-input / I-don't-know a first-class loop outcome the HEADLESS runner can signal, mapping to the loop's existing block-and-resume contract (`_blocked(..., needs_input=<fact>)`) so the loop blocks and surfaces the missing fact instead of landing a confident wrong answer.

Signal carrier (decided): a self-ignored sentinel file the agent writes into its worktree, `.basicly/usage/needs-input.json` = {"fact": ..., "detail": ...}. The loop reads it after a clean (exit 0) dispatch, blocks with needs_input, and consumes it. Robust against output redaction/truncation and agent-neutral. The manual/handoff runner is unchanged (the driver already surfaces missing facts); a manual-driver CLI is explicitly out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A headless dispatch that finishes exit 0 with a valid `.basicly/usage/needs-input.json` in the worktree blocks the loop with a needs-input result (populated `needs_input`), does NOT land the worktree, and consumes (removes) the sentinel so a re-dispatch starts clean.
- A malformed or empty sentinel is tolerated (no crash) and falls through to the normal "finished; advance again to land it" block; a missing sentinel keeps today's behaviour exactly.
- The dispatch prompt and a projected catalog fragment document the protocol (when to write the sentinel and its shape), turning the prose escalation policy into an enforced seam.
- The needs-input reason/fact is surfaced by `loop status` / advance output the same way other blocks are.
- Full suite, ruff, ruff format, pyright, bandit, and projection gates (basicly check / skills-check / agents-check / hooks-check) pass; verified by exercising a real dispatch (not just unit tests).

## Notes

- Scope is the headless dispatch path in `loop._dispatch_runner`; the sentinel lives in the already self-ignored `.basicly/usage/` dir (same convention as run-records, tool-usage, checkpoint-confirms).

title: br 0.2.19 breaks gate report; pin to 0.2.16 (CI installs the pin, so CI stayed green)
description:
br 0.2.19 rejects the harness verify-gate call: 'br gate report <id> --gate verify --provider by-hand --status pass' fails with 'no configured transition from open requires gate verify; add a workflow.gates rule'. Reproduced on origin/main a2cdf23, so it predates the privacy-hardening work and is a tracker-version regression, not a code change.

IMPACT, two levels. Tests: 4 integration tests in tests/test_integration_loop.py fail, which blocks every push because pre-push runs the full-mode verify checks including pytest. CI never caught it because CI does not install br, so all 14 needs_br tests skip there - the gate only fires on a developer machine. Engine: verify.report_gate uses try_run_br and degrades gracefully, so the loop does not crash - it silently stops recording the verify gate. That silent degradation is arguably worse than the test failure and is the part to fix deliberately.

WHAT IS KNOWN about the policy shape, established empirically: it lives in .beads/policy.yaml, not .beads/config.yaml; workflow.gates is a map, not a sequence; its values must be a struct GateRule (serde error: 'invalid type: sequence, expected struct GateRule'); unknown fields are ignored rather than rejected, so a wrong field name parses and still fails validation. Roughly 17 candidate shapes were tried (keys: target status, gate name, from->to string; fields: require, required, requires, gates, all_of, any_of, require_all, required_gates, gate) and none satisfied validation. Passing --to explicitly does not help: --to closed and --to in_progress both fail with 'workflow does not require gate verify for transition'.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST A CONFIG LINE: GateRule is documented nowhere reachable - not br robot-docs guide, not br capabilities, not br schema (which exposes no gate or workflow schema). The obvious next step, reading the beads_rust implementation, is barred by the clean-room boundary recorded in docs/design/work-tracker.md section 7: that licence is MIT with a rider naming analyzing as restricted use for this class of user. So resolving this needs the sanctioned MIT upstream gastownhall/beads, upstream docs, or a design decision instead.

OPTIONS, none chosen: (a) find the schema in the sanctioned MIT upstream and ship a policy.yaml via basicly install; (b) pin a br version floor/ceiling and document 0.2.19 as incompatible; (c) make the 4 tests not depend on br gate report succeeding, accepting reduced coverage; (d) make verify.report_gate fail loudly instead of silently when the tracker rejects a gate, so the degradation is visible. This is a concrete instance of the unowned-external-binary risk that work-tracker.md was opened about.
close_reason: Pinned to br 0.2.16 (fc8f319), version single-sourced with drift warning, and the discarded gate verdict now blocks (0cd6f30). Full gate green: 8/8, 1487 passed. Upstream br 0.2.19 remains broken and beads_rust#398 blocks moving forward; the sibling harness repo still needs an enforced pin, tracked there.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
CORRECTION + resolution (2026-07-29).

The original diagnosis was wrong on one point: CI *does* install br. quality-gates.yml:105
runs .scripts/install_br.py, and all 14 needs_br tests run there. CI stayed green because it
installs the *pinned 0.2.16*, while this machine had drifted to 0.2.19 (installed 2026-07-28
11:16 into ~/AppData/Local/Programs/br). Same commit, same test file, only the binary differs:

  br 0.2.19  ->  4 failed, 10 passed
  br 0.2.16  -> 14 passed

Reproduced outside the harness in a throwaway repo: 0.2.16 records the gate, 0.2.19 answers
'no configured transition from open requires gate verify' and exits 4. Note we ship no
.beads/policy.yaml at all, so this is 0.2.19's *default* behaviour, not a strict-policy opt-in.

CHOSEN: option (b) pin, plus option (d) fail loudly. Not (a): upgrading forward is foreclosed
by beads_rust#398 - current main targets schema 17 and its reviewed migration accepts only
13->17 and 14->17. Our .beads/beads.db is at user_version 16, outside that matrix. Verified on
a COPY that 0.2.16 reads the schema-16 DB (424 issues), records the gate, creates issues, and
leaves user_version at 16 - the downgrade is safe in both directions.

Shipped:
- br.PINNED_VERSION is now the single source; .scripts/install_br.py imports it, and the probe
  warns on ANY difference from the pin, not just below a major.minor floor.
- loop.py no longer discards report_gate's verdict. It blocked nothing before: derive_phase
  keys off gates.can_advance, so a refused gate derived back to build and advance re-ran
  build->verify forever, silently.
- .beads/.gitignore gains *-fsqlite-* - 0.2.19 writes beads.db-fsqlite-ns-{gate,use}, which
  the existing *.fsqlite-* glob misses.

LEAD for anyone who retries the policy schema: beads_rust#399's repro shows workflow.transitions
is a 'from: [to,...]' map with an 'initial:' key, per-transition gates are keyed 'in_review ->
closed' WITH SPACES around the arrow, and a TRANSITION_ANY_FROM ('any') exists. The 17 shapes
tried here used an unspaced 'from->to'. Untested - recorded only so the next attempt starts
further along.

Related upstream, neither of them this bug: #399 (br close skips validate_transition - too
permissive, opposite direction) and #398 (schema 15/16 cannot migrate to 17).

title: Fix env deny-list to Edit-only form Claude Code accepts
description:
The u0zg .env deny strengthening added Write(...)/MultiEdit(...)/NotebookEdit(...) file-permission rules, but Claude Code does not match those tool forms in file-permission checks and rejects them with a startup warning (and MultiEdit no longer exists). An Edit(path) rule already covers every file-mutation tool (Edit, Write, NotebookEdit). Reduce the .env deny to the Edit(...) globs only and narrow the PreToolUse matcher to Edit|Write|NotebookEdit.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the u0zg deny-list with Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit .env rules
2. Start Claude Code
3. It warns that the Write(...)/NotebookEdit(...)/MultiEdit(...) file rules are not valid permission forms

## Acceptance Criteria

* permissions.yaml env-edit rule carries only the Edit(...) globs
* settings.json and the PreToolUse matcher match the source with no startup warning
* the regression test asserts Edit-only coverage and the absence of Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit file rules
* permissions-check reports the projection up to date

title: drive the checkpoint-gated loop state machine
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- advances intake to classify to decompose to build to merge to verify to ship to teardown
- enforces the three human checkpoints and the bounded rework loop via the policy engine
- composes the decomposer, worktree lifecycle, verify runner, and serial merge queue
- resumes correctly from the loop state read purely out of br

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
close_reason: Implemented the checkpoint-gated loop state machine (src/basicly/loop.py): a resumable single-step advance() that reads the current phase from br (loop_state, onb.6.1) and dispatches per phase, composing classify (onb.6.2), the decomposer (onb.4), worktree lifecycle (onb.1), the verify runner (onb.2), and the serial merge queue (onb.5), enforcing the three human checkpoints and the bounded rework loop via the policy engine (onb.3). Key correctness property: because the phase is derived from br, every step either blocks or produces a new br signal that moves the derived phase forward, so handlers and derive_phase never disagree and run_until_blocked cannot spin. Leaf types build in their own worktree; features fan out child worktrees and land them via the merge queue. AdvanceResult reports from/to/action/blocked/needs_input; run_until_blocked driver over advance(). 208 tests pass (18 new); dogfooded on a real throwaway feature (intake records type, blocks on classify checkpoint; fresh advance after approval reconstructs classify phase purely from br and blocks needing children) then hard-deleted. 3rd of onb.6's four children.

CORE SHAPE — a single-step, resumable transition:
- advance(repo_root, issue_id, *, config=None, work_type=None, children=None) -> AdvanceResult.
- It FIRST reads loop_state.read_node_state(issue_id) to get the current phase (resume point), then dispatches on phase via a HANDLER DICT (phase -> _handler), mirroring cmd_worktree/cmd_policy dispatch so we stay under PLR0911 (<=6 returns) / PLR0913 (<=5 args) — pass agent inputs in a small frozen Inputs dataclass, not as many kwargs.
- AdvanceResult(frozen): from_phase, to_phase (== from_phase when blocked), action ("classified"/"decomposed"/"built"/"merged"/"verified"/"shipped"/"tore-down"/"blocked"/"escalated"), blocked_reason|None, needs_input|None (what the agent/human must supply next). No exceptions for normal blocks — return a blocked result.

PHASE -> ACTION MAPPING (each composes an already-tested module):
- intake: requires work_type; absent -> blocked(needs_input="work_type"); present -> classify.classify(repo,id,work_type) -> to "classify".
- classify: gated by the classify human checkpoint (policy.checkpoint_approved) AND DoR (classify returns can_leave_classify / policy.definition_of_ready). Both true -> to "decompose"; else blocked(needs classify checkpoint approval and/or DoR sections).
- decompose: requires children plan; absent -> blocked(needs_input="children"); present -> decompose.decompose(repo,id,children); then gated by the decompose checkpoint -> to "build".
- build: for each dependency-unblocked child (loop_state.ready_ranked, concurrency-capped by WorktreeConfig), worktree.create(name) and stash the binding via br update --external-ref loop_state.format_worktree_ref(name,branch). Agent builds + verifies each child (that is child-level advance recursion — see design Q3). When children are green -> to "merge".
- merge: merge.merge_queue(repo, [(name,bead)...], config) in the decomposer's serial/topological order; on a node failure the queue already records rework + escalation (policy) -> surface as blocked/escalated.
- verify: verify.run_verify(repo, mode) + verify.report_gate(repo,id,report); gate_status must show the required gate green (policy.gate_status.can_advance) -> to "ship"; fail -> policy.record_rework + should_escalate (bounded n=2, config.max_rework) -> blocked/escalated.
- ship: gated by the ship human checkpoint -> to "teardown".
- teardown: worktree.cleanup for the node's worktrees + br close the issue -> "done".

DESIGN QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE IN-SESSION:
(Q1) Single-step advance() core vs a run() loop. RECOMMEND: advance() is the primitive (resumable, agent/human re-invokes each step); add a thin run_until_blocked(repo, issue_id, inputs) driver that loops advance() until it blocks/checkpoints/finishes. The CLI (onb.6.4) wires both; one-shot mode (arch 12.2) = auto-approve the middle checkpoint in the driver.
(Q2) Where agent inputs live: pass work_type/children into advance() (or an Inputs dataclass); when a phase needs one and it is absent, block and report needs_input. Keeps the engine agent-agnostic (no prompting inside the engine).
(Q3) Fractal recursion (epic->feature->task, arch 12.1/12.2). RECOMMEND scope onb.6.3 to the SINGLE-TRACK linear machine; children advance via the SAME advance() invoked per child by the driver over ready_ranked. Full auto-recursion inside one advance() call is deferred (leave a clear hook + a note); the AC only requires the linear phase machine + checkpoints + rework + resume. Confirm this boundary.

TESTS (tests/test_loop.py): unit-test each transition by monkeypatching the composed callables on the loop module (loop.read_node_state, loop.classify, loop.decompose, loop.worktree, loop.verify, loop.merge, loop.policy) — same fake pattern as test_merge/test_loop_state. Cover: resume-from-each-phase advances correctly; a pending checkpoint blocks (not error); DoR-not-ready blocks the classify->decompose exit; a failed verify records rework and escalates at the cap; a clean happy path walks intake->...->done. Assert on AdvanceResult (from/to/action/blocked_reason), and that the right module was invoked.

DOGFOOD (real br, keep it light — build/merge are already dogfooded in their own modules): create a throwaway feature, advance() it: intake w/ work_type -> classify (real br type recorded), then classify blocked on the pending checkpoint; approve_checkpoint + add AC so DoR passes -> advance to decompose blocked on needs_input="children". Verify the machine advances/blocks against REAL br, then hard-delete the throwaway.

GUARDRAILS (from this session): verify REAL br json field names before asserting (dependency_type vs type bit us); commit SUBJECT = lowercase letters/digits/spaces/hyphens only, NO . / + / _ (bead id trailing in BODY); the commit-messages CI gate now validates the FULL message (fixed in basicly-acx) so a body-trailer id is fine; before `git add`, check `git status` so no file left staged from a prior attempt sneaks in; pre-commit stashes unstaged tracked files, so commit a SELF-CONSISTENT set (don't split a symbol from its importer); structure advance() as a phase->handler dispatch dict to stay under PLR0911/PLR0913.

AFTER .3: onb.6.4 (basicly loop CLI) unblocks (last child) -> then onb.6 closes -> onb.8 (guidance) unblocks. onb.7 (P3 runner adapters) independent.

title: Fix the release changelog generator ordering and double-blank seam
description:
Retro finding (v0.5.0 and v0.5.1 this session): the release changelog generator produces the new section in the wrong place and with a lint violation, so it needs hand-fixing every release.

Root cause: .scripts/generate_release_changelog.py _insert_index returns the index of the first "## " heading, which is "## [Unreleased]". The new "## vX.Y.Z" section is therefore inserted ABOVE [Unreleased] instead of below it, and the join leaves two consecutive blank lines before the following section (markdownlint MD012). Both releases this session required a manual reorder plus a blank-line fix.

Proposed fix: insert the new release section immediately AFTER an existing "## [Unreleased]" section (keeping [Unreleased] on top), and never emit a double blank line at the seam. Fall back sensibly (insert after the intro) when no [Unreleased] section exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- generate_release_changelog.py inserts a new "## vX.Y.Z - DATE" section immediately after an existing "## [Unreleased]" section so [Unreleased] stays at the top; when none exists it inserts after the header intro.
- The output has no consecutive blank lines at the insertion seam (markdownlint MD012 passes on the generated CHANGELOG.md without hand-editing).
- A regression test covers insertion order with an [Unreleased] section present and asserts no double blank lines.
- Once correct, trim the "reordering/curation" caveat in the release-process skill to only the genuine curation step (grouping raw commits into Added/Fixed).

- Quirks are NOT a skill; each quirk is distributed into the skill that owns its domain.

Specs (authoritative):
- Agent Skills: https://agentskills.io/specification
- AGENTS.md: https://agents.md/
- Skills tooling + agent discovery paths: https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/README.md

title: Rich-skill engine: full Agent Skills spec compliance (bundle references/scripts/assets + extended frontmatter)
description:
WHY: basicly currently authors a skill as .basicly/core/skills/<name>/skill.yaml (fields: name, description, instructions, technologies) and renders ONLY a single SKILL.md via skills.py:render_skill_md/sync_skills. It does NOT copy references/, scripts/, assets/, or any additional files to the skill roots. The Agent Skills spec (https://agentskills.io/specification) allows a skill directory to contain SKILL.md (required) plus scripts/, references/, assets/, and '... Any additional files or directories'. To author powerful skills (e.g. a python skill with a long references/ style guide + a fixer scripts/), the engine must project the whole skill directory.

SCOPE / FILES:
- src/basicly/skills.py: sync_skills / check_synced_skills / discover_skills / render_skill_md — copy every file & subdirectory of the source skill dir (except the skill.yaml source, which renders to SKILL.md) into each destination root (.claude/skills/<name>/ and .agents/skills/<name>/), verbatim, preserving structure. Prune on technology deselection. Add/verify freshness in check.
- src/basicly/schema.py + .basicly/core/schemas/skill.schema.json: extend the skill source to support the spec's optional frontmatter passthrough — license, compatibility, metadata (map), allowed-tools — rendered into SKILL.md frontmatter. Keep 'technologies' (basicly-internal scoping; NOT emitted into SKILL.md frontmatter, or emitted under metadata — decide and document).
- Generated-marker / protect-generated hooks (.basicly/core/hooks/protect-generated*.py): SKILL.md stays generated (marker), but bundled reference/script/asset files are HAND-AUTHORED sources that must be copied but NOT carry the generated marker and NOT be clobbered/pruned wrongly. Define the rule and enforce it.
- .basicly/generated-manifest.json: track projected skill files (including copied resources) so build/check/uninstall stay consistent.
- catalog-lint (.basicly/core/hooks/catalog-lint.py + src/basicly/catalog_lint.py): validate skill dirs against the spec — name matches dir (1-64 chars, lowercase a-z0-9 and single hyphens, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphen), description non-empty <=1024 chars, SKILL.md body kept small (warn > ~500 lines per spec progressive disclosure), file references one level deep.
- basicly build / skills-build / skills-check / install / uninstall: end-to-end still green with resource files present.
- docs/architecture.md: document the full-spec skill layout and the source->projection mapping.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. A skill authored as .basicly/core/skills/<name>/ with skill.yaml + references/REF.md + scripts/x.sh + assets/y + an arbitrary extra file/dir projects ALL of them (unchanged bytes) into BOTH .claude/skills/<name>/ and .agents/skills/<name>/, alongside the rendered SKILL.md.
2. Optional frontmatter (license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools) round-trips from skill.yaml into SKILL.md frontmatter per spec; omitting them yields today's minimal frontmatter.
3. Technology deselection prunes the whole projected skill dir (all resources), not just SKILL.md.
4. basicly check / skills-check --all-default-roots / hooks-check / catalog lint all pass; protect-generated does not flag hand-authored resource files, and does not allow manual edits to generated SKILL.md.
5. New unit tests cover: full-dir copy, extra '...' files, frontmatter passthrough, prune-on-deselect, and check-detects-drift for a resource file.
6. 'skills-ref validate ./<projected-skill>' (https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/tree/main/skills-ref) passes for a projected skill, or a documented reason if that tool is unavailable in-repo.

SPEC: https://agentskills.io/specification (directory structure incl. the '...' line; frontmatter table; progressive disclosure: metadata ~100 tokens, SKILL.md < ~5000 tokens / < 500 lines, resources on demand; file references one level deep; validation via skills-ref).

title: Correct the stale scoped-tier claim that says no fragment declares a scope
description:
## Context

Found while landing basicly-lelg (2026-07-31) and deliberately left out of scope there, because it is
not among that bead's seven enumerated defects. Same class of error, same file, and it will mislead the
same way.

`docs/architecture/architecture.md` §14 (around line 1320-1325) makes two claims that are now wrong:

1. **"the path-scoped tier is already built ... and no fragment declares one"** — stale. Two fragments
   declare a scope today (`external-review` on `docs/research/**` + `docs/design/**`, and the
   platform-hermetic tests fragment on `tests/**`). The equivalent line at
   `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:125` was already corrected; this one was missed.
2. **"it improves both cost _and_ adherence"** — contradicts the finding basicly-lelg just recorded.
   Scoping is only a cost *reduction* for Claude and Copilot. For codex it is a strict cost
   *increase*: scoped fragments are inlined into `AGENTS.md` at ~1500 chars each (measured 1462 and
   1614), because codex has no glob scoping and nested `AGENTS.md` below the cwd is never loaded. So the
   claim is true for two of three families and false for the third — which is exactly the asymmetry
   `implementation-plan.md:403-409` is careful about and this sentence flattens.

The adherence half of the claim also deserves a look rather than a copy: basicly-agzx.1 measured recall
at 98% / 93%, and Phase 4's own exit criterion was weakened to "recall **not degraded**" precisely
because there is no headroom left to improve. A sentence asserting scoping "improves adherence" sits
badly next to that.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `docs/architecture/architecture.md` around lines 1320-1325.
2. Compare against `.basicly/core/fragments/` (two fragments carry `scope`), against
   `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:125`, and against §7 detail 4 as corrected by basicly-lelg.
3. Observed: the architecture reference says no fragment declares a scope, and that scoping improves
   cost and adherence for everyone. Expected: it names the two fragments that do declare scopes, and
   states the asymmetry — cost falls for claude and copilot, rises for codex — instead of a blanket
   improvement claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the architecture reference section on the path-scoped tier when it is read then it no longer claims that no fragment declares a scope, and the cost claim names the asymmetry between claude and copilot on one side and codex on the other rather than asserting a blanket improvement, with the adherence claim either evidenced against the agzx.1 measurement or dropped

title: Verify gate recorded in a worktree is silently lost at landing - fix and document
description:
Found shipping basicly-3yv: 'basicly verify --issue <id>' records the br gate in whichever checkout it runs from. A gate recorded inside a build-phase worktree lives only in that worktree's tracker copy and is discarded at landing, so the base tracker still shows the verify gate missing and the loop blocks. The intended phase order (build advance lands first, verify phase then runs from base) works but nothing enforces or explains it. Fix in code (e.g. verify warns/refuses when recording a gate from a harness worktree, or the loop merges worktree gate records at landing) and externalize the trap from session memory into the harness-loop skill / agent instructions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A verify gate recorded from a harness worktree can no longer be silently lost: the engine either surfaces it at landing or refuses/warns at record time with guidance to run from base. Tests cover the chosen behavior. The harness-loop skill (and any affected fragment) documents the phase order and the trap. Full gate suite passes.

title: Governance: gate loop human-checkpoint approvals on interactive confirmation so a non-interactive/subagent process cannot self-approve ship
description:
From spike basicly-zv48 field incident (2026-07-17): a Claude Code fork inherited the full directive and autonomously drove the loop to ship+close (checkpoint --approve, loop advance) beyond its read-only mandate. Because the human session and its forks share one OS/git identity (the D1 gap), basicly cannot distinguish a rogue approval from an authorized one. Mitigation basicly can own: make policy checkpoint {classify,decompose,ship} --approve refuse in a non-interactive context (require a TTY or an ephemeral confirm-code the human types), so a subagent Bash without a controlling TTY cannot self-approve. Deterministic, agent-agnostic, aligns with the human-checkpoint intent. First task: verify the 'tool-invoked Bash has no TTY' assumption across claude/codex/copilot before relying on it as a floor. Complementary to attribution (basicly-z6dh run-record, basicly-140a). Does not prevent doc-writing/bead-filing (cheap, reversible) - only the consequential ship.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `policy checkpoint <name> --approve` records approval directly when stdin is an interactive TTY.
- In a non-interactive context (no controlling TTY) with no confirm code, the command refuses to approve (non-zero exit, no marker recorded) and prints a one-time ephemeral confirm code plus the exact re-run command.
- Re-running with `--confirm <code>` records the approval only when the code matches and has not expired; a wrong or expired code is refused with no marker recorded.
- The gate covers all three checkpoints (classify, decompose, ship).
- Confirm-code state lives in the self-ignored .basicly/usage/ dir using the same atomic write pattern as run-records.
- TTY assumption verified for Claude Code (no TTY on stdin/stdout/stderr); codex/copilot use the same piped-subprocess pattern (inferred).
- Deterministic and agent-agnostic; does not defeat a determined same-identity fork (D1 out of scope).
design: Add a guarded-approval layer in policy.py. approve_checkpoint stays the raw recorder. New approve_checkpoint_guarded(repo_root, issue, name, *, interactive, confirm) returns an ApprovalResult(status in {approved,challenge,rejected}, code, detail). interactive True -> record + approved. Non-interactive + confirm None -> generate ephemeral code, store {issue:name -> {code, expires}} in .basicly/usage/checkpoint-confirms.json (atomic tmp-replace, self-ignored), return challenge with the code. Non-interactive + confirm -> consume-and-validate against stored code and TTL -> approved or rejected. Code generator and clock are module-level helpers (_new_code, _now) so tests monkeypatch them and the public signature stays under the 5-arg PLR0913 ceiling. CLI _cmd_policy_checkpoint detects sys.stdin.isatty(), passes interactive + --confirm, and maps ApprovalResult to output + exit code. TTL constant e.g. 900s.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `policy checkpoint <name> --approve` records approval directly when stdin is an interactive TTY.
2. In a non-interactive context (no controlling TTY) with no confirm code, the command REFUSES to approve (non-zero exit, no marker recorded), and prints a one-time ephemeral confirm code plus the exact re-run command.
3. Re-running with `--confirm <code>` records the approval only when the code matches and has not expired (TTL); a wrong or expired code is refused with no marker recorded.
4. The gate covers all three checkpoints (classify, decompose, ship).
5. Confirm-code state is stored in the self-ignored .basicly/usage/ dir (never committed) using the same atomic write pattern as run-records.
6. TTY assumption verified: a tool-invoked Bash (Claude Code) has no controlling TTY on stdin/stdout/stderr; codex/copilot invoke Bash via the same piped-subprocess pattern (inferred, not directly exercised).
7. Deterministic and agent-agnostic; explicitly does NOT defeat a determined same-identity fork (the D1 shared-identity gap is out of scope) - it forces a deliberate second step that an autopilot directive will not contain.

title: Identity: optional per-agent bot git identity and commit-signing tamper-evidence trust model
description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 1. Allow the headless runner to dispatch under a configured per-agent GIT_AUTHOR/COMMITTER identity (opt-in, validated by identity-guard allow-email), and document/optionally gate an append-only tamper-evidence trust model (optional commit signing for harness commits).

## Acceptance Criteria

- RunnerSpec gains optional git_name and git_email fields (default None); _parse_runner_agent reads git_name/git_email from each [[runner.agents]] entry. Both must be set together or neither: a spec with one but not the other raises a clear ValueError at parse time.
- When a runner spec carries a bot identity, runner.run injects GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL and GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL into the dispatched subprocess env (copied from os.environ, not replacing it) so commits the agent makes in its worktree carry the bot identity. When absent, the child environment is unchanged (current behavior, backward compatible).
- The bot identity is subject to the same identity-guard gate as a human: docs state a configured bot email must satisfy basicly.identityAllowEmail when strict mode is set, so a bot commit passes the same pre-commit floor. No weakening of identity-guard.
- DEFAULT_CONFIG_TOML documents the optional git_name/git_email per-agent keys as commented examples in the [[runner.agents]] block, and test_config stays consistent with the built-in defaults.
- The append-only tamper-evidence trust model is documented in docs/architecture.md dimension-1 identity section: per-repo identity gate (identity-guard) + optional opt-in commit signing (commit.gpgsign) with the existing deny-list forbidding --no-verify/--no-gpg-sign as the floor. basicly does not force signing; it documents enabling it. No new signing enforcement code.
- Regression tests: parse of a runner agent with both fields, with neither, and the paired-field ValueError; runner.run injects the four env vars when set and leaves env untouched when not.
- pytest, ruff, and the projection checks stay green.

## Scope

The concrete build is the opt-in per-agent identity injection at the runner-dispatch seam (RunnerSpec + _parse_runner_agent + runner.run env) plus docs for the trust model. The merge-commit already carries agent attribution via Harness-Runner/Harness-Model trailers (basicly-140a); this bead does not change that path. The signing/tamper-evidence half is documentation of an opt-in git-config model, not new enforcement code - the permissions deny-list already backstops --no-verify/--no-gpg-sign. No changes to identity-guard.py. Runner identity lives with [runner]/RunnerSpec, not the .basicly/core/agents/ subagent catalog.

description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 while sequencing the v0.7.0 forecast chain. The release ladder
(`docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` section 4.0) lists `v0.7.0` as containing "model
provenance `kjc5.59`-`.61`" and `v0.8.0` as containing "capability tiers (`imnu.3` +
`kjc5.58`)". The tracker's dependency graph makes that impossible: `basicly-kjc5.58`
blocks `basicly-kjc5.61` and `basicly-kjc5.60`, and `kjc5.61` blocks `kjc5.59`, which
blocks `jr0l.21`, which blocks `jr0l.22`. So none of v0.7.0's model-provenance work can
start until a bead the plan assigns to v0.8.0 lands.

The edges are correct, not over-strict, and were checked before filing: `kjc5.58`
establishes the tier vocabulary (low/medium/high/maximum) in the catalog schema, and
`kjc5.61` is precisely the generator that resolves a tier to a per-family model id.
`kjc5.61` has nothing to resolve without it. So the fix is the plan's placement, not the
graph.

Precedent for the resolution: `m4zv.12` and `m4zv.13` are `phase-2` beads already pulled
forward into `v0.7.0`'s hardening batch with their phase labels unchanged (section 4.0 and
the Phase 2 note). `kjc5.58` is the same shape - a `phase-3` bead a `v0.7.0` chain
depends on.

Docs-only: no code, no projection. The handover file carries the same gap (it lists the
forecast chain as `jr0l.21/.22/.34/.35/.37`, `kjc5.59-.61`), so a session that trusts
either surface starts the chain at a blocked bead.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Read `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` section 4.0: the `v0.7.0` row lists `kjc5.59`-`.61`
  and the `v0.8.0` row lists `kjc5.58`.
- Run `br show basicly-kjc5.61` and `br show basicly-kjc5.59`: both are blocked by
  `basicly-kjc5.58`.
- Observed 2026-07-31: `basicly loop status basicly-kjc5.59` reports it blocked, and the
  ready set contains `basicly-kjc5.58` instead. Expected: the release the ladder assigns a
  chain to contains every bead that chain is blocked on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the release ladder in section 4.0 when a reader takes the v0.7.0 forecast chain as
  the work to start then every bead that chain is blocked on is listed in that same release
  row with the reason it moved, and no release row lists a bead an earlier row depends on

title: Phase 0 make an unattended run possible and stop a published leak
description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 0. Depends on nothing. Size 2-3 sessions.

The 2026-07-26 dogfood met its acceptance criterion but needed one human intervention, caused by two defects that interact. Plus one committed data leak that should not wait behind anything: source_repo_path publishes three machine layouts to every consumer clone (re-measured 2026-07-26 at c175c1a - 365 of 366 records, /home/<user-a>, /home/<user-b> and a Windows <redacted:windows-drive-path> path, up from the 328 of 332 the plan recorded).

Why not later: Phase 1 measures cost per landed package. If a lane can be charged rework for a flake and cannot be released once escalated, the measurement measures the defects.

title: Prove an unattended supervised run by re-running the dogfood shape
description:
## Context

Plan §4 Phase 0 exit criteria: "Re-run the dogfood shape to prove it rather than reasoning about it."

The 2026-07-26 kjc5.22 dogfood met its acceptance criterion - three concurrent lanes, landed through the merge queue, no human editing code - but needed one human intervention. Four defects caused or masked it: 4tjt (nothing clears the rework counter so an answered retry cannot be executed), 55yh (a flaky gate spends a lane rework budget), jr0l.14 (the first commit in a fresh worktree stalls past ten minutes and is indistinguishable from a wedged lane to the StallWatchdog), and 8veb (the supervisor hides its own progress when stdout is a pipe, so the run cannot be observed).

This bead is the proof, not the fixes. It re-runs the same shape on real work and reports the intervention count with its causes, so Phase 1 measures the harness rather than the defects.
acceptance_criteria: Given the four unattended-run defects have landed when the dogfood shape is re-run as a supervised multi-lane run on real work then it completes with zero human interventions attributable to a harness defect and the run reports the intervention count with a cause for each

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
[harness-info] Proof-run plan, drafted 2026-07-26 with the owner. Two corrections to the initial framing are recorded first because they change the risk.

Correction 1 - jr0l is not a low-risk root. It has 20 non-closed children, 19 ready, and the scheduler ranks by priority and score rather than by risk. The lanes it would actually dispatch are kjc5.29 (rank 8, refuse to dispatch an unresolved model - on the critical path to 7bur), kjc5.32 (rank 10, coupling attribution - should precede Phase 5), then kjc5.49, kjc5.50, kjc5.51. Those are real Phase 1/5/7 work, not the catalog capacity fillers the root was chosen for. There is no single root that isolates only the low-risk beads.

Correction 2 - the spend ceiling exists only on a grant. policy.spend_status returns halted=False outright when no grant is active, so at true L0 there is no token cap and the halt predicate is inert. There is no [policy.spend] section anywhere. GRANT_COVERAGE resolves it: L1 delegates only the decompose checkpoint, which a leaf bead never reaches, so an L1 grant carrying a token_budget gives a hard ceiling while leaving classify and ship human on every lane.

Decided with the owner: root basicly-jr0l; autonomy raised one notch to L1 in basicly.toml solely to make the grant issuable, with an L1 grant of 1000000 tokens; every classify and ship checkpoint answered by a human with a minted confirm code; the ceiling reverted to L0 after the run.

Known wart: loop supervise takes only the issue argument, so both the runner and the autonomy ceiling have to be changed repo-wide in basicly.toml for the duration and reverted after. That is exactly what basicly-jr0l.8 exists to fix and it is still open, so doing jr0l.8 first would remove two config round-trips from this procedure.

Also required: [runner] default is currently manual, with a comment that auto-dispatch would double-run the interactively driven loop. It must become a real agent (claude and copilot are both on PATH) for the run to dispatch at all, and revert afterwards.

Pre-flight, before any tokens: basicly runner dry-run to verify the dispatch command; basicly decompose --dry-run on each candidate lane for the sizing verdict, because cost is bounded by sizing the work and never by killing an agent; confirm base is clean and no supervisor lock is held; and fix the intervention tally definition in advance - a checkpoint approval is by design and does not count, an intervention caused by a harness defect does.

Measurement to record: total tokens against the 3.36M baseline, wall clock, lanes landed, and every intervention with its cause. The acceptance criterion is zero interventions attributable to a harness defect.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
[harness-info] Proof run executed 2026-07-26. The acceptance criterion is NOT met, and the run cost 34.16 dollars for 46026602 tokens across three lanes.

What worked. Everything built earlier in the session behaved: the session overrides applied with no committed config touched (jr0l.8, jr0l.15), all three lanes were adopted and dispatched concurrently, progress was visible live through a pipe (8veb), the halt surfaced as a queue item rather than a silent stall, and jr0l.17 correctly reported spend under this grant rather than lifetime. Two lanes landed through the merge queue; the third was cancelled pre-landing by D5 when a sibling landing moved its base, then landed by hand from its committed branch at no extra cost. All three shipped. The suite went 1360 to 1415 tests, all green. kjc5.51 honoured the [harness-wait] comment-marker constraint amended into its AC, so the section 3.4 discipline held under an unsupervised agent.

Interventions attributable to a harness defect: two.

1. The grant budget metered lifetime session spend, so a 5M ceiling halted before dispatching once against 30705839 tokens of history. Fixed mid-run as basicly-jr0l.17.
2. The forecast was wrong by two to three orders of magnitude, so the ceiling admitted a pass that spent nine times it. Now basicly-jr0l.21 (forecast spend and wall clock per model) and basicly-jr0l.22 (admit a pass on forecast spend), with basicly-kjc5.29 promoted to a prerequisite of both.

Ship checkpoints and the D5 re-dispatch do not count - those are by design.

Owner correction that settled the diagnosis: the admission gate is right and must stay. Cost is bounded by sizing the work, never by killing a working agent. The defect is the forecast, and the decomposition has to cut work so each lane is optimally sized - which means learning actual tokens and wall clock per unit of work, per model, because different models need different amounts and models change constantly.

This bead is now blocked on jr0l.22, so a re-run is gated on the spend forecast existing. That is deliberate: repeating this run today would be financially unsafe, not merely inconclusive.

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: [harness-info] Proof-run budget set 2026-07-29 by the owner delegating the call. Grant L1 with a 10000000 token ceiling. Derivation: the successful kjc5.22 dogfood spent 3360000 tokens across three lanes, so 10M leaves about 3x headroom for a correctly sized pass while the 46026602 tokens of the failed attempt is refused at admission once basicly-jr0l.22 makes the gate predictive. At the blended rate the failed run itself demonstrated - 34.16 dollars over 46026602 tokens, about 0.74 dollars per million - that ceiling caps the proof at roughly 7 to 8 dollars against the 34.16 it cost last time. Recorded rather than asserted so the number can be checked.

title: Reconcile the projected skill count against the catalog sources
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 while refreshing the plan's section 2 catalog-entry counts for basicly-aplj. The three counts disagree and the reason is untraced:

- 32 `skill.yaml` sources under `.basicly/core/skills/` plus `.basicly-local/`
- 28 `SKILL.md` files projected to the Claude root `.claude/skills/`
- 27 projected to `.agents/skills/`
- `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots` reports 58 total writes across both roots

So four sources reach neither root and one more reaches only Claude. The likely cause is the `applies_to` and `technologies` filters doing their job, in which case the fix is documentation rather than code - but that has not been checked, and the plan quoted 29 projected skills as an eval-coverage figure without it being checked either.

This matters because the eval-coverage lift in Phase 1 is stated as a count of routable guidance entries. A count that cannot be reproduced from the sources is not evidence, and section 2 now carries a recount flag instead of a number.

## Notes

Check whether a source that projects to no root at all is intentional. If it is not, that is a silently dropped catalog entry and this bead is a bug rather than a task.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/` skill planning and filtering
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` section 2
acceptance_criteria: Given the catalog skill sources when the projected skill count is reported then every source either projects to a named root or its exclusion is attributable to a declared applies_to or technologies filter and the plan states a count reproducible from the sources

title: tool-usage telemetry counts heredoc bodies, python keywords and bare flags as tools
description:
The tool-usage PostToolUse hook pipeline-head extraction still records non-tool tokens as tools. Live 'basicly usage report' (2026-07-17) shows the tools table counting def (90, last used today), assert (83), from (47), return (31), import (18), heredoc delimiters EOF/PYEOF, and bare flags -d (120)/-/t/p, plus words like the/old/new/result. These leak from heredoc bodies and python -c/-m inline snippets that the quote-aware split (basicly-zcvo / commit c5bdc4e) does not fully strip. Impact: pollutes the D3 observability telemetry the harness uses to cull idle skills/tools. Fix: strip heredoc bodies fully, skip python -c/-m inline token bodies, and drop leading bare flags before taking a segment head in tools_in_command (.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py). Add regression cases for a heredoc, a python -c one-liner, and a flag-led segment. Note: earlier in the spike session this was mis-triaged as already-fixed by checking for the fix commit instead of running the report.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a shell command whose heredoc tag is backslash-escaped (e.g. 'python3 - <<\\PY') or whose pipeline has a flag-led segment
2. The PostToolUse tool-usage hook records the heredoc body's python keywords, the terminator tag, and the bare flag as tool names
3. 'basicly usage report' lists def/import/return/PY/-d etc. as tools, polluting the D3 observability telemetry

## Acceptance Criteria

* heredoc bodies are stripped even when the tag is backslash-escaped (<<\\TAG) or tab-stripped (<<-TAG), so no body line or terminator is counted
* a pipeline segment whose head is a bare flag or a shell builtin records nothing for that segment
* python -c/-m inline snippets never leak their code tokens as tool names
* regression tests cover a backslash-tag heredoc, a python -c one-liner, and a flag-led segment

- docs/foundry-spike.md - the research spike it captured is implemented (its follow-up beads are filed and largely shipped), so it is likely archivable or removable rather than a live design doc.
- docs/.nojekyll - a GitHub Pages marker that disables Jekyll so files/dirs starting with _ or . are served; confirm the docs site actually needs it and record why, or remove it if the site does not use Pages that way.

Produce two artifacts: (a) a removal-candidate list, each entry with why it is obsolete plus a safe-removal check (nothing in code, docs, the packaged dist, the site build, or CI references it); (b) a short inventory documenting the purpose of the non-obvious tracked files that stay.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written list of removal candidates, each with a why-obsolete rationale and a reference/usage check proving nothing depends on it (grep across code/docs/CI/site + packaged-dist check).
- A short inventory of non-obvious tracked files (like .nojekyll) and their purpose, committed to docs or the tracker.
- Follow-up removal beads filed for the confirmed candidates; no deletions performed in this bead (deleting files needs explicit confirmation and happens in the follow-up).

title: Own the work tracker: remove the external beads dependency
description:
## Context

Opened 2026-07-25 on the owner's direction. The tracker is not a peripheral integration - it is the harness's state. br is the single source of truth for every phase derivation, gate, checkpoint, dependency edge, decision item and run record, and the engine deliberately keeps no side-state, so every guarantee the harness makes is downstream of it. That dependency is unowned: beads_rust and bv are MIT and excellent today, but licenses change, maintainers move on, and a breaking change upstream lands in our critical path. We already carry a version floor and version-specific workarounds.

Design doc: docs/work-tracker.md, opened as an initialization rather than a build plan. The tractable part is that the harness's tracker surface is narrow and enumerable - roughly twenty subcommands - so this is not rebuilding a general-purpose issue tracker. Telemetry comes first: no schema is designed from memory of our own usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a full factory session including a supervised multi-lane run when its telemetry is reviewed then docs/work-tracker.md carries a frozen surface list a ledger schema a cache decision and a component breakdown, and a differential test shows the owned tracker answering phase derivation ready set and gate status identically to the external one across the tracker whole history

## Scope

- `docs/work-tracker.md`
acceptance_criteria: Given a full factory session including a supervised multi-lane run when its telemetry is reviewed then docs/work-tracker.md carries a frozen surface list a ledger schema a cache decision and a component breakdown, and a differential test shows the owned tracker answering phase derivation ready set and gate status identically to the external one across the tracker whole history

- vkh0.1 (br/bv usage telemetry) - it has LEAD TIME. The whole design waits on measured usage, and data only accumulates while the harness is being used. Deferring it means arriving at the decision point with no data and waiting all over again. It is also small and independent.

comments.text:
[harness-info] Owner decision 2026-07-29: raise this epic's priority and target it as the release *after* v0.6.0 unless something blocks it. Rationale given: br is flaky and costs time and money through its own errors.

The bill so far, all of it already paid and recorded, is the argument:

1. Clock validation rejects an update whose updated_at precedes created_at, blocking a lane twice consecutively with a different victim test each run (basicly-jr0l.41, this session).
2. A machine-global write lock at the user's beads dir with a 30s timeout forced pytest workers to be capped at 4, since worker count is contention on one lock rather than parallelism (basicly-9s59).
3. br create --slug mints multi-hyphen ids that our own commit-msg gate rejects (basicly-jms0).
4. --acceptance-criteria exists only on update, not create, so filing a bead is always two calls.
5. The acceptance-criteria field accepts a single line only.
6. br list --json caps near fifty and drops closed records whatever --limit says, so a zero-finding audit can be silently false (basicly-jr0l.4).
7. Plain br delete resurrects the record from JSONL on the next command; only --hard prunes, and probe beads otherwise leave tombstones the loop commits.
8. The export writes machine-specific absolute paths, needing a scrub step before every hand commit (basicly-vkh0.5, basicly-jr0l.29).
9. br config set destroyed the config file's comments (basicly-jkht).
10. Dependency-field spelling is inconsistent across commands.
11. Lint templates are not configurable.
12. There is no git merge-driver, so parallel-branch tracker state needs an explicit br sync --merge.

Every one of these is requirements input for the replacement rather than a workaround to maintain, which is what basicly-vkh0.6 exists to carry. The plan's sequencing in docs/plan/implementation-plan.md still places this at Phase 6 and explicitly off the critical path; that ordering is now superseded and the plan needs updating to match.

title: Record br and bv usage at subcommand and flag level in a committed ledger
description:
## Context

Prerequisite for docs/work-tracker.md: the surface list must come from measurement, not from memory of our own usage. The tool-usage hook already counts tool invocations, but only at the binary level (br as one token) and it writes to the self-ignored usage dir, so it describes one machine and never travels.

Extend it to record the subcommand and the flags used, and write to a committed append-only ledger so the sample accumulates across machines and team members. Distinguish engine call sites from interactive human calls: the engine's set is the hard requirement for a replacement, while the human's set may be thinner at first. Record enough to answer read/write ratio and per-surface latency so the cache design is measured rather than assumed, and so surfaces nobody uses can simply not exist.

Reuse the existing hook rather than adding a second counter, and keep it telemetry rather than a gate - every path exits 0, writes stay atomic, and a corrupt ledger is discarded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given br and bv invocations from both the engine and an interactive session when the telemetry ledger is read then it reports the subcommand the flags the call-site class and the duration per invocation in a committed append-only file, and a corrupt or missing ledger never fails the invoking command

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given br and bv invocations from both the engine and an interactive session when the telemetry ledger is read then it reports the subcommand the flags the call-site class and the duration per invocation in a committed append-only file, and a corrupt or missing ledger never fails the invoking command

title: Record the scheduler score and rank behind each dispatch
description:
## Context

D9 requires dispatch inputs to be reproducible and recorded, and dispatch order is one of them. loop_state.ready_ranked passes br scheduler's rank through untouched as the primary ordering key, and nothing records it - so a pass's ordering cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

Research 2026-07-25 corrected an earlier characterisation: the ranking is not opaque. br scheduler emits schema br.scheduler.v1 with a per-item score, a fallback_rank, and an explicit fallback policy of priority ASC then created_at ASC then id ASC, noting that tied or incomplete evidence preserves the fallback rank. It is versioned and explainable, so the cheap fix is to record it rather than to replace it.

Record the score, the rank and the policy schema version into the dispatch marker (basicly-kjc5.28). Note for when we own the tracker: our own ranking must drop created_at, because age-based ordering makes dispatch order clock-dependent for an unchanged graph, which D9 forbids for anything outliving the pass - ordering becomes unblocked-only, then priority, then descending dependent count, then id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a supervisor pass that ranks the ready set when a lane is dispatched then its run marker records the scheduler score and rank and the fallback policy version so the pass ordering is reconstructible from the tracker alone

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
acceptance_criteria: Given a supervisor pass that ranks the ready set when a lane is dispatched then its run marker records the scheduler score and rank and the fallback policy version so the pass ordering is reconstructible from the tracker alone

title: Design the cross-repo work exchange as an append-only offer log
description:
## Context

Settled by the owner 2026-07-25. Several repos are worked at once and work is routinely discovered in the wrong repo - a basicly bug surfaces while working in terminal. The resolution is Kanban pull semantics: announce, never push.

Each repo's ledger has exactly one writer, that repo. The development workspace hosts an exchange - an append-only log of offers rather than assignments. A repo that finds foreign work announces an event naming the target repo; it does not create a bead there. Design work brainstormed in development is decomposed in development and its children announced the same way, so the exchange is the single place work becomes available. Consumers poll at their own cadence, pull by creating a bead in their own tracker recording the offer id as provenance, and append the claim back to the exchange rather than to another tracker.

Event kinds are append-only and total - announced, claimed, declined, superseded - so an offer's state is a fold over its events and history is the audit trail. The design consequence worth preserving: an announcement carries no authority, which is the engine-disposes agents-propose stance applied across repo boundaries, and it is what keeps concurrency trivial since no component ever writes across a repo boundary.

This bead covers the design and the schema in docs/work-tracker.md section 8 plus the exchange format; the commands that announce, poll and pull follow once the format is settled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a repo that discovers work belonging to another repo when it announces an offer in the development exchange then no write reaches the target repo's tracker, and given the target repo polls and pulls the offer then it creates its own bead recording the offer id and appends a claimed event to the exchange so a double pull is detectable

## Scope

- `docs/work-tracker.md`
acceptance_criteria: Given a repo that discovers work belonging to another repo when it announces an offer in the development exchange then no write reaches the target repo's tracker, and given the target repo polls and pulls the offer then it creates its own bead recording the offer id and appends a claimed event to the exchange so a double pull is detectable

title: Stop the tracker export from committing machine-specific absolute paths
description:
## Context

Found during the work-tracker review 2026-07-25. The committed .beads/issues.jsonl carries source_repo_path on 328 of its 332 records, and the values expose two different users' home directories - /home/<user-a>/development/basicly and /home/<user-b>/Development/basicly - plus a transient worktree path under .claude/worktrees. The file is committed and this repo is distributed to consumers, so the leak is published.

This violates the repo's own hard constraint that no machine or user specific absolute path, username or hostname may ever be committed. It is also a portability defect in its own right: a path that means something on one machine is noise or a wrong answer on another, and a consumer's clone inherits our directory layout as data.

The field is written by br rather than by the harness, so the fix is either to strip it on export, to configure br not to emit it if that is possible, or to add a gate that catches an absolute path in the tracker export the way secret-scan catches a credential. Whichever route, the requirement for our own tracker is recorded in docs/work-tracker.md: a record is path-free, and provenance is the repo identity rather than a filesystem location.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `grep -c "/home/" .beads/issues.jsonl` in a clean checkout.
2. It reports hundreds of matches.
3. Inspect one record with `head -1 .beads/issues.jsonl | jq .source_repo_path` and observe an absolute path containing a username.

Expected: no absolute path or username appears anywhere in the committed export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the committed tracker export when it is scanned then no record carries a machine-specific absolute path or username, and the harness either strips the field on write or fails the secret-scan style gate that catches it

## Scope

- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/`
acceptance_criteria: Given the committed tracker export when it is scanned then no record carries a machine-specific absolute path or username, and the harness either strips the field on write or fails the secret-scan style gate that catches it

comments.author: niksa
comments.text:
[harness-info] Two requirements confirmed by shipping basicly-vkh0.5, 2026-07-26.

1. A record must be path-free. br stamps source_repo_path with the absolute canonical path of the producing workspace, and there is no config knob to suppress it (br config list carries nothing for it). Our replacement records provenance as the repo identity, never a filesystem location. Regression test: tests/test_tracker_path_scan.py.

2. Text already recorded must have a redaction path. This is the new one and it is worse than the field. br comments offers only add and list - no edit, no delete - so a machine path (or anything else) recorded in a comment cannot be removed through the documented CLI at all. Two usernames on closed beads were only fixable by redacting at export time, which means the committed artifact deliberately diverges from the local database. Our replacement needs a first-class redaction event: append-only history is right, but an append-only log with no redaction event cannot honour a deletion requirement.

Both are already enforced for the current tracker by the tracker-path-scan pre-commit gate plus br.scrub_export, so the replacement inherits a committed proof rather than a description.

title: Stop a worktree teardown from discarding the tracker usage it recorded
description:
## Context

Found immediately after basicly-vkh0.2 landed, by checking a claim that bead's own report
made: the surface report lists `where` as never used, yet `worktree._probe_redirect` calls
`br where --json` on every single worktree provisioning. Three provisionings later the
committed ledger still had zero `where` records.

The cause is that the usage spool does not follow `.beads/redirect` the way every other
tracker path does. `br.run_br` records with the `repo_root` it was handed, which for a lane
is the worktree; `tracker_usage.is_enabled` then sees the worktree's own checked-out
`.basicly/ledger/` directory and returns True, so the record is spooled to
`<worktree>/.basicly/usage/tracker-usage.jsonl`. The loop deletes the worktree at teardown,
taking the spool with it.

So every engine tracker call made from a worktree is silently discarded. That is not a
uniform sampling loss - it is exactly the traffic the harness generates while doing lane
work, and it makes one surface (`where`) read as never-used when the engine depends on it.

This matters because the ledger is the input to the Phase 6 surface freeze. A false
never-used entry is the worst error that artifact can contain: it would omit a surface the
engine calls on every provisioning.

`br.beads_dir` is the precedent to copy - it follows the redirect file to the base
checkout's `.beads`, whose parent is the base checkout.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Provision a loop worktree, which runs `br where --json` against the worktree path.
2. Run `basicly usage tracker --promote` in the base checkout.
3. Observed: no `where` record, and the report names `where` among the never-used surfaces.
   Expected: `where` recorded as an engine surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an engine tracker call made with a linked worktree as its repo root when the record is spooled then it lands in the base checkout's spool so teardown cannot discard it and the surface report counts it
acceptance_criteria: Given an engine tracker call made with a linked worktree as its repo root when the record is spooled then it lands in the base checkout's spool so teardown cannot discard it and the surface report counts it

title: Absorb the measured journal mechanisms into the work-tracker design
description:
## Context

From the hankweave analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/hankweave.md`), the only append-only journal
in the reviewed set running in production, measured against its own committed 6,467-event fixture.
Two mechanisms it has and `docs/design/work-tracker.md` does not, plus one measurement that turns a
section 9.5 assertion into evidence.

**1. The denormalized running aggregate.** Every event carries the totals that hold *after* it
(`state.transition.data.resultingState`, `event-schemas.ts:429-434`), so the overwhelmingly common
query - what is the current cost or count - is answered by reading the tail rather than folding the
whole log, while the fold stays available as the checkable authority. Section 4 of our design admits
the cost it does not solve ("a fold is O(events) and a naive reader re-folds per query") and section
10 defers the index by measurement. This is the mechanism that makes deferring the index defensible
rather than a hand-wave, and it costs one field.

**2. Honest truncation.** A large payload is stored truncated with `truncated: true` plus
`originalLength` (`event-schemas.ts:259-268`). Section 9.1 declines lossy compaction on the grounds
that it discards evidence git already packs - which stands - but that leaves growth bounded by
nothing. Truncation with a recorded original length bounds it while *saying* that evidence was
dropped and how much, which is a different and better thing than summarising it away.

**3. Evidence for section 9.5, not a change to it.** Their journal has **no sequence numbers** and
mints ids as `Date.now()` plus `Math.random()` (`utils.ts:26-28`). The analysis measured **44.5% of
events in their production fixture sharing a millisecond**, so total order exists only as an
unrecorded side effect of file append order. Our rule that a timestamp is evidence and nothing
branches on it was asserted; it can now cite a number.

Also record the rejection and why: their sentinels are injected LLM calls with a per-million-token
cost model (`sentinels/sentinel.ts:108`, `:502`), so their monitoring is a paid external API -
inadmissible under `basicly-ctdz`, and `StallWatchdog` already covers the condition that matters.

Net finding worth stating plainly in the design: our unbuilt design is more rigorous than their
shipped one, so this is an absorption of three narrow mechanisms, not a redesign.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the work-tracker design when it is read after this change then the event schema carries a running aggregate with the tail-read query and the fold-as-authority both stated, truncation records originalLength as the growth bound, section 9.5 cites the measured millisecond-collision rate, and the rejected sentinel approach is recorded with its reason
acceptance_criteria: Given the work-tracker design when it is read after this change then the event schema carries a running aggregate with the tail-read query and the fold-as-authority both stated truncation records originalLength as the growth bound section 9.5 cites the measured millisecond-collision rate and the rejected sentinel approach is recorded with its reason

comments.author: niksa
comments.text: [harness-policy] NARROWED 2026-07-30 on a licence finding (references.md 2.3, basicly-imnu.12). hankweave-runtime is stock Apache-2.0 but its NOTICE.md incorporates Southbridge's Terms of Service, whose key provisions include 'Competition restrictions on using Hanks to build competing products' and 'Managed services restrictions require prior written consent'. basicly is a coding-agent harness and hankweave an agent-orchestration runtime, so the restriction plausibly reaches us, and whether a NOTICE can add terms to Apache-2.0 at all is a legal question we are not qualified to answer. WHAT STAYS IN SCOPE: the measurements, because they are properties of published data rather than derived from code - specifically that 44.5 percent of events in their own committed 6467-event fixture share a millisecond while the journal has no sequence numbers, which turns work-tracker 9.5 from an assertion into evidence, and is the single most valuable thing this bead carries. WHAT IS HELD: adopting the running-aggregate and honest-truncation mechanisms with their source as the reference. Those are good ideas and may well be reachable as ideas, but do not implement from their files pending review by someone qualified. If the mechanisms are built, build them from a written description and record the clean-room posture, exactly as 2.1 requires for beads_rust.

If their mechanisms are ever wanted, obtain them clean-room from a written description - but the owner's reading, which matches the analysis, is that we already have what we wanted. The measurements are the value and they are already recorded here and in the review: 44.5 percent of events in their own committed 6467-event fixture share a millisecond while the journal carries no sequence numbers, which turns work-tracker 9.5 from an assertion into evidence. Treat hankweave source as permanently off-limits as an implementation reference. This bead's remaining scope is therefore the two mechanisms as CONCEPTS - a running aggregate carried on each event so the tail answers the common query while the fold stays the authority, and truncation that records originalLength rather than summarising - to be designed from first principles here, plus folding the measurement into 9.5.
